Discount the China EW 7.6 Sharpe (microcap/limits-to-arbitrage, T+1). (2) Sample fragility: acceptable — multi-regime OOS, but the relevant prior for a 50-name liquid universe is the VW 0.4-0.7 row, not EW. (3) Costs: the cost-neutrality argument is structurally sound (top-7/top-15 caps fix trade count); residual risk is adverse selection/wider spreads on range-bottom entries, mitigated by existing vetoes. (4) PIT: cleanest class; minor caveats on IEX volume share drift and prior-completed-daily-bar discipline. (5) Horizon: the binding flaw — reversal premia accrue overnight (Lou-Polk-Skouras, JFE 2019), the book is flat 15:50-9:45, so all transferred performance numbers are struck; features survive only as gate-arbitrated hypotheses. (6) Redundancy: larger than claimed (repo-confirmed: STOCHk_14_3_3 = pos_in_range(14), BBP/BBB/Price_SMA20_Ratio/Volume_Ratio span much of the L=20 block; the Table 13 orthogonality stat belongs to the CNN, not the distillate) — but the daily-window range-position term structure and lag-OHLC geometry are genuinely absent from the stack. (7) Jetson: honest; rolling ops trivial (numba kernels already exist in indicators.py); only LSTM input-width growth needs gating. Why not survives=false: the proposal is unusually self-aware (pre-applied MP haircut, admitted Stoch overlap, hedged effect size conditional on the DSR gate), costs ~nothing to test, uses the cleanest possible data class, and its core evidence (JF 2023 + JFE 2024 corroboration) has no failed replications — killing it outright would require treating horizon transfer as categorically fatal for a feature (vs a strategy) import, which the in-house triple-barrier labels + purged WFCV + DSR machinery exists precisely to adjudicate. Effective non-redundant validation sample is ~2 windows for ~6 fitted parameters (two z thresholds, three multipliers, floor condition): STLFSI2 — already gated at >1.0 -> 0.5x in macro_indicators.py — CONTAINS the ICE BofA HY spread as a component, and SPY 200d trend + VIX ladder + GARCH/EWMA vol sizing already de-risk 2008, 2011, Aug-2015, Jan-Feb-2016, Dec-2018, 2020, and most of 2022. Internal design contradiction: a 21d-change z-score vs trailing 1y mean-reverts during sustained constant-rate widening (the trailing window absorbs the new vol), so the build UNDER-detects the 2015-16-style slow-grind regimes claimed as the core payload while OVER-detecting fast co-moves where credit coincides with or lags equity — the mechanism argument calls for slow level-anchored measures, but the build ships fast change measures.

The macro premise survives at its native horizon: aggregate credit conditions as a SLOW state variable (quarterly+) remain a live, Fed-maintained indicator (EBP), and worst-credit-state dependence of high-beta returns is real — it is the daily change-z divergence instrumentation that fails, not the state-variable idea.

A reduced salvage version is a defensible near-zero-cost experiment: de-risk-only (delete the VIX-override floor branch entirely), level-anchored slow measure (e.g., 63-126d level z or distance-from-1y-tights on the hedged ratio), weekly cadence as one more graded advisory input in the STLFSI2<1.0 zone, shadow-mode only with no headline drawdown claims; blocking the overnight sleeve on credit stress is the single most defensible piece (cheap, conservative, asymmetric).

EVIDENCE LEG UNVERIFIED POST-2016: the market-timing version is conceded dead (Tse 2015: 1-7 of 48 industries, weaker after CRSP revisions, some sign reversals - sign instability is poison for a pooled ranker). The proposer's decay triage is accurate and unusually honest: market-timing version dead, cross-sectional network version alive as of 2016, and the refusal to clone big->small lead-lag into a mega-cap universe is correct.

A much smaller, different claim might be defensible: a weeks-horizon sector-diffusion signal as a DAILY overlay on decisions the system actually makes at that cadence (overnight-sleeve keeper selection, bucket-cap modulation) - but that is not what was proposed, and it would still face the 2021+ validation-window problem.

REPLICATION STATUS: no failed replication found. Bogousslavsky (JFE 2021) confirms the decomposition through ~2019 with the end-of-day anomaly weakness STRENGTHENING in the second half of sample; Hendershott-Livdan-Roesch night/day beta replicates internationally and is extended by 2024-2026 follow-ups (nuance: negative daytime beta relation reverses after large uncertainty shocks); Akbas-Boehmer-Jiang-Koch (2022) prices tug-of-war intensity; a 2025 FRL paper validates the overnight anomaly in US index ETFs 1993-2024 and large caps through 2024. findings.name: Conformal abstention layer: CQR-calibrated intervals around the LSTM+LGB ensemble with ACI online coverage control (discrete tail-veto, NOT inverse-width sizing)
findings.mechanism: Split/cross-conformal calibration converts the existing uncalibrated lgb_q10 (plus a new q90 head) into prediction intervals with finite-sample marginal coverage, no distributional assumptions (CQR adapts to heteroscedasticity). Under regime shift, Gibbs-Candes ACI's one-parameter feedback alpha_{t+1}=alpha_t+gamma(alpha-err_t) provably restores long-run coverage. Economically: interval width is a per-symbol, per-state uncertainty estimate; abstaining on the widest cross-sectional tail removes trades whose ~bps expected edge is swamped by noise — and abstention is COST-NEGATIVE (saves the 11bps RT + spread on skipped marginal trades). Critical design result from the 2026 ranking literature: in cross-sectional rankers, uncertainty structurally couples to signal strength (median Spearman rho(uncertainty,|score|)=0.616), so continuous inverse-width sizing systematically de-levers the best signals and FAILS; the correct actions are (i) a discrete tail cap/veto (e.g., P85 width) and (ii) a strategy-level trust gate on the model's own trailing realized efficacy — market-stress proxies are poor substitutes (VIX-percentile gate AUROC 0.449, worse than random, at predicting model failure).

Gibbs & Candes (2021, NeurIPS) 'Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift' — long-run coverage guarantee under arbitrary shift via one online parameter

Zaffran, Feron, Goude, Josse & Dieuleveut (2022, ICML) 'Adaptive Conformal Predictions for Time Series' — AgACI (expert aggregation over learning rates) achieves near-nominal coverage on volatile series without tuning

Fantazzini (2024, Journal of Risk and Financial Management) 'Adaptive Conformal Inference for Computing Market Risk Measures' — on 4,000 crypto-assets, ACI variants (FACI, SF-OGD) deliver precise VaR across quantiles while GARCH and daily-range models suffer numerical convergence failures and structural-break breakdowns

Sanderink (2026, arXiv:2603.13252) 'When Alpha Breaks: Two-Level Uncertainty for Safe Deployment of Cross-Sectional Stock Rankers' — LightGBM ranker, ~100-name universe, 109 walk-forward folds 2016-2025: trust-gate AUROC 0.72 (0.75 in broken regime), 80% precision at 47% abstention; Gate+Vol+P85-tail-cap lifts regime-broken FINAL Sharpe to 0.925 vs 0.375; documents the inverse-uncertainty-sizing failure mode

findings.effect_size_net: Channel is selective trading, so net effect is cost-POSITIVE by construction: vetoing the widest ~10-15% of candidate entries removes the trades with worst signal-to-noise plus their full ~11bps+spread round-trip cost. Literature magnitudes: 2.5x deployment Sharpe in regime-broken periods (0.925 vs 0.375, Sanderink FINAL), drawdown containment (Kato), valid VaR where GARCH breaks (Fantazzini). Realistic expectation at this app's scale/horizon: a few percent fewer trades concentrated in chop/regime breaks, modest all-period Sharpe lift, large tail improvement in exactly the periods the DSR holdout penalizes — verifiable through the existing shadow/DM-HLN harness.
findings.decay_evidence: Not a return anomaly — a distribution-free validity guarantee, so no McLean-Pontiff style post-publication decay applies; the failure mode is efficiency (intervals too wide to be informative), never validity. Finance-specific applications 2022-2026 are an expanding literature (Fantazzini 2024; Kato 2024; Sanderink 2026; TCP arXiv:2507.05470) rather than a decaying one. The 2026 benchmark (Sabashvili) is the relevant 'replication': simple rolling split-conformal + ACI controllers hold coverage where fancier EnbPI/SPCI undercover — which pins down the variant to build.
findings.free_data_source: Zero external data. Calibration scores = out-of-fold residuals already produced by the purged walk-forward CV in scripts/hypersearch_v2.py (val-fold predictions vs triple-barrier labels); live coverage errors = matured forward-return labels that shadow.py:_realized() already reconstructs from Alpaca bars. Publication lag: none. Point-in-time subtlety that MUST be modeled: the ACI error at time t is only observable after the fb-hour label window closes, so update alpha_t using the coverage of the prediction made at t-fb (lagged-feedback ACI; coverage guarantee unaffected).
findings.build_sketch: New conformal.py (~150 lines, numpy only). Train-time (run_pipeline retrain, weekly): train one extra LGB quantile booster lgb_q90 alongside the existing lgb_q10 in hypersearch_v2.py (minutes on CPU); pool val-fold nonconformity scores E_i=max(q10_i - y_i, y_i - q90_i) across the 3 purged folds; store the (1-alpha) quantile c_hat in the model manifest. Live (stock_loop, hourly): interval = [q10 - c_hat_t, q90 + c_hat_t]; maintain alpha_t via ACI (gamma~0.01) on fb-lagged coverage errors pooled across the panel; entry rule: among top-7 candidates, veto symbols whose interval width is in the top ~15% of the cross-sectional width distribution (discrete tail cap per Sanderink — do NOT divide size by width); optionally de-rate size one notch for the next widest decile. Log realized coverage as drift telemetry (feeds the wave-2 drift-monitor roadmap item). findings.name: HAR-RV volatility forecasting on realized range from own hourly OHLC bars — replace/challenge the EGARCH sizing layer
findings.mechanism: GARCH infers latent variance from close-to-close returns by MLE; realized measures OBSERVE it from intraday data, reducing forecasting to a 3-regressor OLS projection. Hansen-Lunde showed nothing beats GARCH(1,1) using daily returns alone — the gains come from intraday data, not model complexity. Corsi's HAR (daily/weekly/monthly RV components) approximates volatility long memory (slow hyperbolic ACF decay) that GARCH's geometric decay cannot, matching the heterogeneous-horizon volatility cascade of market participants. Key adaptation for this app: with only ~7 RTH hourly bars/day, plain sum-of-squared-returns RV is noisy, but the realized RANGE (per-bar Parkinson ln(H/L)^2/(4ln2), summed within the day) is ~5x more efficient than close-to-close RV at the same sampling frequency (Christensen-Podolskij), i.e., hourly-OHLC realized range carries roughly the information of ~35 close-to-close observations per day. Bonus: kills a documented reliability/compute hot spot — volatility.py's arch-MLE EGARCH fit fails to converge on short/volatile series (its own fallback logic plus Fantazzini's crypto evidence), while HAR is closed-form OLS.
key_papers: Corsi (2009, Journal of Financial Econometrics 7(2):174-196) 'A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility' — HAR-RV outperforms GARCH-type and short-memory RV models out-of-sample
Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold & Labys (2003, Econometrica 71(2):579-625) — simple linear models of realized volatility dominate daily-return GARCH for forecasting

Hansen & Lunde (2005, Journal of Applied Econometrics 20:873-889) 'Does anything beat a GARCH(1,1)?' — among 330 ARCH-type models on daily data nothing beats GARCH(1,1); the frontier moves only with intraday data

Pollok (2025, arXiv:2506.07928, USC) 'Predicting Realized Variance Out of Sample: Can Anything Beat The Benchmark?' — all S&P 500 firms 1/1993-6/2019: 3-regressor HAR beats ~6,000-regressor LASSO/PCA ML on RMSE/MAE/QLIKE in nearly every panel (average-firm QLIKE: HAR 0.2591 vs LASSO 0.3448 vs rolling-SD^2 0.6449); 'hard to unambiguously and unanimously beat the HAR benchmark'

Bollerslev, Patton & Quaedvlieg (2016, Journal of Econometrics 192(1):1-18) 'Exploiting the errors' — HARQ (realized-quarticity-adjusted coefficients) adds further gains, mainly in QLIKE; optional phase-2 upgrade

Christensen & Podolskij (2007, Journal of Econometrics 141:323-349) and Martens & van Dijk (2007, Journal of Econometrics 138:181-207) — realized range-based variance ~5x efficiency of realized variance at equal sampling; empirically superior under sparse sampling
findings.effect_size_net: Not an alpha signal — a measurement upgrade to the sizing/stop stack, so zero added turnover and zero data cost. Magnitudes: HAR-class forecasts cut QLIKE by ~60% vs rolling-SD benchmarks (Pollok panel) and consistently beat daily-data GARCH in the RV literature; for this app that means tighter risk-targeted position sizes and ATR-stop scaling that adapts ~1-3 days faster after vol shocks (HAR loads ~0.4-0.5 on yesterday's RV vs GARCH's slow MLE-smoothed response), fewer oversized positions entering high-vol regimes. Side benefit on Jetson: replaces per-symbol arch MLE refits (~0.1-1s each, convergence failures handled by fallback code) with microsecond OLS — strictly net-positive at any scale.
findings.decay_evidence: Continuously replicated 2009-2026 with no decay: HAR remains the standard benchmark that large-scale studies fail to beat (Pollok 2025 panel across ~500 firms x 26 years; HARQ 2016 improves it only modestly; 2024-2025 deep-learning RV papers report single-digit-% QLIKE gains over HAR at large compute cost). Because it forecasts a statistical quantity (variance) rather than excess returns, there is no arbitrage-decay channel (McLean-Pontiff inapplicable).
findings.free_data_source: Own Alpaca hourly OHLCV bars already harvested (scripts/harvest_stock_data.py) — RTH bars 9:30-16:00 give ~7 bars/day; daily realized range RRV_d = sum_i ln(H_i/L_i)^2/(4 ln 2) per symbol. Publication lag: zero; revision: none; point-in-time by construction (computable at each day's close from bars already on disk). Crypto: 24h bars give 24 obs/day — even better.
findings.build_sketch: Extend volatility.py (~80 lines, numpy/numba, no new deps): (1) daily RRV series per symbol from cached hourly bars; (2) rolling ~250-day OLS in logs: log RRV_{d+1} ~ const + log RRV_d + log mean(RRV,5d) + log mean(RRV,22d), refit DAILY at the overlay cadence (closed-form normal equations, microseconds/symbol); (3) forecast sigma_{d+1}, scale to hourly via /sqrt(6.5) for get_garch_stop()-style stop multipliers and the risk-based sizing layer; (4) BPQ 'insanity filter': clamp forecasts to the estimation-window min/max; (5) keep EGARCH as fallback for symbols with <60d history and run HAR-vs-EGARCH as a challenger comparison on rolling QLIKE through the existing shadow/DM-HLN harness before cutover. Jetson cost: <1MB RAM, sub-millisecond per symbol per day — strictly cheaper than the current arch MLE path.

findings.name: Online ensemble weighting over the LSTM/LGB heads: low-learning-rate exponential weights (Hedge/BOA) shrunk toward the 0.6/0.4 prior, replacing the fixed blend
findings.mechanism: The fixed lstm_weight=0.6 in model_lgb.py:ensemble_predict() encodes a one-time guess. Exponential-weights aggregation (Hedge/EWA) carries a distribution-free regret guarantee: cumulative loss <= best single head + sqrt(T ln N / 2) regardless of the data process — i.e., if either head degrades for months (the exact regime-failure mode the DM-HLN challenger machinery exists for), the blend automatically tracks the surviving head, with bounded worst case. The forecast combination puzzle is the essential counterweight: 50 years of evidence that AGGRESSIVELY estimated combination weights lose to simple averages because weight-estimation error exceeds the gain when experts are few, correlated, and samples short (exactly 2 correlated heads here). The literature's resolution — and the design this implies — is partial shrinkage toward a fixed prior with a slow learning rate (Diebold-Shin 'partially egalitarian' principle; BOA's second-order adaptive rates), updated at overlay cadence on a long loss window, gated like any challenger.
key_papers: Timmermann (2006, Handbook of Economic Forecasting, ch.4 'Forecast Combinations') — canonical survey: equal/fixed weights are a strong default; gains from learned weights require persistent performance differences
Stock & Watson (2004, Journal of Forecasting 23:405-430) — names the 'forecast combination puzzle' from G7 output-growth forecasting
Smith & Wallis (2009, Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics 71(3):331-355) — finite-sample explanation: weight-estimation noise dominates unless optimal weights are far from equal

Claeskens, Magnus, Vasnev & Wang (2016, International Journal of Forecasting 32(3):754-762) — treating estimated weights as random shows combined forecast is biased with inflated variance — formal warning against aggressive weight learning

Cesa-Bianchi & Lugosi (2006, 'Prediction, Learning, and Games', Cambridge UP) — Hedge/EWA regret bound sqrt(T ln N/2); Wintenberger (2017, Machine Learning 106:119-141) BOA — second-order bounds, adaptive learning rates, no tuning

Remlinger, Briere, Alasseur & Mikael (2021, arXiv:2111.15365 'Expert Aggregation for Financial Forecasting') — BOA over ML return-forecast experts for long-short equity strategies: beats individual algorithms with higher Sharpe, lower expected shortfall, SIMILAR turnover, robust under non-stationarity
Diebold & Shin (2019, International Journal of Forecasting 35(4):1679-1691) — partially-egalitarian LASSO: shrinking weights TOWARD equality beats both equal and fully-estimated weights
Wang, Hyndman, Li & Kang (2023, IJF 'Forecast combinations: an over 50-year review') — adaptive weights pay off only with online loss tracking and expert diversity
findings.effect_size_net: Honest read: small expected mean improvement, but asymmetric payoff — the regret bound caps the downside at ~basis points of loss vs the better head, while the upside (auto-de-weighting a structurally broken head months before a scheduled retrain/promotion would catch it) is material drawdown avoidance. Remlinger et al. report higher Sharpe and lower shortfall at SIMILAR turnover, i.e., no incremental transaction cost; here the weight only modulates an already-computed blend, so net cost is exactly zero new data, zero new trades, microseconds of compute. The realistic prize at this scale is robustness (regime insurance on the blend), not headline alpha.
findings.decay_evidence: The combination puzzle IS the replication record: from Clemen (1989) through Wang et al. (2023), naive learned weights repeatedly fail to beat simple averages out-of-sample, while slow/shrunk adaptive schemes match or beat them — a remarkably stable result, not a decaying anomaly. Online-aggregation theory (regret bounds) is assumption-free and does not decay. Finance-specific empirical evidence (Remlinger et al.) is positive but limited — hence the shrinkage-anchored, shadow-gated design rather than free-running weights.
findings.free_data_source: Own per-head predictions and matured labels only: predict_now.py already computes lstm_pred and lgb_pred separately (lines 314-333) before collapsing them; shadow.py already implements prediction logging (shadow_preds.jsonl) and fb-window label maturation (_realized()). Publication lag: zero; point-in-time: weights at hour t must use only labels matured by t (fb-hour lag), which the existing shadow machinery already enforces.
findings.build_sketch: ~60 lines. (1) Persist lstm_pred/lgb_pred per symbol-hour into the existing snapshot/journal path; (2) daily overlay job: over a rolling >=30-trading-day window of matured labels, compute per-head squared (or pinball) loss; EWA weights w_i ∝ exp(-eta * cumloss_i) with eta = sqrt(8 ln 2 / T_window); shrink w* = 0.5*w_EWA + 0.5*(0.6,0.4); clamp to [0.3,0.8] to bound estimation noise (Claeskens et al.); (3) pass w* as the lstm_weight argument that ensemble_predict() in model_lgb.py:137-144 ALREADY accepts — no signature change; (4) run as challenger vs fixed 0.6/0.4 through shadow.py DM-HLN before promotion. Jetson cost: numpy over a few thousand rows once a day — milliseconds, zero RAM impact.

findings.name: Fractionally differentiated (FFD) log-price feature for the LGB head — cheap numba test, evidence-limited, gate behind existing CV/DSR
findings.mechanism: Plain returns (d=1) erase the long-memory level information that tree models could exploit; raw prices (d=0) are non-stationary so the learner fits regime-specific levels that do not transfer. FFD applies the binomial-expansion filter (1-B)^d at the minimal d where ADF rejects a unit root (typically d≈0.3-0.5 for equity log prices), producing a series that is stationary for training purposes yet retains correlation >0.9 with the original level series — a slow 'trend-state' feature qualitatively different from the bounded oscillators (RSI/MACD/Stoch) and short-window returns already in the feature set. Lopez de Prado's claim is that this resolves the stationarity-vs-memory dilemma; the honest caveat is that independent, ablation-style evidence remains thin.
key_papers: Lopez de Prado (2018, 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning', Wiley, ch.5) — origin: most liquid futures/equity series achieve ADF stationarity at d<0.6 while preserving memory; proposes the fixed-width-window FFD estimator used here

Walasek & Gajda (2021, International Journal of Advances in Engineering Sciences and Applied Mathematics 13:183-200; Univ. of Warsaw WP 2020-32) — the strongest INDEPENDENT evaluation found: WIG20, S&P 500, DAX, Nikkei 225 with neural networks — fractionally differentiated inputs produced more accurate out-of-sample forecasts than integer differencing
Raubitzek et al. (2023, Entropy 25(1):35) 'Combining Fractional Derivatives and Machine Learning: A Review' — survey confirming applications are growing but rigorous head-to-head ablations are scarce
Applications without clean ablations: Chinese futures ML trading system (arXiv:2303.04581) uses FFD price transforms with triple-barrier labels — adoption evidence, not effect-size evidence
findings.effect_size_net: Unproven at this horizon — that is the finding. One positive independent study (ANNs, daily indexes), book-ecosystem advocacy otherwise, and no published hourly-equity ablation. Expected value comes from option value at near-zero cost: zero data cost, zero turnover impact (feature only), and the existing purged-CV + DSR holdout + PBO machinery is precisely the right kill-gate. Worst case: LGB feature importance ~0 and it is dropped at the next hypersearch; best case: a low-correlation trend-state feature the current set lacks.
findings.decay_evidence: Too thin to have a decay literature — which is itself the assessment: 8 years post-AFML, no flagship journal replication establishes robust forecast gains, while the one careful independent test (Walasek-Gajda 2021) is positive on 4 indexes with ANNs. Treat as a hypothesis to test, not an edge to trust. Known practitioner pitfall to avoid: choosing d on the FULL sample's ADF test is lookahead — d must be selected per training fold only.
findings.free_data_source: Own Alpaca hourly bars (log close; optionally log dollar volume). Publication lag: zero; revisions: none. Point-in-time: fixed-width FFD window uses only past bars; select d on train folds only (per-fold ADF scan over d in {0.1,...,0.7}, pick smallest d with p<0.05) and freeze it in the model manifest for live use.
findings.build_sketch: Numba kernel in indicators.py (~40 lines): weights w_0=1, w_k = -w_{k-1}(d-k+1)/k, truncated at |w_k|<1e-4 (window ~100-250 hourly bars at d≈0.4); FFD_t = dot(w, logclose[t-W:t]). One-time panel transform: 96 symbols x ~10k bars x W≈100 ≈ 10^8 multiply-adds — a few seconds in numba on the Jetson, ~zero incremental RAM; live update is O(W) per symbol-hour. Add 1-2 columns (FFD log close, FFD log dollar-volume) to the LGB feature matrix in hypersearch_v2.py; evaluate through the existing purged walk-forward + DSR holdout; retain only on gated lift, otherwise delete. Do NOT feed to the LSTM (sequence scaler already handles returns; FFD's value proposition is tree splits on a stationary level).

fatal_flaws: Evidence base: single-author, unreplicated v1 working paper (SSRN May 2024 / arXiv Apr 2025), no journal placement, zero third-party replications or citations found as of June 2026; per-model L/S six-factor alpha t-stats 2.34-2.77 (only the 4-model combo reaches 3.80) fail Harvey-Liu-Zhu t>3 given 4 ML algorithms + OLS + 2 signal pools searched with Optuna tuning; median OOS R^2 is NEGATIVE for every algorithm; predecessor family (Nguyen 2012 Geographic Momentum) never achieved publication in 14 years.

Tail-only, non-monotonic effect cannot map to the book: alphas concentrate in the extreme top/bottom 5% of ~500 names and decile alphas are non-monotonic — LASSO (the best model) shows NO significant top-decile or decile-spread alpha. A top-7-of-50 selection cuts at the 14th percentile, exactly the region where the paper itself finds nothing.

Sample 2012Q1-2022Q1 with in-paper decay aimed at the proposal's own basket: efficiency gains are concentrated in emerging-market signals (Bai-Philippon-Savov channel) and high-attention episodes, yet 6 of the 10 proposed ETFs are EM/Asia; 4+ years of unobserved post-sample decay plus McLean-Pontiff post-publication decay stack on top.

Signal-object mismatch: the paper uses LOCAL-CURRENCY Datastream local-index returns across all 47 ACWI markets explicitly to remove FX, and finds valuable signals are NOT concentrated in the largest markets (Qatar frequently top-5). The proposal substitutes USD, US-session-priced ETFs of the 10 LARGEST markets — reintroducing FX noise, embedding a lagged-SPY common component from US-hours trading, and discarding the long tail of markets where the paper locates the signal.

Architecture transplant is structurally invalid (verified in repo): training pools all tickers via np.vstack (scripts/hypersearch_v2.py) with no symbol-ID/sector/exposure features (model_lgb.py, indicators.py, panel_ranks.py). Broadcast weekly ETF returns are cross-sectionally CONSTANT date-context features — the CS_Dispersion/CS_Breadth/VIX/HMM class the system already saturates — and cannot express the paper's mechanism of stock-specific, SIGN-HETEROGENEOUS loadings (Lockheed up vs McDonald's down on the same Russia shock) learned by 100k+ per-stock-quarter models; pooling averages sign-heterogeneous effects toward zero. The claim's premise that the paper's per-stock setup 'matches our pooled architecture exactly' is false.

Long-only + intraday-flat economics: long-leg six-factor alpha is 3.2-3.7bp/day gross at 33-64% DAILY turnover; at ~11bp+spread retail RT the paper's own long-leg net alpha is ~0 (LASSO) to negative (GB) — the quoted '8.35bp/day net' subtracts institutional costs (6.24bp) from RAW returns still containing market/size/value beta a high-beta long book already owns. Multi-week diffusion drift also accrues largely overnight/close-to-close, which a 15:50-flatten book with a small sleeve structurally cannot hold.

The proposed kill-switch underprices testing cost: 20 mutually correlated weekly-constant features have only ~150-500 distinct historical values; LightGBM assigns nonzero SHAP to such noise (the 'kill if it never loads' criterion cannot trigger), so the real gate is a consumed DSR/challenger slot — eroding the multiple-testing budget the gauntlet exists to protect.
surviving_caveats: The data plumbing itself is sound: US-listed country-ETF closes are point-in-time by construction (no publication lag, no revisions, no foreign-timestamp alignment) and Jetson cost is negligible — the engineering pattern is reusable for a better-specified variant.

A redesigned, economically honest variant is not refuted and could be queued separately: symbol-VARYING exposure interactions — lagged country-ETF weekly return x per-name rolling 252d beta/correlation to that ETF, or EDGAR 10-K geographic-segment revenue weights (free, point-in-time by filing date) building a Nguyen-style per-name geographic return. That gives the pooled LightGBM features it can actually use; route as an exploratory challenger with a pre-registered kill criterion and expect any drift to be mostly overnight (sleeve-relevant only).
If Jiao (2025) achieves peer-reviewed publication or independent replication with post-2022 out-of-sample evidence, the evidence axis should be re-scored.

A weekly-cadence regime OVERLAY use of EM/global stress (rather than ranker features) is permitted by the system's cadence constraints and was not the object refuted here — but it must clear redundancy against the existing VIX ladder / HMM / dispersion-breadth stack on its own evidence.
output.notes: Verified directly against the paper PDF (arXiv 2504.07855, pp.1-22) and the repo. Decisive facts: (1) paper signals are local-currency local-index returns across 47 markets with importance NOT concentrated in large markets (Qatar frequently top-5) — the proposal's 10 largest-market USD ETFs are a different, weaker object; (2) sample is 2012Q1-2022Q1 with in-paper decay concentrated in EM signals, which dominate the proposed basket; (3) per-model t-stats 2.34-2.77 with LASSO showing no decile-level significance (tail-only effect, inexpressible in top-7-of-50); (4) repo check (scripts/hypersearch_v2.py np.vstack pooling; model_lgb.py, indicators.py, panel_ranks.py — no symbol/sector/exposure features) proves broadcast weekly ETF returns enter as date-constant context features that cannot carry the paper's sign-heterogeneous per-stock mechanism; (5) at 11bp+spread the paper's own long-leg net six-factor alpha is ~0 to negative. No third-party replication exists (WebSearch, June 2026). Verdict: claim as proposed fails on evidence, non-redundancy, and long-only viability despite genuinely clean point-in-time plumbing. adjusted_confidence=2 reflects residual confidence in the CLAIM (a cheap gauntlet test of a redesigned exposure-interaction variant might salvage something), not in the as-proposed feature block, which I expect to add noise dimensions and consume a challenger slot. surviving_caveats: Theory overstated: the quoted Hedge bound sqrt(T ln N/2) does NOT hold for the actual estimator — fb-hour delayed feedback inflates regret by the delay factor, a rolling 30d window is not anytime Hedge, and the 0.5-shrink + [0.3,0.8] clamp breaks the bound entirely. By Jensen the shrunk mixture permanently carries ~half the prior's excess loss; a structurally broken LSTM head retains >=0.3 weight forever — it does NOT 'track the surviving head'. Sell this as approximately-equal weights with a slow bounded tilt (which the puzzle literature supports), not a regret-guaranteed tracker. The clamp, not the theorem, is the safety mechanism.

Loss normalization is unspecified and is the most likely silent failure: eta=sqrt(8 ln 2/T) assumes losses in [0,1]; raw squared %-return losses will leave weights either inert (~0.55 forever, vacuous adaptivity) or pinned at the clamp. Use BOA's second-order adaptive rates (cited but absent from the build sketch) or normalize losses, and verify in backtest replay that weights actually move when a head is degraded and stay put when not.

Loss-function mismatch: squared/pinball loss on return levels is not the decision loss — the book trades top-7/top-15 cross-sectional ranks, and a head can be worse in MSE yet better at ordering (level bias is rank-irrelevant). Prefer a per-hour cross-sectional loss (rank-IC or pinball on standardized cross-sectional scores); in any case the DM-HLN shadow on strategy PnL is the real gate and must remain mandatory before promotion.

Loss window must be tagged with champion model identity and reset on every retrain/promotion (copy the exact 'cm' mtime-filter precedent in shadow.py _load_rows, lines 204-210), or weights learned on the old head get attributed to the new one. Also exclude LGB-fallback hours (lgb_pred=None -> LSTM-only) from LGB's loss tally.

Persist per-head preds for ALL scored symbols via the existing hourly all-symbol path (base_loop.py:799 monitor_drift.log_predictions, or the snapshot dict like Q10 at predict_now.py:400-402) — NOT the trade journal: trade-conditioned losses are selection-biased by the very gates the heads feed. Cold start: ~30 trading days of logging + fb maturation before the first adaptive weight; hold the 0.6/0.4 prior until then.

Payoff honestly re-sized: with weekly retrains + 14-28d shadow + daily PSI drift monitor + meta-label/q10 vetoes already bounding a broken head's damage, the unique coverage is the asymmetric, distributionally-invisible single-head decay in the ~3-5 week gap before promotion machinery acts — and the shrunk/clamped 30d EWA itself needs weeks of matured labels to move. Realistic edge: partial de-weight (0.6 -> ~0.3-0.45) arriving ~1-3 weeks earlier than the existing machinery, not 'months'. Expected mean improvement ~0 per the claim's own cited literature; the most probable outcome is DM-HLN (correctly) declines to promote, which is an acceptable result at this cost.

Minor: weight drift slightly perturbs top-7/top-15 membership, so incremental turnover is small-but-nonzero (bounded by the clamp and daily cadence), not literally 'exactly zero new trades'. Immaterial at 11bps+spread. Build estimate ~60 lines is mildly optimistic; ~100-150 with reset logic, normalization, and tests.
output.notes: Survives — as a near-zero-cost robustness overlay, not an alpha claim; the proposal's own framing already concedes this and that honesty is why it stands. Code audit (all verified): fixed blend at model_lgb.py:137-153 with sole production call predict_now.py:333 using default 0.6; per-head preds computed separately (predict_now.py:314/332) but not yet persisted; every plumbing piece has an in-repo precedent (Q10 snapshot predict_now.py:400-402; hourly all-symbol pred logging base_loop.py:799 + monitor_drift.py:60-73; fb-lag maturation shadow.py:_realized 225-234; DM-HLN 153-185; model-identity reset template shadow.py:204-210; weekly retrain->challenger slot in run_pipeline.py). No redundancy: adaptive_config.py is HPO-space adaptation; nothing currently adapts the head blend; the mechanism is aggregation-level, uncorrelated with any feature, and covers the between-promotion gap that PSI/DM-HLN leave open — though that gap is narrower (~3-5 weeks) than claimed. Decay axis fails to kill it: the combination puzzle is a 50-year replicated result (Stock-Watson 2004; Smith-Wallis 2009; Timmermann 2006; Wang et al. 2023), regret bounds are theorems, and Remlinger et al. is peer-reviewed (Journal of Finance and Data Science, 2023; arXiv:2111.15365; SSRN 4513503) though lightly replicated — the design correctly does not lean on it. PIT clean: own predictions + own matured labels, zero publication lag, maturation enforced by existing shadow machinery. Long-only, costs, Jetson: all trivially fine (daily numpy job, milliseconds). What does NOT survive: the mechanism section's regret-bound rhetoric ('bounded worst case', 'automatically tracks the surviving head', 'months before retrain would catch it') — see caveats 1, 2, 3, 6; the safety comes from the clamp + shrink + DM-HLN gate, not the theorem. Confidence 3/5: net-non-negative with high probability given the gates, but expected mean gain ~0 and the insurance window is narrow; the most likely end state is the challenger gate never promotes it. Condition for build: implement caveats 2-5 (loss normalization or BOA rates; cross-sectional/rank-aware loss preferred; model-identity window resets; all-symbol logging path) and run it through shadow DM-HLN exactly as proposed. findings.name: Persistent shorting-flow cross-sectional feature from FINRA Reg SHO daily short-sale volume files (free, daily, same-day 6pm ET)
findings.mechanism: Short sellers are informed traders who arbitrage overpricing and long-horizon public information (they concentrate in the short legs of ~20 documented anomalies). Their aggregate flow per symbol is published FREE and DAILY by FINRA, unlike biweekly short interest. Critically, the informative construct is the PERSISTENT shorting level (trailing weeks/months of short-volume-ratio), not short-term spikes: Wang-Yan-Zheng show abnormal short-term shorting flows do NOT predict returns or anticipate news, while persistent flows predict negative returns that decay slowly over up to a year with NO long-run reversal (informed, not destabilizing). Market-maker liquidity shorting inflates the LEVEL of the ratio (avg ~36% of volume), but cross-sectional and time-series RANKS remain informative because MM contamination is roughly common-mode. For a long-only top-7 selector this works as an avoid/underweight tilt: stop buying the names the informed short community is persistently leaning on.
key_papers: Wang, Yan & Zheng (2020), Journal of Financial Economics 135(1):191-212, 'Shorting flows, public disclosure, and market efficiency' — uses the EXACT free FINRA daily files, all common stocks 2010-2015 (~3,766/day): daily quintiles on prior 5-day short-volume ratio, skip 1 day, hold 20 days -> heavily shorted underperform lightly shorted by 12.6%/yr risk-adjusted EW (t=6.00) and 6.0%/yr VW (t=4.03); predictability lasts ~1 year, driven by long-term (month/quarter) flows; abnormal short-term flows NOT predictive; no reversal

Boehmer, Jones & Zhang (2008), Journal of Finance 63(2), 'Which Shorts Are Informed?' — proprietary NYSE system order data 2000-2004; heavily shorted stocks underperform lightly shorted by ~1.16%/month (~15.6% annualized) risk-adjusted; institutional non-program shorts most informed

Diether, Lee & Werner (2009), Review of Financial Studies 22(2):575-607, 'Short-Sale Strategies and Return Predictability' — Reg SHO daily data 2005 (NYSE/Nasdaq, shorting = 24-31% of share volume): short sellers are contrarian in contemporaneous/past returns and correctly predict future negative abnormal returns at daily-weekly horizons; flow-based strategy profitable gross but authors note it does not survive costs as a STANDALONE high-turnover strategy (which is why this belongs as a ranking feature, not a strategy)
findings.effect_size_net: Anchor: 6.0%/yr VW gross quintile spread (large-cap relevant for our top-60-dollar-volume universe); long-only avoid-side captures roughly half, and assume ~50% post-publication decay (McLean-Pontiff) -> realistic ceiling ~1-2%/yr of avoided drag on the stock book. NET-of-cost is the key advantage: consumed as 2-3 extra LightGBM features that re-rank the same top-7/top-15 trades, it adds ZERO incremental turnover and zero data cost — the 11bps RT + spread budget is unchanged. Success metric is rank-IC lift and DM-HLN significance in shadow, not standalone P&L.
findings.decay_evidence: No formal published replication on 2016-2025 FINRA data found (honest gap — in-app shadow validation is the test). The paper itself documents regime change (2005-07 predictability was short-term; 2010-15 long-term), suggesting adaptation, and per McLean-Pontiff (2016 JF) expect 26-58% post-publication decay after the 2019/2020 publication. Post-2021 caveat: crowded-short squeeze regimes (GME era) make heavily-shorted names occasionally rip upward — benign for our LONG-ONLY use (worst case is forgone squeeze upside, never short-squeeze loss), and the q10 tail veto / meta-labeler already screens entry quality. Related supporting strands: Blocher et al. (2018) two types of short sellers (short-horizon traders vs long-horizon investors), Hu (2017) and Kahraman & Pachare (2018) on disclosure frequency improving price discovery.
findings.free_data_source: VERIFIED LIVE: https://cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/CNMSshvol{YYYYMMDD}.txt (pipe-delimited Date|Symbol|ShortVolume|ShortExemptVolume|TotalVolume|Market; fetched the 2026-06-10 file successfully; full daily history back to Aug 2009 at same URL pattern for backfill; also available via FINRA Query API). LAG: FINRA posts by ~6:00pm ET on the SAME trade date (FINRA Information Notice 5/10/19; Wang-Yan-Zheng footnote: 'rarely the next business day') -> point-in-time rule: nightly download after 8pm ET, feature usable from the NEXT session's open. Files are final (rare corrections); scope is FINRA-reported (TRF/ADF/ORF off-exchange) prints only — consistent over the sample, compute SVR = ShortVolume/TotalVolume within-file so numerator and denominator share scope.

findings.name: Treasury coupon-auction demand-shock gate for the 14:30-15:30 PM entry window (1pm ET scheduled event, same-day free results API)
findings.mechanism: Treasury auctions are scheduled 13:00 ET price-discovery events for the risk-free curve; weak demand (low bid-to-cover, high primary-dealer takedown, tailing high yield) repricing term premium transmits within minutes to equities via discount rates and risk appetite — hitting long-duration/high-beta names (our universe) hardest. The channel has STRENGTHENED structurally: Treasury demand is ~5x more inelastic since 2010 amid supply growth, so a given auction surprise moves prices more now. Our PM entry window opens 90 minutes after coupon-auction results — currently the system is blind to a known, free, scheduled risk event that sits directly upstream of it. This mirrors the already-implemented FOMC/CPI stand-down logic, extended to the ~8-10 coupon auction days/month with a CONDITIONAL (result-dependent) rather than unconditional stand-down.
key_papers: Phillot (2025), American Economic Journal: Macroeconomics 17(1):245-273, 'US Treasury Auctions: A High-Frequency Identification of Supply Shocks' — futures-price moves in tight windows around auction events 1998-2020: positive Treasury supply shocks shift the whole yield curve up (partly term premium) and cause STOCK PRICES TO DECLINE and equity volatility to RISE

Hanson et al. (HBS Working Paper 26-033, December 2025), 'What Treasury Auctions Reveal About Investor Demand' — demand elasticity measured from bidding data: pre-2010 a 1% supply increase moved long yields ~2bps, post-2010 ~9bps (5x more inelastic); pre-2010 yields fell ~1.5bps on average after auctions (strong-demand auctions), post-2010 that reversed; Treasury demand shocks account for >50% of corporate-bond-ETF price variation in the short windows around auction close and result RELEASE — direct evidence the 13:00-13:05 release window carries tradable risk-asset information

Lou, Yan & Zhang (2013), Review of Financial Studies 26(8), 'Anticipated and Repeated Shocks in Liquid Markets' — secondary Treasury prices systematically fall into auctions and recover after (auction-cycle price pressure), establishing that even fully ANTICIPATED supply events move prices when intermediary risk-bearing is constrained
findings.effect_size_net: Pure gating/sizing economics — adds ZERO trades and zero data cost; value is avoided tail loss and avoided fee-burn on PM entries made into a deteriorating rate tape. Coupon auctions (2y/3y/5y/7y/10y/20y/30y) cluster ~8-10 afternoons/month; composite-bad results at -1.5σ/-2.5σ thresholds fire on roughly 1-3 afternoons/month. Case studies (Oct-2023 and Aug/Nov-2024 30y tails) saw SPX drop 50-150bps from 13:00 to close with high-beta names ~1.5-2x that — skipping or halving 2-4 PM entries on such days at ~0.5-1% average adverse move per skipped entry is worth roughly 10-40bps/yr of avoided drawdown at book level, at the cost of forgoing ~5-8% of PM entry windows (measurable opportunity cost in shadow). Long-dated (10y/30y) auctions only for the hard gate; bills excluded (their results populate in the morning and carry little term-premium news).
findings.decay_evidence: Not a published cross-sectional anomaly subject to McLean-Pontiff crowding decay — it is a structural transmission channel that the 2025 HBS evidence shows has INTENSIFIED since 2010 (fiscal-supply era, dealer balance-sheet constraints). Honest framing: the literature establishes direction and magnitude of the rates/credit/equity-index response, but an equity-entry GATE at this app's cadence is an original formulation that must earn promotion via the shadow framework; main failure mode is that SPY's existing rest-of-day PM tape gate already partially captures post-13:00 weakness (test incremental value vs that gate explicitly, via DM-HLN on PM-window entries).
findings.free_data_source: VERIFIED LIVE: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/TA_WS/securities/auctioned?days=N — free JSON, no key, fields confirmed: BidToCoverRatio, PrimaryDealerAccepted ($), IndirectBidderAccepted, DirectBidderAccepted, HighYield, AuctionDate (compute PD share = PrimaryDealerAccepted/TotalAccepted). SAME-DAY population verified: today's 30y reopening (BTC 2.33, HY 5.02%) was present intraday on auction day; official results release is ~13:02 ET via press release, API populates shortly after. Calendar from /TA_WS/securities/upcoming (announced ~1 week ahead; tentative schedule quarterly). POINT-IN-TIME: results are final at release and never revised — zero vintage risk; the when-issued TAIL is NOT free -> proxy the surprise with TLT 13:00->13:15 reaction from Alpaca bars (market-computed surprise, PIT by construction), with BTC and PD-share z-scores vs the trailing 8 same-tenor auctions as confirmatory daily features.
findings.build_sketch: macro_calendar.py: add auction calendar (weekly cache of /upcoming, tag 10y/30y/20y coupon days). stock_loop.py PM-window gate, evaluated once at ~14:25 ET on coupon-auction days: composite z = mean(TLT 13:00-13:15 return z (Alpaca bars), -BidToCoverRatio z, PD-share z from TA_WS poll at 13:10); z < -1.5 -> halve new-entry budget for 14:30-15:30; z < -2.5 -> skip PM entries entirely (identical plumbing pattern to existing FOMC/CPI stand-down). Log gate decisions to shadow.py for gated-vs-ungated DM-HLN comparison against the incumbent SPY PM tape gate. Jetson cost: 1 JSON poll + 2 bar fetches per auction day — negligible.

findings.name: Stablecoin aggregate net-issuance as a crypto-sleeve liquidity state variable (daily, on-chain, zero lag)
findings.mechanism: Stablecoins (USDT+USDC ~ $260B verified today) are the funding currency and settlement medium of crypto markets; aggregate float expansion means net fiat is entering the ecosystem (minting requires wiring dollars to issuers), loosening the liquidity constraint for the majors we trade, while sustained redemptions mark de-risking/collateral stress regimes (e.g., post-FTX, USDC depeg week). Direction-of-causality is debated — supply-push (issuance precedes price support) vs demand-pull (minting responds to peg premia from inflow demand) — but BOTH interpretations make net issuance a valid liquidity STATE variable for sizing the crypto sleeve, which is exactly how we'd use it (overlay, not directional alpha). This is the on-chain analog of the funding-rate tilt already implemented, capturing fiat-side rather than leverage-side liquidity.
key_papers: Griffin & Shams (2020), Journal of Finance 75(4):1913-1964, 'Is Bitcoin Really Untethered?' — flows of Tether to exchanges follow Bitcoin downturns and precede strong rebounds; the 1% of hours with heaviest Tether flow account for a large share of Bitcoin's 2017 boom (supply-push/manipulation evidence, historical era)

Ante, Fiedler & Strehle (2021), Finance Research Letters 41, 'The influence of stablecoin issuances on cryptocurrency markets' — event study of 565 on-chain issuance events >= $1M across 7 stablecoins, Apr-2019 to Mar-2020: significant positive abnormal returns for major cryptos in the 24h around issuance, market downturns in the week BEFORE issuance (mint-the-dip dynamic); issuance SIZE not significant

Lyons & Viswanath-Natraj (2023), Journal of International Money and Finance 131, 'What Keeps Stablecoins Stable?' — signed-trade/order-book evidence that flows respond to peg deviations (arbitrage/demand-pull), arb spreads fell 70bps -> 30bps after 2019 Ethereum migration; stablecoins trade at >100bps PREMIUM in crises (Mar-2020) as crypto-internal safe haven — the rigorous pushback that kills naive causal supply-push trading and motivates the state-variable (sizing) use instead
findings.effect_size_net: As a weekly-cadence multiplier (0.7-1.3x) on crypto sleeve gross, incremental turnover is a few delta-adjustment trades/month on 6 liquid majors at ~10-25bps taker cost — order of 5-15bps/yr total cost, against the targeted benefit of sidestepping redemption-regime drawdowns (BTC drawdowns >20% in 2022-2023 coincided with multi-week stablecoin float contraction) and modestly upsizing expansion regimes. Target is crypto-sleeve Sharpe/max-drawdown improvement, not new alpha; the Ante et al. 24h event CARs are too small/fast to trade directly net of taker fees and are NOT the proposal.
findings.decay_evidence: Griffin-Shams 2017-era supply-push channel is gone (Lyons & Viswanath-Natraj; Tether market structure matured, arb spreads halved). Issuance-event abnormal returns documented pre-2021 have not been formally replicated post-2021 — honest status: the LEVEL/GROWTH overlay for 2023-2026 is practitioner-grade evidence (float growth tracked the 2023-2025 rallies; contractions tracked 2022 stress) and would be original in-app research validated through the crypto shadow framework. Regulatory regime change (GENIUS Act-era issuance growth) may strengthen the fiat-inflow interpretation but also adds non-crypto demand (payments) noise to the signal — monitor via drift monitors.

Jetson cost: one GET + 20 lines of pandas daily — negligible.

findings.name: Real-time SEC Form 144 (insider intent-to-sell) supply gate — electronic and machine-readable only since April 2023
findings.mechanism: Form 144 is the notice an affiliate must file CONCURRENTLY with placing an order to sell restricted/control stock (>5,000 shares or >$50K in 90 days) — it is forward-looking SUPPLY information (size + 90-day sale window), unlike Form 4 which prints up to 2 business days AFTER execution. Until April 2023 these were paper filings destroyed after 90 days — effectively invisible; the SEC's electronic mandate (compliance date 2023-04-13) put them on EDGAR in real time, creating a genuinely NEW, barely-studied data stream. For a concentrated 50-name high-beta book, a fresh large 144 cluster on a held/candidate name signals (a) mechanical sell pressure over coming days-weeks and (b) insider-timed exits that historically precede underperformance when non-routine (Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski logic). Proposed use is defensive: entry-tiebreak/size-haircut, not alpha — sign at short horizons is ambiguous because insiders sell into strength.
key_papers: Neupane (2026), arXiv:2602.17890 [q-fin.CP] (Feb 2026, PREPRINT, not yet peer-reviewed) — post-mandate Form 144/Form 4 linkage: Carhart-adjusted CAR(0,+2) after 144 filings is +14.49bps and statistically significant in LARGE caps (p=0.021) vs +32.21bps insignificant in small caps (insiders execute into strength — contrarian timing); 52.4% of notices are never fully executed within the 90-day window and are statistically indistinguishable from executed ones at filing time (a structural noise floor); prior idiosyncratic volatility amplifies post-filing illiquidity ~2.6x

Franzen, Li & Vargus (2013) — documents the 'reporting inversion': Form 144 preceded the Form 4 in 93.7% of cases pre-SOX but only 17.5% post-SOX (Form 4's 2-day e-filing deadline vs historically delayed paper 144s) — the key institutional caveat; the 2023 e-filing mandate restores Form 144 to same-day public visibility, which is precisely why the post-2023 stream is unstudied territory

Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski (2012), Journal of Finance 67(3), 'Decoding Inside Information' — only OPPORTUNISTIC (non-routine) insider trades predict returns (routine calendar-driven trades carry no information); value-weighted opportunistic-trade portfolios earn abnormal returns of ~7-8%/yr annualized — motivates filtering 144s by size vs insider's holdings and vs ADV rather than treating all equally; Lakonishok & Lee (2001, RFS 14(1)) — insider SALES are weakly informative relative to purchases, the standing caution for any sale-side signal
findings.effect_size_net: Too small to trade directionally: 14-32bps CAR(0,+2) is at/below our 11bps RT + spread budget, and the 52.4% non-execution rate halves effective precision — so this is strictly a ZERO-COST gate: when a fresh 144 cluster exceeds ~0.75x one day's ADV (or >2% of the insider's holdings, opportunistic per CMP screen) on a top-7 candidate, demote it for 1-3 sessions (buy the next-ranked name instead). Net economics = swap cost of zero (same trade count) vs avoided overhang drag on a handful of symbol-days/month; high-beta tech names in our universe (recent IPO/SPAC alumni, founder-heavy registers) are exactly where 144 supply is chunkiest relative to float.
findings.decay_evidence: Honest status: essentially UNSTUDIED post-electronic-mandate — one non-peer-reviewed 2026 preprint plus strong adjacent peer-reviewed insider-trading literature; this is original research to be proven or killed in the shadow framework, with the meta-label veto as the natural consumer. No crowding-decay risk yet (data is 3 years old as a machine-readable stream and obscure); main risks are the Franzen-Li-Vargus timing caveat (notice can arrive same-day as first execution — acceptable for an overhang gate), the 52% false-positive (non-execution) floor, and sale-side weakness per Lakonishok-Lee. Kill criterion: if 12 months of shadow shows no measurable difference in post-gate 1-3 day candidate returns, drop it.
findings.free_data_source: VERIFIED LIVE: EDGAR current-filings Atom feed https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcurrent&type=144&output=atom (returned live 144 entries with issuer CIK, accession, accepted timestamp; requires declared User-Agent header; ~minutes latency; EDGAR accepts filings to 22:00 ET so many post after close -> apply next morning). Filing XML (post-2023) carries shares, aggregate market value, approximate sale date, broker; CIK->ticker via https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json; EDGAR full-text search API (efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?forms=144, verified JSON with UA header) for historical backfill to Apr-2023. POINT-IN-TIME: append-only feed — log first-seen accepted-datetime ourselves; treat 144/A amendments as new events; only ~3 years of electronic history exists, so validation must be live/shadow rather than long backtest (state this in validation.py docs).
findings.build_sketch: edgar_events.py (extends existing 8-K/M&A EDGAR plumbing): poll the type=144 Atom feed every 15 min during RTH (1 HTTP GET + XML parse), filter to the ~96-name panel via CIK map, parse share count/value from filing XML, normalize by 21d ADV from existing Alpaca bars -> symbol-day field fresh_144_pct_adv with first-seen timestamps in the events store. stock_loop.py entry gate beside the existing earnings/8-K gates: demote candidate if fresh_144_pct_adv > 0.75 within last 3 sessions; also emit as a meta_label.py feature so the veto model can learn its true weight. Jetson cost: negligible (small XML polls, no model change).

fatal_flaws: Evidence base is a single unreplicated, non-peer-reviewed working paper (Jiao, SSRN ~May 2024 / arXiv Apr 2025): ~2 years public with zero independent citations or replications found; built on a 100,000-model search with wide cross-model dispersion (the LightGBM-class GB learner is the weakest variant at 3.80bp/day gross; positive OOS R-squared share swings 8%-36% by model class) — a data-snooping signature, with McLean-Pontiff decay and the paper's own documented absorption-speedup stacked on top.

Architecture/mechanism mismatch verified in the repo: the paper's effect is carried entirely by stock-specific, sign-heterogeneous loadings (hence 100k per-stock models), but the proposed build broadcasts cross-sectionally CONSTANT features into a pooled LightGBM that has no symbol ID, no sector, and no foreign-exposure characteristic (indicator_config.py / panel_ranks.py) — there is no channel to learn 'AMD loads on Taiwan'. The expressible residual is a common time-series response, i.e., lagged-foreign->US market timing — exactly the direction Rapach-Strauss-Zhou (2013, JF, peer-reviewed) shows is weak/absent. The proposal cites RSZ to kill the naive version while proposing an architecture that can mostly only express the naive version.

The advertised kill-switch ('quarterly per-symbol LASSO screen to zero out features for never-loading names') is unimplementable as described: a broadcast column in a pooled model cannot be zeroed for some rows without per-name interaction columns (500-2000 extra features) or per-name models, neither proposed nor scoped.

Return-timing mismatch: the paper's alpha is daily close-to-close on L/S 5% tails of ~500 names; this book is long-only top-7-of-50 and flat by 15:50 ET. Multi-week diffusion premia plausibly accrue largely overnight (Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019 tug-of-war evidence), which the system cannot hold except via the small overnight sleeve — so even an optimistic ranking-IC gain may not convert to realized intraday P&L.

Source-market mismatch: the paper locates surviving predictability in EM/low-media-coverage source markets, but the proposed basket (EWJ, EWG, EWU, EWQ, MCHI/FXI, EWY, EWT, INDA, EWZ, EEM) is DM plus the highest-coverage EMs — the signals absorbed fastest; and US-session ETF closes carry ~0.7-0.9 weekly correlation to SPY, so the lagged 'foreign' block substantially duplicates lagged US market state already conditioned on by the HMM/VIX-ladder/SPY-trend overlays (effective novel dimensionality ~3-4 relative-country factors, not 20 features).

Integration claim mischaracterizes the actual plumbing: predict_now.py loads one shared feature_cols for both models, so +20 weekly-constant features enter the hourly LSTM as dead channels AND model_lgb.flatten_sequence replicates each across seq_len lags into 20xL near-duplicate LGB columns diluting feature_fraction sampling; an LGB-only side-feature path does not exist and building it is unscoped new infrastructure.
surviving_caveats: Point-in-time plumbing is genuinely clean — the strongest axis: completed-prior-week US-listed ETF closes have zero publication lag, no revisions, no reconstitution, no rescaling; only a trivial yfinance-to-Alpaca adjustment-convention seam at the backfill splice.

The features-not-strategy reframing correctly neutralizes the turnover/cost objection; a feature block mandates no extra trades and the DSR-holdout + challenger-shadow gauntlet makes the marginal test cost low (the objection is expected benefit ~0, not expected harm).

The parent literature family — gradual diffusion across economic links (Cohen-Frazzini 2008, Hong-Torous-Valkanov 2007, Menzly-Ozbas 2010, Rizova 2010) — is among the better-replicated lead-lag mechanisms; the mechanism is plausible, it is this specific unreplicated implementation and its architecture translation that fail.

Salvage path if ever revisited: convert to NAME-VARYING exposure features (rolling 26-52w beta of each name to SPY-residualized country-ETF returns — time-varying, CS-rankable, fits the existing GKX rank machinery and supplies the missing heterogeneity channel), gated on third-party replication or journal acceptance of Jiao (2025) appearing first.
Jetson data/compute cost for the raw inputs (10 daily ETF series, weekly resample) is honestly negligible as claimed.
output.notes: Verdict rests on two independent kills, either sufficient. (1) Evidence: sole support is Jiao 'Foreign Signal Radar' (arXiv 2504.07855 / SSRN 4822651), an unpublished single-author working paper public ~2 years with no independent citations or replications found in repeated searches (only author postings on arXiv/SSRN/RePEc/alphaXiv); its 100k-model design, wide cross-model dispersion (GB-class weakest at 3.80bp/day), self-documented absorption acceleration, and McLean-Pontiff/HXZ priors put the post-2020, GB-class, DM-plus-high-coverage-EM residue below DSR-holdout detectability. (2) Architecture, verified against the actual repo (/Users/kywwilson/Desktop/Projects/trader/indicator_config.py, panel_ranks.py, model_lgb.py, predict_now.py): the pooled model has no symbol/sector/exposure channel, so broadcast cross-sectionally-constant ETF features cannot express the paper's per-stock heterogeneous loadings — the learnable component collapses to lagged-foreign->US common timing, which peer-reviewed Rapach-Strauss-Zhou (2013) rules out; the proposed per-symbol LASSO kill-switch is unimplementable for broadcast columns; and the shared feature_cols pipeline means the '+20 features' actually lands as dead LSTM channels plus 20x seq_len duplicated LGB columns. PIT plumbing (completed-week US-listed ETF closes) is genuinely clean and the feature-not-strategy cost framing is sound — hence adjusted_confidence 2 rather than 1 — but survives requires surviving evidence AND non-redundancy AND long-only viability, and the claim fails the first (unreplicated WP), the third (close-to-close alpha plausibly overnight-accruing vs a 15:50-flatten book), and partially the redundancy bar (US-session ETF closes are ~0.7-0.9 correlated with SPY, duplicating existing regime conditioning). Recommendation embedded in caveats: do not build as specified; if wave-5 wants this family, the only defensible variant is name-varying exposure-interaction features (rolling betas to SPY-residualized country ETFs through the existing GKX/CS-rank machinery), and only after third-party replication or journal acceptance of Jiao materializes. Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07855, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4822651, https://ideas.repec.org/p/arx/papers/2504.07855.html.

hint: JKX image-scale distillation: rolling high-low-range-normalized OHLCV+MA features (the paper's OWN linear approximation

surviving_caveats: Redundancy is materially understated despite the 'honest overlap note'. Verified in code: STOCHk_14_3_3/STOCHd (= pos_in_range at L=14) already feed the models (/Users/kywwilson/Desktop/Projects/trader/indicator_config.py lines 49/68/102), and CS_RANK_BASE_COLS in /Users/kywwilson/Desktop/Projects/trader/panel_ranks.py already contains Price_SMA20_Ratio (= ma_gap@20), Volume_Ratio (= vol_trend family), ATR_Pct (~= range_width, corr ~0.9 with Parkinson), and Return_4h/Return_12h/ROC/RSI (short-reversal content overlapping midrange_gap). The JKX Table-13 orthogonality argument (McFadden R^2 4.6-11.9%) applies to the CNN, NOT the linear distillate, which explains only 20-35% of CNN forecast variation — it does not license an orthogonality claim against this app's stack. Genuinely new content is limited to: multi-window pos_in_range (5/60), lag-1..5 OHLC window-scaled levels, midrange_gap exact form, range-denominator normalization, and the daily 50/100/200d MA-gap stack (HZZ/AKS — confirmed absent from the stack). REQUIRE an ablation null of 'multi-window Stoch + existing columns' so a DSR pass is not misattributed to JKX novelty.

Horizon mismatch: every cited result is >=5-day returns at daily formation; zero cited evidence at hourly/intraday horizon, and the 15:50 daily flatten discards most of the multi-day drift the daily features predict (only the small overnight sleeve carries it). The hourly-bar window variants are an unevidenced extrapolation, redeemed only by re-supervision on the app's own triple-barrier labels + purged WFCV + DSR gate. Directionally favorable: the 2024 AUT dissection finds the signal strongest at 5-day and monotonically weaker to 60-day, so shorter is better — but hourly remains untested. Expect the BOTTOM of the claimed +0.005-0.02 IC range.

Standalone calibration is shakier than claimed at the 20-day point: the independent AUT replication (July 2024) reproduces JKX (EW H-L Sharpe 7.18, VW 1.57 weekly — validates the algorithm) but finds the JKX value-weighted portfolio 'not significant at all' at the MONTHLY horizon, and the trend-persistence component disappears or turns negative VW (small-firm effect). In a 50-name liquid universe, what plausibly survives is the short-horizon reversal component; treat the VW 0.5-0.7 20-day Sharpe anchor as optimistic.

Adverse-selection cost nuance: 'cost-neutral' is right on trade COUNT (top-7/top-15 caps + daily flatten fix turnover), but a low-in-range reversal tilt systematically buys high-beta names right after sharp drops, when spreads are widest — the spread component of cost rises at fixed trade count. Existing q10 tail veto, meta-label veto, and earnings/8-K gates mitigate; monitor realized spread on JKX-tilted entries.

Data quality, not PIT: Alpaca free tier is IEX-only OHLCV (~2-3% of tape, no auction prints), so hourly highs/lows/volume — the defining inputs of range features — are noisy proxies of consolidated extremes. Not a bias (same feed in training and live, population parity holds; same issue already affects Stoch/ATR), but use consolidated daily OHLC from Stooq/yfinance for the daily-window variants and keep volume strictly within-symbol-relative as proposed.

Wave-3 adjacency: pos_in_range(60d, daily) at its HIGH end is a 60-day-high-proximity feature — a cousin of the killed 52-week-high anchoring signal. The JKX sign is reversal (low-in-range bullish) and AKS MAD survives 52WH controls, so it is not a re-proposal, but verify via meta-label/SHAP that the 60d daily variant does not reconstitute a 52WH clone before keeping it.

Decay realism: 2023 publication is too recent for a McLean-Pontiff estimate; the WSTR-correlated component (-26% to -34%) sits in the most-arbitraged corner of the market. The proposer's ~50% haircut is appropriate; the HZZ/AKS MA-gap evidence ends 2018 (AKS sample 1977-2018), so apply the same haircut there. Feature-count discipline: ~30-40 new columns on a 96-name panel invites dilution — prune aggressively via the existing meta-label/SHAP pass.
output.notes: Verdict: survives, with expectations marked down. This is the rare TA-class proposal that clears the kill criteria: (1) Evidence survives attack — no failed replication found; the AUT working paper (acfr.aut.ac.nz/__data/assets/pdf_file/0005/925943/CNN-Draft-July-2024.pdf, fetched and read) independently reproduces JKX's headline numbers and explicitly 'validates' the algorithm; JKX trained once on 1993-2000 with 19y OOS (papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3756587; onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/jofi.13268); Murray-Xia-Xiao JFE 2024 (ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v153y2024ics0304405x2400014x.html) confirms price-only ML predictability is strong among the largest 500 stocks and stable through time; AKS MAD (onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/rfe.1118) is confirmed real with ~9% VW alpha and — key for this app — 'stronger on the long side', supporting long-only viability. (2) PIT is genuinely clean (price/volume only, zero publication lag); the IEX-feed issue is noise with train/live parity, not bias. (3) Long-only viable per AKS long-side dominance and positive long-leg deciles in both JKX and the replication. (4) Non-redundancy is real but THIN — roughly 4 of 6 proposed feature families have close cousins already in the stack (verified in indicator_config.py and panel_ranks.py); the load-bearing novel pieces are the multi-window structure, lag-OHLC common-scaled levels, midrange_gap, and the 50/100/200d MA-gap stack. Compute is trivially honest (vectorized rolling ops, no CNN). Cost attack fails structurally (daily flatten + capped entries fix turnover). The two reasons confidence is 3 not 4: all supervised evidence is >=5-day horizon vs the app's intraday holds, and the independent replication finds JKX VW insignificant at the monthly horizon — so the realistic payoff is the bottom of the claimed IC range, decided by the existing purged-WFCV + DSR gate, which is exactly the right adjudicator. Demand before merge: (a) ablation vs multi-window-Stoch null, (b) consolidated daily OHLC source for daily windows, (c) SHAP check that pos_in_range(60d) is not a 52WH clone, (d) meta-label prune of duplicated columns. Sources: SSRN 3756587; Wiley jofi.13268; AUT CNN-Draft-July-2024 PDF; RePEc jfinec v153 (Charting by Machines); Wiley rfe.1118 (AKS MAD); SSRN 2182667 (HZZ trend factor); github.com/lich99/Stock_CNN (community replication).
