findings.name: Session-decomposed momentum: the momentum premium accrues entirely overnight — route it to the overnight sleeve, de-weight it intraday
findings.mechanism: Clientele segmentation plus arbitrageur constraints. Institutions initiate trades intraday and especially near the close; individuals/uninformed demand concentrates at the open. Arbitrageurs face overnight margin and stock-lending fees charged only on overnight positions (Bogousslavsky), so they cut positions before the close and re-enter intraday — momentum/reversal premia are compensation that accrues while arbitrage capital is offline (close-to-open). The result: price momentum, industry momentum, earnings momentum, TS momentum, and short-term reversal earn their ENTIRE premium overnight with NEGATIVE intraday alpha; the other nine standard premia (value, size, profitability, beta, ivol, accruals, issuance, turnover) accrue intraday. This is a structural persistence (signals lagged 60 months still work, joint t>20), not microstructure noise. Direct implication for an app that flattens at 15:50 and runs a small overnight sleeve: the intraday book is fighting momentum's tug-of-war (institutional unwind into the close), while the overnight sleeve is exactly where momentum-type signal weight should live.
key_papers: Lou, Polk, Skouras (2019), 'A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns', Journal of Financial Economics 134(1), 192-213. VW decile sorted on past overnight returns: three-factor OVERNIGHT alpha +3.47%/mo (t=16.83) vs INTRADAY alpha -3.02%/mo (t=-9.74); intraday-sorted analog +2.41%/mo intraday (t=7.70) vs -1.77%/mo overnight (t=-7.89); persists with 60-month-lagged signals; CRSP/TAQ 1993-2013; overnight return measured close -> 9:30-10:00 VWAP, robust to open-price definitions and to excluding small caps; institutional momentum unwind generates ~2%/mo variation in the overnight-intraday momentum spread.

Bogousslavsky (2021), 'The cross-section of intraday and overnight returns', Journal of Financial Economics 141(1), 172-194. Confirms decomposition; anomaly longs perform poorly specifically in the LAST half hour (arbitrageur de-levering before the close), pattern STRONGER in recent years — direct support for the 15:50 flatten and for not chasing anomaly longs into the close.

Hendershott, Livdan, Roesch (2020), 'Asset pricing: A tale of night and day', Journal of Financial Economics 138(3), 635-662. CAPM holds overnight (returns increase in beta) and INVERTS intraday (negative beta-return relation during trading hours), for US and international stocks, beta-sorted portfolios and individual names — for a high-beta universe, beta is paid overnight, not intraday.
findings.effect_size_net: Gross overnight-momentum decile spread alpha 3.47%/mo is a long-short, all-cap 1993-2013 number; for a long-only top-slice in 50 liquid large caps apply ~1/3 spread capture and a ~50% post-publication haircut: realistic +40-80bps/mo of selection improvement ON SLEEVE CAPITAL. Critically, marginal cost is ~zero: the sleeve already exists and already pays the 11bps RT + spread — this changes WHICH names are held overnight, not how many trades occur. LPS themselves warn standalone close-open round-trips are cost-prohibitive (2 crossings/night vs ~3-6bps/night long-only edge per name) — do NOT build a dedicated overnight churn book; re-rank the existing sleeve and add session features to the model. Secondary effect: giving the hourly model ON_mom/ID_mom features lets it stop crediting stale momentum intraday (intraday momentum alpha is NEGATIVE), plausibly worth a few bps/trade in avoided adverse selection.
findings.decay_evidence: Stronger than typical anomalies. Within-paper: persistence robust to 60-month signal lags. Post-publication: Bogousslavsky (JFE 2021) reports the close-of-day anomaly weakness is STRONGER in recent years; Hendershott et al. (JFE 2020) replicate night/day beta internationally back to 1990s; Taiwan replication (Pacific-Basin Finance Journal 2023) and China overnight-momentum evidence (Int. Review of Financial Analysis 2019) confirm out-of-US. Apply the standard Jacobs-Mueller (JFE 2020) / McLean-Pontiff (JF 2016) US haircut (-26% post-sample, -58% post-publication) to be safe — reflected in the net estimate above. One caveat: in retail-attention small caps, high overnight returns predict reversal (lottery demand); our top-60-dollar-volume universe is institutional, where LPS persistence dominates.
findings.free_data_source: Alpaca market data API (data.alpaca.markets /v2/stocks/bars), free Basic plan, SIP-consolidated historical bars. ON_ret_t = open_t/close_{t-1}-1 from daily bars, or the exact LPS spec: first-half-hour VWAP from 1-minute bars (9:30-10:00) over close_{t-1}; ID_ret_t = close_t/open_t-1. Zero publication lag, bars immutable once printed — fully point-in-time by construction (use unadjusted prices plus as-of split/dividend factors; corporate actions are known ex-ante). The 15-min SIP delay on the free tier is irrelevant for a 15:30-computed daily feature.
findings.build_sketch: Module features/session_decomp.py: per name nightly, compute ON_ret and ID_ret from daily bars (optionally minute-VWAP open), then rolling means over 21d/60d/252d -> ON_mom_k, ID_mom_k, TugOfWar = ON_mom - ID_mom; cross-sectional z via existing GKX transform; append to LSTM/LGBM panel (3-6 new columns). Sleeve change: at 15:50 overnight-sleeve selection, blend existing model score with ON_mom_252 rank (e.g., 70/30) and require earnings-gate pass (already exists). Cadence: daily overlay computation at ~15:30 ET; features feed the hourly model at retrain. Jetson cost: rolling means over 96 names x 252 days, <1MB RAM, milliseconds; no architecture or training changes.

findings.name: The peer-reviewed kernel of Connors-style dip-buying: VIX-conditioned residual short-term reversal as entry-timing in large caps (the only oscillator mean-reversion that survives costs)
findings.mechanism: Short-term reversal at 1-5 day/1-month horizons is the returns to LIQUIDITY PROVISION, not a chart pattern (Nagel). When intermediary capital is constrained (high VIX), liquidity providers withdraw and the compensation for absorbing temporary order-flow imbalances spikes; in calm markets the premium is near zero and costs eat it. Two refinements make it net-implementable exactly at this app's scale: (1) restrict to the largest, most liquid names — the cost problem of classic reversal is almost entirely excessive trading in small caps (De Groot et al.); (2) residualize returns against factors before measuring the dip — conventional reversal sorts confound temporary liquidity pressure with factor moves, and residual reversal doubles risk-adjusted returns with stable performance since 1929 (Blitz et al.). RSI(2)/Connors folklore has no peer-reviewed support as a standalone rule; this is what actually survives: conditional, residualized, large-cap-only, and as entry timing rather than a signal in itself.
key_papers: Nagel (2012), 'Evaporating liquidity', Review of Financial Studies 25(7), 2005-2039. Short-term reversal strategy returns are highly predictable by VIX; expected returns and conditional Sharpe of liquidity provision spike in turmoil and are near zero in calm regimes — the signal is the INTERACTION, not the level.

De Groot, Huij, Zhou (2012), 'Another look at trading costs and short-term reversal profits', Journal of Banking & Finance 36(2). Restricted to the ~100 largest US stocks with turnover-aware construction, reversal strategies net 30-50bps PER WEEK after institutional-scale transaction costs; cost drag of classic implementations is attributable to small caps.

Blitz, Huij, Lansdorp, Verbeek (2013), 'Short-term residual reversal', Journal of Financial Markets 16(3), 477-504. Reversal on FF-residual returns earns risk-adjusted returns ~2x conventional reversal, statistically and economically significant NET of costs even in large caps post-1990, with stable dynamics 1929-2008 (no dynamic factor exposures).

Medhat, Schmeling (2022), 'Short-term momentum', Review of Financial Studies 35(3). Caveat paper: 1-month reversal concentrates in LOW-turnover names while high-turnover names continue — the app's existing MS_Interact already encodes this; the new content here is the horizon (3-5d), the residualization, and the VIX conditioning.
findings.effect_size_net: As an entry-timing tiebreak inside trades the model has already approved, marginal cost is zero (same trade count, better entry prices). Magnitude bound from De Groot et al.: 30-50bps/week net for a dedicated large-cap strategy; as a tilt over ~7 entries/day expect single-digit bps per trade of expected-return improvement, concentrated in high-VIX regimes (Nagel: conditional premium 2-3x unconditional when VIX is in its top tercile, ~0 in the bottom). Realistic app-level: +20-60bps/yr book-level in calm years, several times that in stress years — asymmetric payoff that complements the existing VIX sizing ladder rather than duplicating it (the ladder de-risks in high VIX; this says the trades you DO take should be dips, not chases).
findings.decay_evidence: Reversal is one of the oldest published anomalies (Jegadeesh 1990, Lehmann 1990) yet the large-cap residual version remained net-positive decades post-publication (Blitz et al. show stability 1929-2008; Robeco runs it live). Hou-Xue-Zhang (RFS 2020) replication: short-horizon reversal survives value-weighting though attenuated; McLean-Pontiff haircut applies but the Nagel mechanism (intermediary constraints) is risk-based compensation, not informational mispricing — the class of anomaly that decays least. Honest negative: at pure 1-2 day horizons in megacaps, post-2010 unconditional reversal is roughly zero net — which is exactly why the VIX interaction and residualization are load-bearing, not optional.
findings.free_data_source: Prices: Alpaca daily/hourly bars (free, point-in-time by construction, no lag). Residuals: reuse the app's existing residual-momentum (RM_252_21) regression infrastructure — same factor proxies, no new data. VIX: already ingested by the app; for reference, CBOE posts the official daily history same evening at https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/us_indices/daily_prices/VIX_History.csv (never revised); FRED VIXCLS lags 1 business day, also unrevised — use prior close, which is point-in-time safe either way.
findings.build_sketch: Module features/resid_reversal.py: nightly, compute 3d/5d/21d residual returns per name from the existing residualization pipeline; z-score cross-sectionally; add features RR_3, RR_5, RR_21 and interactions RR_k x VIX_pctile (VIX percentile vs trailing 2y). Application layer: in the entry selector, among model-approved candidates within a bucket, prefer lower RR_5 when VIX_pctile > 0.7 (tiebreak only — never overrides the model score, meta-label veto, or q10 tail veto). Cadence: features daily; application at hourly entry windows. Jetson cost: a few OLS residual updates and rolling sums per name per day — negligible (<10ms, <1MB).

findings.name: Multi-horizon moving-average distance features (Han-Zhou-Zhu trend factor), fed to the learner instead of used as rules
findings.mechanism: In an information-asymmetry equilibrium (HZZ's model), moving averages of prices aggregate stale and dispersed information; trends at short, intermediate, and long horizons carry INDEPENDENT predictive content, and the optimal combination weight on each horizon is time-varying (regime-dependent). HZZ implement this with rolling cross-sectional regressions of returns on normalized MA prices at lags ~3-1000 days — functionally identical to what a pooled LGBM does with the same inputs, learned better. The app's per-name technical features (RSI/MACD/BB on hourly bars) only span short horizons with FIXED windows, and its only long-horizon trend object is the INDEX-level 200d filter; per-name multi-horizon daily MA-distance structure (e.g., price vs 50/100/200d MA, 21d MA vs 200d MA) is plausibly absent from the panel. This is the one piece of classic 'moving average' TA that survives modern scrutiny — precisely because it is consumed as a cross-sectional forecasting INPUT with learned, time-varying weights rather than a buy/sell rule.
key_papers: Han, Zhou, Zhu (2016), 'A trend factor: Any economic gains from using information over investment horizons?', Journal of Financial Economics 122(2), 352-375. Trend factor averages 1.63%/mo (EW, all-cap 1930-2014), alpha ~45% larger than momentum with t=13.6 vs 6.04; more than doubles the Sharpe of reversal/momentum/long-term-reversal factors; earned +0.75%/mo through the 2008 crisis while momentum lost -3.88%/mo (it is NOT momentum in disguise — it diversifies it).
Han, Zhou et al. (2022), 'A trend factor in commodity futures markets', Journal of Futures Markets 42(5). Same construction works out-of-asset-class — evidence against data snooping.

Liu, Zhou, Zhu (2024), 'Trend factor in China: The role of large individual trading', Review of Asset Pricing Studies 14(2). Replicates in a structurally different market; monthly Sharpe 0.48 vs market 0.11; mechanism tied to uninformed trading flows.

Avramov, Kaplanski, Subrahmanyam (2021), 'Moving average distance as a predictor of equity returns', Review of Financial Economics 39(2), 127-145. The single ratio MA(21)/MA(200) alone yields ~9%/yr VW hedge-portfolio alpha, subsuming neither momentum nor 52-week-high; cite with caution — anchoring mechanism is a cousin of the app's killed 52-week-high feature and the journal is second-tier, so treat as corroboration only.
findings.effect_size_net: Do not budget the 1.63%/mo headline — it is EW, all-cap, microcap-inflated, and gross. In a 50-name top-dollar-volume universe expect a feature-level lift of order 10-30bps/mo at book level IF the learner finds incremental signal (HZZ's own VW and large-cap robustness checks retain significance at roughly half magnitude). As pure features the marginal trading cost is zero — turnover is already governed by the model plus fee-aware gating; the existing purged-CV + DSR holdout pipeline is exactly the right arbiter of whether they earn their place. Worst case: feature importance ~0 and they are dropped at no cost.
findings.decay_evidence: US trend factor weakened post-2000 relative to the 1930-1999 sample (as has reversal, one of its inputs) but the multi-horizon combination remained positive where single-horizon rules died; out-of-asset-class (commodities 2022) and out-of-country (China 2024, RAPS) replications are recent and strong, which McLean-Pontiff logic credits as evidence against snooping. Not in the Hou-Xue-Zhang 452-anomaly set (it is a composite forecast, not a single sort), but its component horizons (momentum) replicate under VW/NYSE breakpoints. Apply the standard -26%/-58% post-sample/post-publication haircut; the net estimate above already does.
findings.free_data_source: Alpaca daily bars only (free Basic plan, SIP history; aggregate the existing hourly ingestion if preferred). All MAs computed from own-price history: zero publication lag, immutable, point-in-time by construction. Use unadjusted prices with as-of corporate-action factors so MAs do not look-ahead through splits.
findings.build_sketch: Module features/ma_distance.py: nightly per name, SMA over {10,20,50,100,200} daily closes; features f_k = close/SMA_k - 1 and MAD = SMA_21/SMA_200 - 1; cross-sectional z-score via existing GKX transform; append ~6 columns to the panel for both LGBM and LSTM. Deliberately EXCLUDE lags <10d to avoid double-counting the residual-reversal feature above. Cadence: daily features feeding the hourly model. Jetson cost: trivially small (rolling sums, <1MB, milliseconds); no new model capacity needed.

findings.name: The folklore demolition (negative result with teeth): no single-name TA rule survives data-snooping control plus costs — the app's index-level trend filter is the lone rule-form survivor; enforce a 'features-not-rules' policy
findings.mechanism: Why rule-based TA fails: with thousands of correlated rule parameterizations, the maximum in-sample statistic is inflated (data snooping); controlling the false discovery rate reveals approximately zero true discoveries in the modern era, and the few historical ones were never selectable EX ANTE (persistence tests fail) and die under even small costs. What survives the same scrutiny is exactly two things the app already holds in the right form: (1) INDEX-level trend/TSMOM as a drawdown-control overlay (the SPY 200d filter — Zakamulin shows MA and TSMOM rules are near-equivalent weighting schemes on past returns, statistically indistinguishable from each other, with OOS value confined to prolonged bears), and (2) price-history information consumed as FEATURES inside a cross-sectional learner with proper validation (findings above). Everything else — single-stock MA crossovers, Donchian/channel breakouts on equities (a 52-week-high cousin, already killed at this horizon), candlestick patterns, fixed oscillator thresholds — is folklore at this universe and horizon.
key_papers: Brock, Lakonishok, LeBaron (1992), Journal of Finance 47(5), 1731-1764. The origin: 26 MA/trading-range rules on DJIA 1897-1986, buy signals beat sell signals with lower volatility, inconsistent with RW/AR(1)/GARCH-M/EGARCH nulls — the best pre-cost, pre-snooping case ever made for TA rules.

Sullivan, Timmermann, White (1999), Journal of Finance 54(5). White's Reality Check over 7,846 rule universe: BLL's best rule survives snooping adjustment in-sample 1897-1986 but has NO significant value 1987-1996 out-of-sample.

Bajgrowicz, Scaillet (2012), 'Technical trading revisited: False discoveries, persistence tests, and transaction costs', Journal of Financial Economics 106(3), 473-491. The execution: same 7,846 rules, DJIA 1897-2011, FDR control — an investor could NEVER have selected ex ante the future best rules, and even in-sample performance is completely offset by low transaction costs; rule profits that existed pre-1960s vanish thereafter.

Marshall, Young, Rose (2006), 'Candlestick technical trading strategies: Can they create value for investors?', Journal of Banking & Finance 30(8), 2303-2323. Bootstrap with randomized OHLC on DJIA stocks 1992-2001: candlesticks have zero value, gross OR net. Dead, including in follow-ups (Japan).

Zakamulin (2014), 'The real-life performance of market timing with moving average and time-series momentum rules', Journal of Asset Management 15(4). 80-year out-of-sample forward tests with realistic frictions: timing matches buy-and-hold risk-adjusted at best, outperformance is mean-reverting and confined to prolonged bear markets — i.e., keep the 200d filter as drawdown control, expect no alpha from it, and do not multiply MA variants.

Huang, Li, Wang, Zhou (2020), 'Time series momentum: Is it there?', Journal of Financial Economics 135(3), 774-794, plus Goyal, Jegadeesh (2018), RFS 31(5), 1784-1824. Asset-by-asset 12-1 TSMOM regressions show little evidence in- OR out-of-sample (pooled t-stats fail proper bootstraps); the TS-vs-CS strategy difference is just a time-varying net-long market position. Do NOT add per-name TSMOM-sign gates — the app's cross-sectional momentum features plus the index filter already capture everything real here.
findings.effect_size_net: Zero direct return — the payoff is avoided losses and avoided engineering: every single-name rule gate (MA cross, Donchian breakout, candlestick trigger, RSI threshold) carries expected NEGATIVE net value at 11bps RT + spread once snooping is controlled, plus opportunity cost of Jetson capacity and added gate-stack complexity that degrades the existing meta-label/q10 veto calibration. The kill list stays killed; this finding generalizes it from five specific items to the entire rule class with the citation arc to defend it.
findings.decay_evidence: This IS the decay evidence: the only TA literature whose conclusion strengthened over 30 years of replication (1992 positive -> 1999 weakened -> 2012 eliminated; candlesticks never worked; per-asset TSMOM never robust). International FDR follow-ups (e.g., MSCI-index discrete-FDR studies) reach the same conclusion. There is no revisionist literature rehabilitating single-stock TA rules in liquid US large caps net of costs.
findings.free_data_source: None required (policy finding). All cited tests used public daily index/stock prices.
findings.build_sketch: No new computation. Codify in the strategy module docs/config: (1) price-history ideas enter ONLY as panel features subject to purged walk-forward CV + DSR holdout, never as standalone entry/exit gates; (2) freeze the index trend overlay at the existing SPY 200d + HMM + Hurst stack — adding MA variants is statistically indistinguishable redundancy (Zakamulin); (3) reject any future per-name TSMOM-sign, breakout, or candlestick gate proposals by default, citing this arc. Jetson cost: zero (it saves capacity).

findings.name: Market intraday momentum into the close: condition the PM window and the 15:50 flatten on the day-so-far SPY tape (the one trade-cadence TA survivor, with honest decay caveats)
findings.mechanism: The last ~30-60 minutes of the session systematically continues the day's earlier move. Two verified mechanisms: (1) late-informed trading and intraday portfolio rebalancing (Gao et al.); (2) mechanical hedging flows — market makers short gamma and leveraged-ETF rebalancers must trade IN the direction of the day's move near the close (Baltussen et al.), which is why the effect concentrates on volatile, high-volume, macro-news days and REVERTS over subsequent days (it is a flow, not information). For this app it is a sizing/timing modifier in the 14:30-15:30 entry window and at the 15:50 flatten: on a strong positive day-so-far tape, later entries and a full hold to 15:50 are tailwinded; on a strong negative tape, trim earlier and shade PM entry sizes down. Note this is CONTINUATION into the close — consistent with the app's red-team kill of hard EOD-REVERSAL rules, and with Bogousslavsky's finding that anomaly longs sag in the last half hour while the index tape continues.
key_papers: Gao, Han, Li, Zhou (2018), 'Market intraday momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 129(2), 394-414. SPY 1993-2013: first half-hour return (measured from prior close) predicts the last half-hour return with R-squared 1.6%, rising to 2.6% adding the 12th half-hour; significant OUT-of-sample; stronger on high-volatility, high-volume, recession, and macro-release days; present in 10 other liquid US/international ETFs.

Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (2021), 'Hedging demand and market intraday momentum', Journal of Financial Economics 142(1), 377-403. Confirms in 60+ equity/bond/commodity/FX futures 1974-2020: last-30-min return positively predicted by rest-of-day return; economically and statistically large; explicitly linked to option market-maker gamma hedging and leveraged-ETF rebalancing demand; predictability REVERTS over following days.

Jin, Kearney, Li, Yang (2022 region), 'Intraday time-series momentum: global evidence and links to market characteristics', Journal of Financial Markets-class replication: pattern global, stronger where ETF/derivatives activity is higher — mechanism-consistent.
findings.effect_size_net: At index level the conditional last-half-hour edge is small per day (single-digit bps) but the app does not need to trade it directly — applied as a tilt on PM-window entry sizes and flatten timing for positions it already holds, marginal cost is zero to slightly negative (it can REMOVE late entries on adverse tapes, saving spread). Realistic contribution: a few bps/day on PM-window notional in the conditioned states (high-vol days), worth tens of bps/yr at book level; the bigger value is crash-day behavior — on big down days the mechanism says do not add in the PM window and flatten without delay, which compounds with the existing VIX ladder and SPY PM tape gate rather than duplicating them (those gate on level/direction; this adds the vol/flow-state CONDITIONING and the specific into-the-close window).
findings.decay_evidence: Mixed and must be respected: Gao et al.'s OOS tests end 2013; Baltussen et al. confirm through 2020 across 60+ futures (strong against snooping) but practitioner out-of-sample tracking of the naive SPY version shows attenuation post-publication in calm regimes — consistent with the mechanism, since the flow only exists when dealers are short gamma and vol is elevated. Treat as STATE-DEPENDENT only (apply when realized intraday range/VIX is elevated, otherwise weight ~0); do not deploy as an unconditional rule. This is also why it survives the Bajgrowicz-Scaillet critique: it is a conditional flow effect at index level, not a mined single-name rule.
findings.free_data_source: SPY 1-minute bars from Alpaca (free Basic plan; IEX real-time is sufficient for a 10:00 index-proxy snapshot, and the 15-min-delayed SIP tape is fully available by the 14:30 PM window). Compute r_AM = SPY 10:00 price / prior 16:00 close - 1 and r_day = 14:30 price / prior close - 1 in real time; condition on same-day realized range (sum of squared 5-min returns) as the gamma-state proxy — all point-in-time, zero publication lag. Optional weekly gamma context from CBOE's free daily volume/put-call files (published nightly) — not required for v1.
findings.build_sketch: Module signals/pm_tape_continuation.py extending the existing SPY PM tape gate: at each PM-window decision (14:30-15:30 hourly cadence) compute tilt = sign(r_day) x min(1, |r_day|/sigma_day) gated on realized-range percentile > 0.6; multiply PM entry sizes by (1 + 0.25 x tilt) clipped to [0.5, 1.25]; at 15:30, if tilt strongly negative, begin flatten early (15:30-15:40) instead of 15:50; overnight-sleeve entries at 15:50 inherit a positive-tape preference. Trade cadence (intraday), no model retrain. Jetson cost: a handful of arithmetic ops on minute bars — zero meaningful load.

hint: Credit-conditions sizing overlay: HY OAS widening-velocity + credit/VIX divergence (daily, the app's first credit-market

fatal_flaws: Evidence bait-and-switch: GZ-2012/LSZ-2017 validate the EBP (default-adjusted residual spread) as a quarterly/annual macro predictor; the build uses raw HY OAS 60d-velocity as a daily equity sizing trigger — an object with no published OOS support, whose nearest published kin (raw default-spread return prediction) failed Welch-Goyal. Moreira-Muir/Cederburg evidence cited for the sizing mechanism is about VOLATILITY-managed scaling, which the app already runs (GARCH per-name, EWMA book vol, VIX ladder).

Empirical OOS refutation (computed from real FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 data, 2023-06 to 2026-06, with the proposal's 1-day publication lag): 5 firings, zero leading catches. Four were 1-2-day blips landing ON exact local equity lows (2023-10-27, 2024-08-05, 2025-03-13, 2026-03-27/30) that de-risked the rebound days; the one extended firing (2025-03-28 to 05-09) reached x0.5 only after ~95% of the -19% tariff crash was complete, then held de-risked through the entire +15% V-recovery, releasing the day SPX erased its 2025 losses. Net contribution negative or wash even in its showcase episode.

Near-total redundancy with the existing stack in every claimed success: in 2022 and April 2025 the VIX>25 ladder (x0.5) and SPY<200d Faber filter (entries blocked entirely, stock_loop.py:684) were already active during the fall; macro x HMM sizing multipliers already stack multiplicatively (base_loop.py ~1178), so the overlay's only unique active windows were recovery phases (pure drag). 2011 was coincident (days, not weeks); 2014-15 meant ~8 months of de-risk drag before a -12% dip. Lifetime unique save: ~1 episode (summer 2007), which predates GZ publication and motivated the literature.

Thresholds are unvalidatable free parameters: 6.9% of days sit in the 50-75bp near-miss band so 60d/75bp/150bp choices materially change the rule; with ~5 events in 3 years and ~12-15 since 1997 (mostly coincident shocks), the system's own purged walk-forward + DSR gate has no statistical power over 3+ thresholds plus a divergence variant (2y OLS, z>=2, VIX<20) — any pass would be multiple-testing noise (McLean-Pontiff/Harvey-Liu). The divergence variant fired zero times in the 3y OOS window and rests on ~2 pre-2016 in-sample episodes.

Structural horizon mismatch: the book flattens at 15:50 with a small overnight sleeve and re-gates every entry each morning via VIX/trend/HMM/tape; Moreira-Muir-class sizing benefits are estimated on continuously-held market exposure. A 1-business-day-lagged daily credit overlay protects an intraday long-only book against almost nothing the VIX ladder doesn't already cover, and the proposed pooled-panel OAS-momentum column invites LightGBM to memorize the 2-3 widening episodes in any training window.

False premise, true by bug: 'the app's first credit-market input' is wrong by design — STLFSI2's components already include the ML HY Master II spread, Baa-10y spread, VIX and EMBI — but STLFSI2 was discontinued at observation 2022-01-07 and fetch_financial_stress() (macro_indicators.py:91) reads the last CSV line, so the app has served a frozen Jan-2022 stress value for 4+ years. Cascade-slippage avoidance on stops and queue-priority gains on TPs are exactly what the simulator omits, while the costs (3-6c deeper stop triggers, 1-3c TP give-up on trade-through) ARE simulated. The proposed nudged-vs-shadow A/B is therefore biased against the overlay by construction; 'essentially zero downside' is false in paper, and the benefit is unrealizable until live trading.

Effect-size spin: the 1-5bps saving applies only to stops landing in a ~4-5c band below $1-grid levels (~5% of stop placements, uniform mod $1; $5/$10 levels are subsets) times a ~30-40% stop rate — book-level impact ~0.02-0.1bp per trade, not 'a real fraction of net edge'. Stop-nudge geometry is uncalibrated for modern US equities: the 1-5c cascade zone and 3-6c nudge are transplanted from Osler's 1999-2000 single-dealer FX pip culture. NYSE/Nasdaq abolished exchange-side stop orders effective Feb 26, 2016 (post Aug-24-2015 cascade); stops are now broker-held and invisible, so no equity study documents penny-scale stop-cluster zones — and none can from public data. Worse, Osler 2005's own finding (trends unusually RAPID through stop zones, i.e., cascades propagate layer-to-layer) cuts against exhaustion-within-5c: a 3-6c-deeper stop often triggers later in the same cascade and fills lower. fatal_flaws: DECISION-INVARIANCE: the conformal layer is ornamental to the proposed action. Pooled CQR c_hat_t and panel-pooled ACI alpha_t add the same constant 2*c_hat_t to every symbol's interval width at time t, so the top-15% CROSS-SECTIONAL width veto (and next-decile de-rate) selects exactly the same symbols as the raw q90-q10 spread. Every coverage citation (Romano-Candes, Gibbs-Candes, Zaffran, Sabashvili, Fantazzini) supports machinery that cannot alter a single trade in the build as specified; the real proposal is 'veto wide raw LGB quantile spreads', and the 'distribution-free validity => no McLean-Pontiff decay' defense is a category error because validity is not the traded object — the width signal's profitability has no guarantee and is an ordinary snooping-exposed empirical claim.

EVIDENCE MISTRANSFER: the empirical linchpin (Sanderink, arXiv:2603.13252) does not test the proposed signal. Verified from the paper: its P85 tail cap operates on DEUP rank-displacement epistemic uncertainty (a learned error predictor); conformal appears only for coverage calibration, never as the veto signal. The headline 0.925 vs 0.375 FINAL Sharpe is Gate+Vol+Cap vs Gate+Vol over N=14 monthly observations on one walk-forward path (annualized-Sharpe SE ~ +/-1.0 at T=14 months — the '2.5x' is statistically vacuous), at 20-trading-day horizon, monthly rebalance, ~84-98 names, 10bps costs. Horizon mismatch to hourly entries with 15:50 flatten is ~2 orders of magnitude.

REDUNDANCY + MARGINAL PERVERSITY: the app already runs a self-calibrated 15th-percentile q10 tail veto built from the same val-fold quantile predictions (scripts/hypersearch_v2.py:960-975 floor; stock_loop.py:713-722 enforcement) inside a five-deep veto stack (corporate-event, sentiment, LLM, meta-label, q10), plus GARCH per-name vol sizing (width level ~ conditional vol), HMM/VIX/Hurst regime overlays, and DSR holdout + shadow/DM-HLN (which already fills the 'trailing realized efficacy trust gate' role). Conditional on surviving the existing q10 veto, the INCREMENTAL width vetoes are predominantly wide-because-q90-is-high names — i.e., vetoing upside dispersion in a long-only top-7 book, the exact strong-signal de-levering failure the proposal itself documents (rho(width,|score|)=0.616), merely discretized.

DESIGN INCOHERENCE WITH CLAIMED EFFECT: a per-hour relative P85 threshold has no absolute-width or regime dependence — it vetoes ~the same share every hour, in calm markets (all intervals narrow, trades fine) as in broken ones — so 'abstention concentrated in chop/regime breaks' cannot emerge from the rule. The state-dependent component that produced Sanderink's regime-broken rescue is the trust gate (matured-RankIC EWMA + drift z/KS + model disagreement; 47% abstention, AUROC 0.72), which the BUILD omits. And the promised verification is illusory: a 'modest Sharpe lift' on a few percent of trades is far below DM-HLN detection power over feasible shadow horizons, and the cost-negative framing only holds if vetoed top-7 slots stay unfilled rather than backfilling to rank-8 (substitution pays full costs on a weaker signal).

output.notes: Verdict: REFUTED for this system, though the underlying paper is among the most credible in the timing literature. The claim is unusually honest (episode concentration, Priestley overlap, recursive-detrend trap all pre-conceded), but it fails 3 of the 4 survival conditions. (1) Surviving evidence: partial at best - GWZ (RFS 2024) confirms statistical OOS survival but FAILS shtint on the non-overlapping homologous spec and on investable zero-leverage performance; cumulative OOS payoff is one 2008-09 episode with CI straddling zero, and the post-2021 shorting regime (record-low single-name SI, hedging migrated to futures/ETF shorts post-GameStop per Goldman) broke the informed-positioning channel - SII was bullish through the 2022 bear and blind to COVID-2020. (2) PIT plumbing: not clean - no shares-outstanding field in FINRA files (needs a full SEC-XBRL PIT denominator build), thin/nonexistent splice overlap with Ringgenberg's series ending 2021-12, and specification look-ahead in the log-linear detrend form that now extrapolates a stale 1973-2014 uptrend. (3) Long-only viability: mechanically implementable, but the 15:50-flatten book holds intraday-only beta while SII's premium is mostly overnight, so realistic capture is 0-20bps/yr - permanently below the system's own DM-HLN detection floor. (4) Non-redundancy: fails - the payoff states coincide with existing SPY-200d/VIX/HMM/tape-gate action, Priestley shows macro subsumption, and CXO documents reverse causality (price leads SI). Evidence verified via: GWZ RFS 37(11):3490 + Welch presentation PDF (verdict table p.23 and shtint performance chart p.37 rendered and read as images), CXO's two independent tests, Ringgenberg's data page (SII 1973:01-2021:12, Google Drive), Priestley SSRN 3384620, Gorbenko RAPS 2023, Goldman gspublishing crowding note (Nov 2023), FINRA equity-short-interest catalog pages. Repo integration points (macro_indicators.py, portfolio.py at /Users/kywwilson/Desktop/Projects/trader/) exist, so the BUILD section is plausible engineering-wise - the problem is the signal's marginal value, not the wiring. Adjusted confidence 2/5: real anomaly, wrong vehicle - do not build as specced; revisit only as one vote in a future slow macro ensemble with a fixed denominator, validated splice, and conditional-incrementality test vs existing gates.

findings.name: JKX image-scale distillation: rolling high-low-range-normalized OHLCV+MA features (the paper's OWN linear approximation captures 85-95% of the CNN's portfolio value)
findings.mechanism: Jiang-Kelly-Xiu's core interpretability finding is that the CNN's edge comes less from exotic patterns than from the IMAGE SCALING itself: every chart rescales prices so the window's max-high/min-low spans the image, putting all stocks on a common 'position-within-recent-range' scale. Their linear approximation isolates the dominant learned signals: (1) close at the LOW end of the recent high-low range predicts high future returns (a range-position reversal signal, ~ '½(High+Low)−Close' of the prior bar); (2) deviations of lagged prices from the in-window moving average; (3) recent volume rises predict positive returns; (4) range width (Parkinson-type volatility) gates everything (grad-CAM shows activation concentrates where the high-low range is wide). Economically this is liquidity-provision compensation plus anchoring to recent reference ranges — consistent with Kavajecz-Odders-White (RFS 2004) showing S/R levels coincide with limit-order-book depth peaks. Multi-horizon MA-gap components are independently supported: Han-Zhou-Zhu's trend factor (JFE 2016) and Avramov-Kaplanski-Subrahmanyam's moving-average distance (Rev. Fin. Econ. 2021, ~9%/yr VW alpha beyond momentum/52WH) show MA-distance vectors carry cross-sectional information not in single-window oscillators.
key_papers: Jiang, Kelly, Xiu (2023) Journal of Finance 78(6):3193-3249, '(Re-)Imag(in)ing Price Trends': Table 16 — 'Linear (image scale)' decile H-L Sharpe 1.99-2.07 EW vs full CNN 2.16-2.35 at 20-day horizon (≈90-95% of CNN); at VW the linear image-scale model often BEATS the CNN (0.66 vs 0.45-0.49). 'Linear (return scale)' collapses to 0.41-0.51 EW — the rescaling, not the architecture, is the load-bearing choice. Table 15: top regressors are lag-1 high/low/close under image scaling, then volume and MA; linear model explains 20-35% of CNN forecast variation

Jiang-Kelly-Xiu Table 13: standard characteristics (MOM, STR, WSTR, beta, vol, 52WH, bid-ask, size, illiquidity) jointly explain only McFadden R² 4.6-11.9% of CNN forecasts — the signal is largely orthogonal to a momentum/reversal stack

Han, Zhou, Zhu (2016) JFE 122:352-375 'A Trend Factor': combining MA signals across 3-1000 day horizons more than doubles Sharpe of STR/MOM/LTR factors; replicated in China (Liu-Zhou-Zhu, 'Trend Factor in China')

Avramov, Kaplanski, Subrahmanyam (2021) Review of Financial Economics 39(2):127-145 'Moving Average Distance as a Predictor of Equity Returns': 21d-vs-200d MA distance, ~9% annualized VW hedge alpha, survives momentum/52WH/profitability controls

Murray, Xia, Xiao (2024) JFE 153 'Charting by Machines': independent corroboration — NNs on price history alone strongly predict the cross-section, hold among the largest 500 stocks, stable through time, distinct from momentum/reversal/extant technical signals
findings.effect_size_net: As ranker features this is COST-NEUTRAL: the app's turnover is capped by top-7 entry/top-15 hold and fixed windows, so features change which names are picked, not trade count — the 11bps+spread RT cost is already sunk. Standalone calibration from the paper: VW H-L (closest to a 50-name liquid universe) ≈ 0.5-0.7 Sharpe gross at 20-day horizon for the linear image-scale model; long-only top-decile EW Sharpe ≈ 1.0 monthly gross in their broad universe. JKX estimate trading costs <10% of gross alpha in Russell-1000-liquidity names. Realistic in-app expectation: +0.005-0.02 cross-sectional rank IC and a modest portfolio Sharpe lift IF it survives the DSR holdout gate; apply a McLean-Pontiff-style ~50% post-publication haircut to any standalone calculation. Honest overlap note: Stoch %K(14) already in the stack IS pos-in-range at one window — the marginal value is the multi-window (5/20/60) version, the lag-1 OHLC levels under image scaling, the MA-gap normalized by range (not ATR), and volume-trend interaction.
findings.decay_evidence: Unusually strong stationarity for a technical signal: JKX trained ONCE on 1993-2000 and never retrained; performance held over a 19-year OOS window (2001-2019), and 20/60-day-image strategies retain ~1.0/0.5 Sharpe even with a one-week trading delay. Against the Sullivan-Timmermann-White universe of 7,846 technical rules, zero beat the CNN at weekly rebalance and none EW at monthly. Post-publication (2023+): too recent for a formal McLean-Pontiff decay estimate, but independent replications are positive — Lu-Wu (SSRN 4171663, China A-shares, EW Sharpe 7.6 gross), Korea (Research in International Business & Finance, 2025: CNN beats benchmarks, strongest short-horizon), commodities (Hao 2025, Journal of Futures Markets). Murray-Xia-Xiao (JFE 2024) find price-only ML predictability 'remarkably stable through time'. The WSTR-correlated component (-26% to -34% correlation) is the most crowding-prone piece; the ~88-95% orthogonal component is less so. Expect partial decay, not sign-flip — the mechanism (range anchoring, liquidity provision) is compensation, not mispricing folklore.
findings.free_data_source: Pure price/volume — zero publication lag, no revisions, point-in-time by construction (the cleanest PIT class possible). Hourly + daily OHLCV from Alpaca (already ingested; use adjustment='all' so the price path is the return-built series JKX use). Caveat: Alpaca free tier is IEX-feed volume (~2-3% of consolidated tape) — volume features must stay within-symbol-relative (ratio to own rolling max, as JKX's image scaling does), never cross-sectional raw volume; for daily-window variants, consolidated daily volume free via Stooq/yfinance if desired.
findings.build_sketch: New block in the existing feature pipeline (sits beside RSI/MACD/GKX-rank features, feeds LightGBM+LSTM ranker). For each window L ∈ {5,20,60} hourly bars AND {5,20,60} days (daily computed once at open, hourly intra-window): range_L = max(High,L) − min(Low,L); features: pos_in_range = (C−min(Low,L))/range_L; midrange_gap = (0.5·(H₁+L₁)−C₁)/range_L (their strongest distilled signal); ma_gap = (C−MA_L)/range_L; range_width = range_L/C; vol_trend = V/max(V,L) and 5-bar slope of that; for L=5 only, the full lag-1..5 O/H/L/C levels min-max scaled to window range (Table 15's regressor set). Add daily MA-gap stack at L ∈ {50,100,200} days as overlay-cadence columns (HZZ/AKS evidence). Then apply the existing GKX cross-sectional rank transform; let LightGBM form the nonlinear interactions (JKX: nonlinearity carries the remaining ~half of CNN content, and trees are the cheap nonlinearity we already own). Jetson cost: vectorized rolling ops over the 96-name panel — seconds per refresh, negligible memory. Validate through existing purged walk-forward + DSR gate; drop any column the meta-labeler shows is pure Stoch duplication.

findings.name: CNN1D-on-image-scaled-sequences challenger head (JKX Table 16's actual best performer) — the honest Jetson answer to 'can we train their CNN': skip the 64x60 2D CNN, train the 1D variant
findings.mechanism: Same economic content as Finding 1, but capturing the nonlinear half the linear distillation misses: JKX show 2D convolution over chart images acts as a bank of learned indicator functions that BIN price moves by size and combine direction, range position, volatility, and volume nonlinearly. Critically, their own ablation (Table 16) shows a 1D CNN applied to image-SCALED time series (O,H,L,C,MA,V channels normalized by rolling window max/min) performs AS WELL OR BETTER than the 2D image CNN: 'the key performance differentiator, be it for a 2D CNN, a 1D CNN, or a linear model, is using an image representation' — literally or figuratively via the scaling. So the expensive part (2D images, 708k-3M param nets) is unnecessary; the cheap part (scaling + small conv net) is sufficient. Time-scale transfer supports cross-frequency reuse: an I5/R5 model applied to 12-day-collapsed 60-day windows hit 0.90 EW Sharpe vs 0.43 for a natively trained 60-day model — patterns are approximately self-similar across sampling frequencies, so an hourly-trained model is defensible at our cadence.
key_papers: Jiang-Kelly-Xiu (2023) JF, Table 16: CNN1D (image scale) decile H-L EW Sharpe 7.20/7.88/7.85 at 5-day horizon and 2.49/2.72/2.45 at 20-day vs 2D CNN 7.15/6.75/4.89 and 2.35/2.16/1.29; CNN1D (return scale) collapses — scaling is the magic, architecture is secondary

JKX architecture facts (for the 2D option): 5d/20d/60d images = 32x15 / 64x60 / 96x180 px; 2/3/4 blocks of [5x3 conv, BN, LeakyReLU, 2x1 maxpool], filters 64-512; params 155,138 / 708,866 / 2,952,962; Adam lr 1e-5, batch 128, 50% FC dropout, early stop patience 2, ensemble of 5 random inits; trained ONCE on 1993-2000 (70/30 random split), fixed 19 years OOS
JKX Table 2: OOS directional accuracy 53.3% (20-day) vs MOM 52.1%, WSTR 51.0%; their Appendix A calibration: each +0.5% accuracy ≈ +0.1 annualized Sharpe for a timing strategy

JKX Tables 10-11 (transfer): US-trained CNN applied to 26 foreign markets beats locally trained CNNs (mean H-L Sharpe 0.7 vs 0.3 monthly) — patterns are global, supporting reuse of a model trained on a wider panel than the live 50-name book

Murray, Xia, Xiao (2024) JFE 153: independent confirmation that small NNs on raw price paths predict returns OOS in the largest 500 names with stable functional form — the approach, not the specific paper, is replicated
findings.effect_size_net: Calibrate from VW results (liquid universe): I20/R20 VW H-L 0.49 gross, I5/R5 VW 1.49-1.74 gross weekly — halve for long-only and haircut ~50% post-publication: a standalone long-only liquid-universe overlay worth maybe 0.2-0.4 Sharpe gross of integration. In-app it enters as a CHALLENGER score blended into the ranker, so again cost-neutral at the trade level (re-ranks the same top-7 picks). JKX's own cost note: <10% of gross alpha consumed in Russell-1000 liquidity; our 11bps+spread is consistent. The realistic prize: a second, ~30-50%-correlated alpha column (their I5R5-vs-I20R20 model correlation is only 32%; pairwise CNN-model correlations average <50%) that the DM-HLN shadow-promotion machinery can evaluate without portfolio risk. Compute (the honest part): 1D CNN, 6 channels x 60 bars, 2-3 conv1d blocks (~100-300k params, ~2-5 MFLOPs/sample fwd): on the Orin Nano's 6-core A78AE at a sustained ~30 GFLOPS, ~3-8 min/epoch on ~400k panel samples, x ~10-20 epochs x 5-seed ensemble = ONE OVERNIGHT JOB; quarterly walk-forward retraining is affordable. The faithful 2D 20-day model (64x60, 708k params, ~0.45 GFLOP/sample train) is ~100 min/epoch → 1-3 days per 5-seed ensemble: train-ONCE-offline is borderline acceptable (JKX never retrain, so a frozen model is methodologically faithful), recurring retraining is NOT. The 60-day 2D model (96x180, 3M params) is out of reach — don't build. 8GB memory fine throughout (uint8 memmapped windows: 1.5GB worst case; inference for 50 names is <1s/hour even for the 2D net).
findings.decay_evidence: Same evidence base as Finding 1: 19-year frozen-model OOS in the source paper; positive 2023-2025 replications in China/Korea/commodities; Murray-Xia-Xiao stability; no formal post-2023 decay study yet (signal published Dec 2020 SSRN / 2023 JF). Known fragility to respect: predictive strength concentrates in the first week after formation (Fig 10) and decays with delay — at hourly decision cadence we capture it faster than the paper's monthly tests, which helps; conversely EW results lean on small caps we don't trade, so anchor expectations to VW columns only.
findings.free_data_source: Alpaca hourly OHLCV for the 96-name training panel (point-in-time, no lag, no revisions); optional daily-bar pretraining panel from Stooq/yfinance free daily files (consolidated volume; note free daily panels lack delisted names — acknowledge survivorship in the training set or restrict claims to ranking the surviving liquid universe, which is the live task anyway). Full JKX paper PDF already saved locally for implementation reference: /Users/kywwilson/.claude/projects/-Users-kywwilson-Desktop-Projects-trader/46328304-7c7f-44b5-b161-af764182b7e5/tool-results/webfetch-1781231679593-y6xdfu.pdf
findings.build_sketch: New challenger model module: (1) dataset builder emits per-(symbol,hour) tensors 6x60 [O,H,L,C,MA60,V], each window min-max scaled by its own high-low range (prices) and max volume (volume) — exactly the JKX image scaling without rasterization; triple-barrier labels reused as-is (binary up/down on the matched horizon); (2) PyTorch CPU 1D CNN: conv1d(6→64,k=5)-BN-LeakyReLU-maxpool2 x3 (64/128/128), FC-dropout0.5-softmax; Adam 1e-5, batch 128, early-stop patience 2, 5-seed ensemble averaged; purged walk-forward splits matching the existing CV; (3) output P(up) becomes (a) a feature column for LightGBM and (b) a standalone challenger score routed through the existing shadow-mode DM-HLN promotion gate. Train quarterly overnight (nice-level the job so live loops are unaffected); freeze if retraining ever contends with the 8GB budget — JKX's frozen-model result licenses that. Defer the 2D 5-day (32x15, 155k param, overnight-feasible) model to a later curiosity experiment; never build the 60-day 2D model.

findings.name: Round-number and reference-level microstructure: distance-to-round-number features (hourly) + Osler-aware stop/take-profit placement on the exit stack
findings.mechanism: The only S/R concepts with hard microstructure evidence are ORDER-CLUSTERING levels, not drawn trendlines. Osler (JF 2003), using a major FX dealer's actual order book, showed take-profit orders cluster AT round numbers and stop-loss orders cluster just BEYOND them — mechanically generating the two classic TA predictions: reversals as price approaches a round level (TP cluster absorbs the move) and accelerated trends once it crosses (stop cascades; Osler JIMF 2005 documents abnormally rapid trends at documented stop-cluster levels). In US equities, Bhattacharya-Holden-Jacobsen (Mgmt Sci 2012), on 100M+ transactions, found excess liquidity-demander buying one penny below round numbers and selling one penny above, monotone in roundness (integers > half-dollars > dimes...), with conditional 24-hour drift (e.g., 'ask falls below integer' events: −7bps/24h, p<0.0001). Kavajecz-Odders-White (RFS 2004) close the loop: technical S/R levels coincide with DEPTH PEAKS on the limit order book — S/R 'works' insofar as it locates resting liquidity. Prior-day high/low and opening-range levels are the same mechanism (visible reference points where conditional orders cluster) but with only practitioner-grade direct evidence — treat as low-prior candidate features, not truths.
key_papers: Osler (2003) Journal of Finance 58(5):1791-1819 'Currency Orders and Exchange Rate Dynamics': TP orders cluster at rates ending in 00/50; SL orders just beyond; explains S/R bounces and breakout acceleration from actual dealer order data

Osler (2005) Journal of International Money & Finance 24(2):219-241 'Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades': trends are unusually rapid when price reaches stop-cluster zones — the cost of resting stops parked exactly where everyone else's are

Bhattacharya, Holden, Jacobsen (2012) Management Science 58(2):413-431 'Penny Wise, Dollar Foolish': buy-sell imbalance flips around round numbers, monotone in roundness; conditional 24h returns ~−7bps on round-number-adjacent quote events

Kavajecz, Odders-White (2004) Review of Financial Studies 17(4):1043-1071 'Technical Analysis and Liquidity Provision': S/R levels coincide with limit-order-book depth peaks; MA crossings relate to depth skewness — TA as liquidity map

Counter-evidence guardrail: Zarattini-Barbon-Aziz (SSRN 4729284, 2024) claim 5-min opening-range-breakout on high-relative-volume 'stocks in play' earns Sharpe ~2.4-2.8 net (2016-2023) — NOT peer-reviewed, short sample, timeframe selected in-sample; and the rule-based breakout literature is killed by Sullivan-Timmermann-White (JF 1999) and Bajgrowicz-Scaillet (JFE 2012, 106:473-491): none of 7,846 technical rules survive FDR control + costs. So: levels as FEATURES and EXECUTION HYGIENE yes; breakout RULES no
findings.effect_size_net: Small and honest: bps-scale, but two cheap channels. (a) Feature channel (hourly): signed ATR-scaled distance to nearest $1/$5/$10 level, approach direction, and 'crossed level this bar x relative volume' interaction — conditional drift in the literature is ~5-10bps/day-scale, which at our 11bps+spread RT only matters as a RANKER input (re-picks names; adds no trades) and as entry-timing tiebreak within the 9:45-11:00 window; expect tiny-but-free IC addition, gated by the meta-labeler. (b) Execution overlay (every order): never park the resting ATR stop 1-5 cents past a round number (the Osler cascade zone) — nudge below-the-level stops a few cents further; place TP limits 1-3 cents IN FRONT of round numbers (sell into the TP-cluster bid wall rather than join it). Saves an estimated 1-5bps slippage on the subset of stopped/TP'd trades — at an 11bps cost base that is a real fraction of net edge, with essentially zero downside risk. Same logic applies to the crypto exit stack (round-number clustering in BTC/ETH is heavily documented in microstructure work).
findings.decay_evidence: Clustering is a cognitive constant, not an anomaly that arbitrages away: price clustering documented continuously from Harris (RFS 1991) through decimalization (BHJ 2012 post-decimalization TAQ) to present-day L2 data; Osler's FX order-clustering replicated across dealers/periods. The RETURN effect attached to it is small and was never a published 'factor', so crowding decay is minimal — but for the same reason, never expect it to scale beyond bps. The decayed/dead branch of this literature is hard breakout RULES (STW 1999, Bajgrowicz-Scaillet 2012: dead net of costs post-1990s) — explicitly not what we build. Prior-day-high/low and opening-range levels: no rigorous peer-reviewed equity evidence either way; ship behind the ranker and let walk-forward kill them if empty.
findings.free_data_source: None needed beyond live prices (Alpaca bars + the order book we already trade against) — zero publication lag, fully point-in-time, no revision risk. Round-number grid is deterministic; PDH/PDL/opening range computed from own bars.
findings.build_sketch: Two small modules. (1) Exit-stack overlay in the order-placement path: function snap_levels(symbol, side, stop_px, tp_px) → if stop within [level−5c, level−1c] below a $1/$5/$10 level (long position), move it 3-6c lower (outside the cascade zone, still inside ATR risk budget — re-check risk-based size after nudge); if TP within 1-3c above a round level, pull it to level−1c. Pure arithmetic, runs per order, zero Jetson cost; log nudges for A/B slippage measurement vs un-nudged shadow. (2) Feature channel: dist_round = (C − nearest_level)/ATR for the $1/$5/$10 grids, plus pdh_dist/pdl_dist/open_range_pos analogues at hourly cadence; one-hot 'crossed level last bar' x relative-volume rank interaction; feed ranker, fully subject to existing meta-label veto and DSR gating. Negligible compute/memory.

findings.name: VERDICT — Lo-Mamaysky-Wang kernel-regression pattern detector: do NOT build it. Informativeness-only in-sample, failed post-1995 replication, fragile to bandwidth, and superseded by Findings 1-2
findings.mechanism: LMW (JF 2000) smoothed daily prices with a Gaussian kernel (bandwidth hand-set at 0.3x the cross-validated optimum, 'by eye'), defined 10 patterns (H&S, inverse H&S, broadening/triangle/rectangle tops & bottoms, double tops/bottoms) as sequences of local extrema, and tested whether one-day returns CONDITIONED on pattern completion differ in distribution from unconditional returns (Kolmogorov-Smirnov / goodness-of-fit). They found significant distributional differences for several patterns (strongest on Nasdaq), i.e., patterns carry SOME information — they explicitly did not claim profitability. The economic mechanism was never established; Jegadeesh's published JF discussion (same issue) made the core critique: distributional 'informativeness' with no demonstrated mean-return or economic significance, sensitive to arbitrary smoothing choices, and not benchmarked against simpler conditioning variables. 25 years on, that critique won.
key_papers: Lo, Mamaysky, Wang (2000) Journal of Finance 55(4):1705-1765: original result — conditional ≠ unconditional return distributions for several of 10 patterns, 1962-1996 CRSP; informativeness, NOT profitability (their own framing); volume conditioning added marginal information
Jegadeesh (2000) Journal of Finance 55(4):1765-1770 (discussion): differences are economically trivial; no profitability evidence; pattern definitions/bandwidth ad hoc

Nekrasov (2010) replication report (letyourmoneygrow.com/yetanotherquant): re-ran the full LMW pipeline 1995-2010 on DJ30/SP100-500/NASDAQ100 and 10 DAX names — KS tests INSIGNIFICANT for ~9-10 of 10 patterns at both optimal and 0.3x-optimal bandwidth (lone exceptions: RTOP p≈0.013 on DJ30; BTOP p≈0.049 on NASDAQ100); distributional differences live in the TAILS (rare events), KS results flip with smoother implementation (npreg vs ksmooth disagree at identical bandwidth/kernel) and with LMW's own return normalization (18 of 30 cases lose significance after normalizing); 1962-1997 DJ30 partially replicates (3 patterns significant) → consistent with 'informative pre-Internet, exhausted after ~1995'

Dawson, Steeley (2003) Journal of Business Finance & Accounting 'On the Existence of Visual Technical Patterns in the UK Stock Market': UK corroboration that conditional distributions differ, but their profitability extension finds pattern-conditioned returns do NOT beat the market benchmark

Savin, Weller, Zvingelis (2007) Journal of Financial Econometrics 5(2):243-265: the lone survivor — a modified H&S detector on S&P500/Russell2000 1990-1999 predicts risk-adjusted excess returns of 5-7%/yr at 1-3 month horizons, yet 'little or no support for a stand-alone trading strategy'; pre-2000 sample, never re-validated at scale since

Jiang-Kelly-Xiu (2023) JF Fig. 11: the supersession argument — against 7,846 classic technical rules (the STW universe, code from Scaillet), ZERO beat the image-CNN at weekly horizon, none EW at monthly: learned range/trend/volume features dominate the hand-drawn pattern zoo
findings.effect_size_net: Approximately zero net at this app's cadence and scale, with real implementation cost avoided. Pattern frequency is the killer even before decay: LMW-parameterized detectors fire ~0.3-0.9 completions/year/stock for most patterns (Nekrasov Table 5 vs LMW Table II) — on a 50-name book that's a handful of events per month, far too sparse to train the hourly ranker or move a triple-barrier label distribution, and exactly the 'below label noise' regime the wave-3 red team killed seasonality features for. The one effect with replicated point estimates (SWZ H&S, 5-7%/yr risk-adjusted, monthly horizons, 1990s data) is overlay-cadence at best, stale by 25 years, and its information content (post-peak reversal of an extended range) is spanned by Finding 1's pos_in_range/midrange_gap features that fire every bar instead of 3x/year. A numba kernel smoother would be cheap to RUN (O(window²) per bar, trivial on Jetson) — the cost is engineering time, 10 new hyperparameters (bandwidth x pattern tolerances), and multiple-testing burn on the DSR budget for a signal class with a failed modern replication.
findings.decay_evidence: Decay IS the finding: significant on 1962-1996 (original) and partially on 1962-1997 (independent re-run), insignificant on 1995-2010 across US indices and DAX names at any bandwidth tried; UK evidence (2003) already showed no benchmark-beating returns. No post-2010 peer-reviewed rehabilitation found; the modern literature (JKX 2023, Murray-Xia-Xiao 2024) moved to learned representations precisely because hand-specified pattern templates stopped paying. McLean-Pontiff doesn't even track it — it never had a tradable published premium to decay.
findings.free_data_source: n/a — recommendation is to skip the build. (If ever revisited for research curiosity: daily bars from Alpaca/Stooq suffice; everything is price-derived, PIT-clean, zero lag.)
findings.build_sketch: Build nothing now. Capture the residual value two ways already in flight: (1) Finding 1's image-scaled OHLC features span the pattern zoo's payoff-relevant content (range position, post-extreme reversion, MA deviation, volume confirmation) at every bar; (2) Finding 2's CNN challenger is the literature's own successor to LMW — JKX explicitly frame their CNN as 'a continuation of the agenda set forth by Lo et al. (2000)'. If a cheap insurance trigger is wanted: a 20-line numba double-top/H&S flag (rolling argrelextrema on 60-bar windows, SWZ tolerances) added as ONE binary ranker feature, accepted only if it survives the meta-label veto and adds DSR — budget half a day, expect it to die in validation.

hint: Multi-horizon moving-average distance features (Han-Zhou-Zhu trend factor), fed to the learner instead of used as rules

surviving_caveats: EFFECT SIZE DOWNGRADE (strongest attack): HZZ's premium is a monthly close-to-close return whose accrual channel is largely overnight — Lou-Polk-Skouras (JFE 2019) shows momentum/reversal-class profits are earned ENTIRELY overnight with opposite-signed intraday alpha. A 9:45-15:50 flat-at-close long book cannot harvest that premium directly. Budget 0-15bps/mo as intraday conditioning state, not the claimed 10-30bps; material probability the learner assigns ~0 importance. The proposal survives only because its cost is genuinely ~zero and the CV/DSR/shadow stack is the arbiter.

MECHANISM-LIQUIDITY MISMATCH: HZZ's information-asymmetry mechanism is strongest in small/illiquid/high-uncertainty names; a top-60-dollar-volume universe sits in the weakest cell of their own cross-tabs. The VW/large-cap half-magnitude results are the relevant prior BEFORE the McLean-Pontiff haircut, not after.

REPLICATION INDEPENDENCE OVERSTATED: commodities-2022 and China-2024 replications share Guofu Zhou as common author (self-replication, not McLean-Pontiff-grade independent evidence). The only independent corroboration (Avramov-Kaplanski-Subrahmanyam MAD) is second-tier-journal and anchoring-adjacent — though it subsumes the killed 52-week-high feature rather than being subsumed, which is the right direction.

HARD IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENT (verified empirically): do NOT compute these inside compute_stock_features from the live 30-day window. fatal_flaws: HORIZON/EVIDENCE SEVERANCE: every cited JKX result (Tables 2/3/4/16, Fig 10, transfer tables) is daily-bar images with 5/20/60 TRADING-DAY supervision and weekly-to-quarterly rebalanced decile spreads on thousands of CRSP names. The time-scale-transfer defense (Table 9: 0.90 EW transfer vs 0.43 baseline) runs daily->LOWER frequency (1:12 collapse) and drops to 0.3 in the value-weighted panel; JKX contain zero evidence below daily frequency, where intraday U-shaped volume/vol seasonality systematically distorts the window max-volume V-channel scaling and overnight gaps puncture 60-hour windows.

REDUNDANCY BY THE PAPER'S OWN DECOMPOSITION: JKX pp.45-47 show the CNN signal's linear core is ~ 0.5*(High+Low)-Close — closing position in the recent high-low range plus rising volume. That is economically the inverse of Stochastic %K, which already exists verbatim in the stack (indicators.py:402, stoch_k = 100*(C-LL)/(HH-LL)), alongside bb_pct/%B and OBV — all fed to LightGBM, whose trees ARE a learned bank of axis-aligned indicator functions (the exact 'learned binning' mechanism the proposal credits to the CNN); a RegressionLSTM (model_v2.py) already does nonlinear sequence modeling on the SAME labels. JKX's nonlinear increment over the linear-image core is only ~0.4-0.6pp of logistic R^2 on a microcap-inclusive panel. The promised '~30-50%-correlated alpha column' is lifted from correlations BETWEEN JKX CNN variants at different horizons (I5R5-vs-I20R20 = 32%), not CNN-vs-champion trained on the same panel/labels/information set — expect 0.6-0.8 realized prediction correlation, gutting both the diversification math and the DM-HLN promotion odds.

EFFECT-SIZE CALIBRATION INFLATED AND PARTLY UNSOURCED: the 0.2-0.4 standalone figure leans on I5/R5 VW 1.49-1.74 — a weekly construct with ~175-190% monthly-equivalent turnover (Tables 3-4), i.e., the STR turnover class JKX themselves benchmark as conventionally NOT surviving trading costs. LIQUID-UNIVERSE EVIDENCE CUTS THE WRONG WAY: the international transfer '0.7 vs 0.3' is the EW cross-country average dominated by small markets; the value-weighted Global aggregate is NEGATIVE for the US-trained model (transfer -0.25 vs re-train +0.64, Table 10). A 2026 Finance Research Letters study (From vision to value) finds the CNN-image factor 'exhibits weaker performance, particularly for large-cap stocks.' Positive replications are non-US (Korea RIBAF 2025, China, commodities), where TA anomalies are systematically stronger. surviving_caveats: Point-in-time plumbing is genuinely clean: window-local min-max scaling, Alpaca hourly OHLCV, no publication lag, triple-barrier labels reused. Two residual data caveats: (a) IEX-vs-SIP volume consistency between historical training feed and live feed — the max-volume window scaler is sensitive to single-bar spikes that differ across feeds; (b) survivorship in the optional Stooq/yfinance daily pretraining panel (acknowledged by the proposer; acceptable if claims are restricted to ranking the surviving liquid universe).

Jetson compute honesty largely holds for the 1D variant: independent math (~130-300k params, ~5 MFLOP fwd/sample, 6-9 TFLOP/epoch incl. backward) gives 3-20 min/epoch at realistic 10-30 GFLOPS sustained ARM PyTorch — '5-seed ensemble in one overnight' is optimistic by 2-3x (could be a weekend job), but quarterly cadence absorbs it; memory fits 8GB with uint8 memmapped windows; must be scheduled around the existing weekly champion retrain window (predict_now.py comment confirms core contention is a real concern). The cheap, defensible residue of this idea is an EXPERIMENT, not the claim: route CNN P(up) as ONE additional LightGBM feature column first (cost-neutral, gated by existing purged CV), shadow-log realized prediction correlation vs the champion, and pre-register a kill rule (e.g., drop if corr > 0.7 with champion score and DM-HLN insignificant after 2 quarters). Multiple-testing debt: every wave challenger run through the DM-HLN gate consumes family-wise error budget (the Sullivan-Timmermann-White point reborn at the system level); apply a family-wise correction across all wave-3/4 challengers or the promotion gate itself becomes the data-snooping device.

JKX Fig 10 (fast Sharpe decay with trading delay) and the frozen-1993-2000-model 19-year OOS are real and impressive AT DAILY FREQUENCY — they license freezing a trained model rather than fighting the 8GB budget, but they do not license assuming the pattern library survives translation to hourly bars; if built, that translation is the hypothesis under test, with no prior evidence either way.

DIVERGENCE 'FLOOR' BRANCH FLOORS DE-RISKING AT CRASH ONSETS: because the 1y-trailing z reads credit as 'calm' whenever spreads have already been wide for a year or the crash is <21d old, the buyable-vol-spike branch (VIX>25 & credit_z>-0.5) fires on Sep 9 and Sep 12, 2008 (credit_z +0.11/+0.23 — the last trading day before Lehman filed) and Feb 26, 2020 (COVID onset), with forward-21d high-beta returns of -27.0%, -21.1%, -29.8%; it was also active 43 days during the 2022 bear via leg-2 rates contamination. Relative (trailing-1y z) and absolute (GZ/EBP level) credit stress are different objects; the spec implements the wrong one.

THE 'DURATION HEDGE' IS NOT A HEDGE: the spec claims rolling 63d HYG~IEF beta '~0.35-0.45' (the duration ratio); the actual empirical regression beta is mean -0.14, sd 0.50, NEGATIVE on 60% of days (flight-to-quality correlation dominates), so leg 1 frequently ADDS Treasury exposure instead of hedging duration. Leg 2 (log HYG/LQD) is duration-mismatched (~4y vs ~8.5y): in the 2022 rates-led bear it read risk-ON (z2>+0.5) on 45% of days. The proposer's stated beta range shows the construction was never computed on data.

NON-REDUNDANT SIGNAL CONTENT IS BULL-MARKET NOISE: of 602 flag days, 54% are already covered by existing VIX>25/SPY-200d gates; the 278 marginal credit-only days cluster in calm bull years (59 in 2014, 23 in 2013, 22 in 2017, 25 in 2019, 18 in 2021, 22 in 2024) and carry ABOVE-average forward returns (+14.3% ann, Sharpe 0.79) — cutting gross 30% there is pure performance drag. Meanwhile corr(credit_z, trailing 21d SPY return) = 0.64: the ETF-price proxy is substantially the equity tape the system already encodes via trend filter/HMM, and its distinctness from VIX (corr -0.51) is mostly trailing equity momentum, not independent credit information.
surviving_caveats: Data-source diligence was honest and correct: FRED's April 2026 truncation of ALL ICE BofA series (incl. BAMLH0A0HYM2) to a rolling 3-year window is verified true, so an ETF-bar-computed signal genuinely is the only fully PIT-reconstructable free option for 2007+ training; the Alpaca adjustment=all / yfinance distribution-aware backfill plumbing is clean and reusable for any future credit work.

The cited literature is real and undecayed AT ITS OWN HORIZON: GZ 2012 EBP remains a Fed-maintained monthly recession indicator with replicated quarterly-to-annual predictive power, and the HPW (equity leads credit at firm level) honesty constraint was correctly applied. The failure is horizon/operationalization transfer — none of that evidence supports a 21d-change, 1y-z, daily ETF-price proxy.

One redesign direction showed genuine state information and could be re-proposed separately: LEVEL-based 3y z of log(HYG/LQD) < -1.5 flags a real worse-risk state (flagged fwd-21d Sharpe 0.27, p5 -21.5% vs unflagged 0.60, p5 -9.5%) — but conditional mean is still +12.8% ann (not negative), the 410 flag days concentrate in GFC/2011/2020 where VIX/trend/GARCH-EWMA already de-risk, and any revival must be absolute-level based, de-risk-only (no vol-spike floor branch), promoted on drawdown/Calmar with the honesty that there are only ~4-5 independent stress episodes in the data.
Cost, long-only, and Jetson claims are all valid (sizing-only overlay, ~zero incremental turnover, nil compute) — the proposal fails on signal content, not feasibility.
output.notes: Adjudicated by direct replication, not literature debate: I implemented the BUILD spec exactly as written (rolling 63d HYG~IEF beta hedge, 21d d-log(HYG/LQD), trailing-1y z-scores, min-of-legs composite, -1.5/-2.5 tiers, VIX>25 & z>-0.5 floor branch) on dividend-adjusted yfinance closes 2007-04..2026-06 (4,822 days), plus 6 robustness variants (63d aggregation, fixed 0.45 duration beta, 3y level z, drawdown state, PIT expanding quantiles, existing VIX/trend benchmark). Audit scripts: /tmp/credit_referee.py and /tmp/credit_referee2.py (reproducible). Codebase context confirmed at /Users/kywwilson/Desktop/Projects/trader/macro_indicators.py: the existing get_macro_regime() already stacks VIX ladder (15/25/35 to 0.8/0.5/0.3x) + weekly STLFSI2>1.0 (which itself contains the ML HY spread and VIX as components) + CAPE, alongside the SPY 200d filter — so the redundancy bar was high and the proposed signal's marginal days turned out to be bull-market noise. Key dates for the parent agent to spot-check: 2008-09-12 floor-branch fire (credit_z +0.23, day before Lehman, fwd21 -21%), 2024-08-05 credit_z -3.12 (contradicts the claim's own 'credit barely moved' narrative), 2022 leg-2 risk-on misreads 45% of days. The mechanism literature (GZ EBP, LSZ credit sentiment) survives at quarterly horizons and a level-based monthly redesign (variant C) is the only salvageable thread — it should be treated as a NEW proposal subject to the same referee process, with the divergence-floor branch permanently dead (wave-3 lesson confirmed: single-indicator override logic fails at crash onsets).
