findings.name: Credit-conditions sizing overlay: HY OAS widening-velocity + credit/VIX divergence (daily, the app's first credit-market input)
findings.mechanism: Corporate credit spreads embed the risk-bearing capacity of levered intermediaries, not just expected default. Gilchrist-Zakrajsek show that the non-default component of spreads (EBP) contracts credit supply and drags down activity AND equity prices; Lopez-Salido/Stein/Zakrajsek show aggressively-priced credit predictably mean-reverts, with spread widening leading real downturns by 1-2 years. At shorter horizons the exploitable object is NOT level (correlates ~0.8 with VIX, which the app already ladders) but (a) widening VELOCITY off the trailing low — credit-cycle downturns (2007: HY OAS troughed at ~240bp in June, +200bp by the October SPX peak; 2014-15 energy: HY widened ~12 months before the Aug-2015/Jan-2016 equity breaks) — and (b) DIVERGENCE: OAS widening while VIX stays low means credit is pricing stress equities haven't, historically preceding major drawdowns. Critically, Norden-Weber show stocks lead credit at daily/weekly frequency firm-by-firm — so this must be built as a weekly-scale risk-appetite regime overlay (where credit's slower intermediary-balance-sheet information dominates), never as an hourly trade signal.
key_papers: Gilchrist & Zakrajsek (2012), American Economic Review 102(4):1692-1720, 'Credit Spreads and Business Cycle Fluctuations' — GZ-spread innovations orthogonal to the macro state lead to significant, persistent declines in economic activity and equity prices; the spread's forecasting power for downturns is attributable to the excess-bond-premium component, not expected defaults

Lopez-Salido, Stein & Zakrajsek (2017), Quarterly Journal of Economics 132(3):1373-1426, 'Credit-Market Sentiment and the Business Cycle' — elevated credit sentiment (tight spreads) in year t-2 predicts spread widening and a cumulative ~4.2pp drag on real GDP per capita over t/t+1; 1929-2015 sample; mechanism is predictable mean reversion in credit pricing

Norden & Weber (2009), European Financial Management 15(3), 'The Co-movement of CDS, Bond and Stock Markets' — stock returns LEAD CDS/bond spread changes at daily-weekly frequency (confirmed by later price-discovery literature); disqualifies hourly use, mandates weekly-scale overlay design

Moreira & Muir (2017), Journal of Finance 72(4), 'Volatility-Managed Portfolios' (general sizing-overlay mechanism: scaling exposure down in stress raises Sharpe ~20-25% for the market factor) — tempered by Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang & Yan (2020), JFE 138(1), who show real-time implementable versions survive for the MARKET factor but degrade for most others; supports using this as broad gross-exposure sizing, not per-name alpha
findings.effect_size_net: As a gross-exposure sizing overlay on a long-only ~$100k book: expected benefit is drawdown/vol reduction, not entry alpha. Historical pattern: a 'HY OAS >= +75-100bp above its trailing 60d low' de-risk trigger would have cut exposure ahead of or early in 2007-08, 2011, 2015-16, and during 2022, while staying ~fully invested >85% of days. Moreira-Muir-class market-factor scaling gains are ~20-25% Sharpe gross; realistically expect a few points of max-drawdown reduction and slightly smoother equity at the cost of ~1-3% CAGR drag in straight-up years. Added turnover is tiny: the multiplier changes state a handful of times/year, position deltas execute at the next scheduled rebalance, so incremental cost at 11bps+spread is roughly $50-250/yr at $100k — negligible vs. the tail protection. Coincident (not leading) in shock-driven crashes (2018Q4, COVID, 2025 tariff episode), so it complements rather than replaces the VIX ladder.
findings.decay_evidence: Not a published 'anomaly' that can be arbitraged away — it is a risk-management mapping of one of the most-replicated macro-finance results (GZ 2012 has thousands of citations; the EBP remains the Fed's preferred recession-risk input per Favara et al. 2016). The classic Baa-Aaa 'default spread' as a RETURN predictor failed Welch-Goyal (2008, RFS) out-of-sample tests — which is why this is framed as drawdown-state sizing, not expected-return forecasting. Post-2012 out-of-sample: HY OAS velocity flagged 2015-16 and 2022 correctly, was coincident-only in Feb-2018/Q4-2018/Mar-2020. Divergence variant: low-VIX-plus-widening-credit fired usefully mid-2007 and mid-2015; rare (<5% of days) by construction.
findings.free_data_source: FRED series BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS, daily, history to 1996) via the same fredgraph.csv endpoint macro_indicators.py already uses for VIXCLS/STLFSI2: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=BAMLH0A0HYM2. Publication lag: previous business day's close posted next morning (~1 business day). Point-in-time: ICE index closes are final when published — the series is effectively unrevised, so the FRED history IS the real-time history (verify once against ALFRED vintages); just lag all signals by 1 business day in backtests. Optional companion: BAMLC0A0CM (IG OAS) for an HY-IG quality spread at zero extra cost.
findings.build_sketch: macro_indicators.py: add fetch_hy_oas() (cached daily, mirroring fetch_financial_stress()); compute three scalars at the daily overlay refresh: (1) oas_vel = OAS - min(OAS, 60d) in bp; (2) oas_mom20 = 20d change; (3) divergence z = z(OAS residual from a 2y rolling OLS of OAS on VIX). Map in get_macro_regime(): oas_vel >= 75bp -> sizing_mult x0.75; >= 150bp -> x0.5; divergence z >= 2 with VIX < 20 -> x0.75 and overnight sleeve off. Also expose the daily OAS 20d change as one slow feature column in the stock panel (daily value forward-filled to hourly rows, 1-day lagged). Cadence: one CSV fetch/day at ~9:00 ET; Jetson cost: one HTTP GET + a few pandas ops, microseconds of compute, zero model footprint. Thresholds must be set/validated on the existing purged walk-forward + DSR harness, not hand-tuned.

findings.name: Regime-conditional jobless-claims momentum: fastest free labor signal, with the Boyd-Hu-Jagannathan sign flip built in
findings.mechanism: Initial claims are the highest-frequency official labor datum (weekly, 5-day lag) and historically deteriorate before recessionary equity bear markets (claims troughed in early 2006, ~18 months before the Oct-2007 SPX peak; turned decisively in 2000-01). The critical design input is Boyd-Hu-Jagannathan (JF 2005): the equity response to labor-market bad news is STATE-DEPENDENT — in expansions, rising unemployment is on average GOOD for stocks (discount-rate channel dominates: lower expected policy rates), while in contractions it is BAD (cash-flow channel dominates). A naive 'claims rising -> de-risk' rule is therefore mis-specified and would have fought the tape through 2024-25 'bad news is good news' regimes. Correct mapping: claims deterioration acts as a risk-off multiplier ONLY when the app's existing HMM regime/SPY-trend layer is already in its weak state — i.e., it sharpens the existing regime classifier with orthogonal (labor) information rather than acting alone.
key_papers: Boyd, Hu & Jagannathan (2005), Journal of Finance 60(2):649-672, 'The Stock Market's Reaction to Unemployment News: Why Bad News Is Usually Good for Stocks' — robust sign flip of equity response to unemployment surprises across expansion vs. contraction states, 1957-2000; announcement-day effects of tens of bps; the canonical citation for state-conditioning any labor signal

Sahm (2019), 'Direct Stimulus Payments to Individuals' (Brookings/Hamilton Project) — the Sahm-rule template: small absolute deteriorations from the trailing low in labor data reliably mark recession starts in real time (0.50pp unemployment-rate version: zero false positives 1970-2019 in real time)

Barnichon & Nekarda (2012), Brookings Papers on Economic Activity, 'The Ins and Outs of Forecasting Unemployment' — claims-based flow models beat SPF consensus unemployment forecasts, establishing claims as the fastest-information labor series

Cautionary post-publication: the unemployment-rate Sahm rule fired in Aug-2024 with NO ensuing recession (acknowledged by Sahm herself) — immigration-driven labor-supply shifts distorted thresholds; claims-based variants stayed borderline. Any fixed threshold must be re-validated, not imported
findings.effect_size_net: Composite trigger (4-week avg of NSA claims up >= ~12-15% YoY AND HMM in weak state) fires early in 1990-91, 2001, 2008, 2020 episodes and is silent in 1995-99, 2013-19, and (borderline) 2024-25. Expected contribution at app scale: shaves entries/overnight exposure during the handful of genuinely recessionary windows — historically the deepest drawdown environments for a high-beta long-only book (avg recessionary SPX drawdown ~30%+ vs ~12% non-recessionary per standard drawdown catalogs; high-beta universe amplifies ~1.3-1.6x). Cost side: triggers <5-8% of weeks; forgone-entry cost in false-positive windows (e.g., parts of 2024) is the main risk — bounded by applying it as a 0.5-0.75x sizing multiplier plus overnight-sleeve shutoff rather than a full entry ban. Direct transaction-cost impact ~zero (it only scales already-planned trades).
findings.decay_evidence: Announcement-day claims-surprise effects are heavily studied and arbitraged at the minutes horizon (not our use). The slow regime content has no crowding-decay mechanism — it is macro state, not cross-sectional alpha. McLean-Pontiff-style post-publication decay doesn't apply; the relevant failure mode is structural (2024 Sahm false positive from labor-supply shifts; COVID-era seasonal-factor chaos made SA claims unreliable 2020-22 — another reason to use NSA YoY). BHJ's sign flip replicated in follow-ups (e.g., Boyd-Liu-Jagannathan on stock-bond correlation state-dependence) and in the 2022-25 'bad news is good news' regime, which is exactly what the conditional design exploits.
findings.free_data_source: FRED ICNSA (initial claims, NOT seasonally adjusted, weekly) — DOL/ETA release every Thursday 8:30 ET for the week ending the prior Saturday (5-day lag). Point-in-time: use ICNSA YoY (same-week-of-year comparison) — raw counts get only one tiny prior-week revision, whereas ICSA's seasonal factors are re-estimated annually (most recently the 2026-03-19 release revised 2021-forward), making SA history NOT point-in-time stable. ALFRED carries ICSA/ICNSA vintages (https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/series?seid=ICSA) for honest backtests: realtime_start=realtime_end=as-of-date via the free FRED API key.
findings.build_sketch: macro_indicators.py: fetch_claims() pulling ICNSA Thursday ~9:00 ET; compute claims_yoy = 4wk_avg / same-4wk_avg_prior_year - 1. regime_detector.py: add labor_deterioration flag (claims_yoy >= threshold, threshold fit on purged WF); apply ONLY when HMM regime is bearish/weak: sizing_mult x0.6 and overnight sleeve disabled; in HMM-bull state the flag is logged but inert (BHJ sign flip). Backtest via ALFRED vintage pulls (one-time download of vintage matrix, ~MBs). Cadence: weekly fetch + one comparison; Jetson cost: nil. Also dodges the macro_calendar stand-down overlap: claims release is 8:30 ET, before the 9:45 entry window, so no intraday plumbing needed.

findings.name: Funding-stress stand-down gate from money-market plumbing (SOFR-IORB / SOFR99 dispersion, reserves context) — the rigorous salvage of the 'net liquidity' folklore
findings.mechanism: Two separate claims must be split. (1) The trader thesis that the LEVEL of 'net liquidity' (WALCL - TGA - RRP) drives/leads SPX is data-mined folklore: the 2020-22 fit (level correlation 0.81-0.95) is two trending series; from Sep-2022 to Mar-2026, QT removed ~$2.14T while RRP drained ~$2.37T — net liquidity went sideways and SPX rose ~78%. No peer-reviewed cointegration/Granger evidence exists; rigorous QE literature (Krishnamurthy & Vissing-Jorgensen 2011 BPEA) supports announcement/stock effects of policy, not weekly flow-tracking of plumbing aggregates. Do NOT build a net-liquidity feature or gate. (2) The defensible kernel is reserve SCARCITY: Copeland-Duffie-Yang (QJE 2025) show that as reserves at the largest repo-active banks decline, repo rates distort and spike nonlinearly (Sep-17-2019: SOFR printed 5.25% vs IORB 1.80%, 99th-percentile repo ~9%), with stress propagating through delayed intraday payments. Funding-stress events coincide with sharp equity-vol regime breaks (Sep-2019, Mar-2020, quarter-end squeezes during QT endgames, the late-2025 repo tightness that pushed the Fed to end QT). A daily spread-based stress gate captures a tail state the app's VIX ladder only sees AFTER equities react — repo prints at 8:00 ET reflect yesterday's funding before today's equity open.
key_papers: Copeland, Duffie & Yang (2025), Quarterly Journal of Economics 140(1):239-281, 'Reserves Were Not So Ample After All' — reserve declines at large repo-active BHCs increase repo-rate distortions and spike severity nonlinearly; identifies SOFR-IORB-type spreads and payment delays as the real-time stress observables

Afonso, Cipriani, Copeland, Kovner, La Spada & Martin (2021), FRBNY Economic Policy Review 27(2), 'The Market Events of Mid-September 2019' — anatomy of the spike: TGA rebuild + settlement drained reserves; documents the equity-vol spillover window

Lopez-Salido & Vissing-Jorgensen (2024, JF forthcoming/Fed WP), 'Reserve Demand, Interest Rate Control, and Quantitative Tightening' — estimates the reserve-demand curve slope from rate spreads, formalizing 'how scarce is scarce' from observable spreads alone

Krishnamurthy & Vissing-Jorgensen (2011), Brookings Papers on Economic Activity, 'The Effects of QE on Interest Rates' — the rigorous benchmark for what balance-sheet policy does and does not move; supports announcement-effects, not level-tracking folklore
findings.effect_size_net: This is a rare-event tail gate, not a return stream: expected to bind ~1-3% of days. Payoff profile: standing down new entries + cutting the overnight sleeve on the handful of funding-stress days avoids entering immediately before vol spikes (Sep-2019 SPX chop, Mar-2020 cascade, repo-squeeze windows in late-2025) on a high-beta book where a single avoided -3% overnight gap on 7 names ~= +40-60bp book P&L per episode. Cost: forgone entries on false-positive days (mostly quarter-ends; calendar-suppress those or require 2-day persistence) — bounded and small since the gate only delays entries, never forces liquidations. Direct transaction cost: zero. Folklore verdict net effect: building net-liquidity-as-feature would ADD noise and overfit risk; rejecting it is itself the finding.
findings.decay_evidence: CDY is 2025-published but the mechanism strengthened post-publication: QT-driven reserve drawdown through 2025 reproduced mild spread elevation exactly as predicted, and the Fed's own framework now watches the same spreads (EFFR-IORB, SOFR-IORB) as ample-reserves diagnostics — the signal is policy-monitored, not arbitraged (you cannot trade away a funding squeeze). Net-liquidity folklore decay is empirical and terminal: the 2022-26 divergence (flat net liquidity, +78% SPX) falsifies the level-tracking thesis out of sample. Caveat: the Fed's standing repo facility (SRF, 2021) caps spike magnitude vs 2019, so calibrate trigger thresholds in bp above IORB, not 2019-size blowouts: e.g., SOFR >= IORB + 10bp or SOFR99 >= IORB + 25bp, 2-day persistence.
findings.free_data_source: All FRED, all free, no revisions (administered/transaction rates are final at first print): SOFR and SOFR99 (NY Fed publishes ~8:00 ET next business day — available before the 9:45 entry window); IORB (set in advance, known same-day); EFFR (~9:00 ET next day). Context series: WRESBAL (weekly avg reserves, H.4.1, released Thursday ~4:30 ET, 1-day lag). For the folklore post-mortem only: RRPONTSYD (same-day ~1:15 ET) and TGA via Treasury FiscalData API (next business day ~16:00 ET). Point-in-time: rate series are never revised, so FRED history = real-time history; lag SOFR/EFFR one business day in backtests; WRESBAL by its Thursday release date.
findings.build_sketch: macro_indicators.py: fetch_funding_stress() pulling SOFR, SOFR99, IORB, EFFR each morning ~8:15 ET (3 cached CSV GETs); stress = max(SOFR-IORB, 0) and tail = max(SOFR99-IORB, 0). stock_loop.py gate (same pattern as the existing SPY rest-of-day PM tape gate): if stress >= 10bp or tail >= 25bp for 2 consecutive prints (quarter-end dates exempted), block new entries for the day and disable the overnight sleeve; log-only mode first month for live calibration. Jetson cost: nil (no model, 3 tiny fetches/day). Explicitly do NOT add WALCL-TGA-RRP as a feature.

findings.name: Excess Bond Premium (EBP) monthly slow-regime anchor — plus documented kills of NTFS, NFCI, and PMI from the same research sweep
findings.mechanism: The EBP is the credit spread component NOT explained by expected defaults — a direct read on intermediary risk appetite. Favara-Gilchrist-Lewis-Zakrajsek show the predictive power of credit spreads for recessions is due ENTIRELY to the EBP, and the Fed publishes the series + a 12-month-ahead recession probability monthly, free. As a monthly overlay it anchors the slow end of the app's regime stack: when model-implied recession probability is elevated (e.g., >30-40%, the threshold region that captured 1990/2001/2008 in-sample), compress the top-7 entry book's gross and shift the GARCH sizing toward its defensive setting. This complements finding #1: daily HY OAS velocity is the fast proxy; monthly EBP is the cleaner default-risk-purged level read.
key_papers: Favara, Gilchrist, Lewis & Zakrajsek (2016), FEDS Notes, 'Updating the Recession Risk and the Excess Bond Premium' (Oct 6, 2016) — operational series; probit of NBER recession within 12 months on EBP; spreads' downturn-forecasting power attributable entirely to EBP
Gilchrist & Zakrajsek (2012), AER 102(4) — original decomposition; EBP shocks depress activity and equity prices (see finding #1)

KILL — Engstrom & Sharpe (2019), Financial Analysts Journal 75(4):37-49, 'The Near-Term Forward Yield Spread as a Leading Indicator' — NTFS statistically dominates 2s10s and showed in-sample equity-return predictability, BUT its post-publication record is disqualifying for this app: it read near-zero recession probability in mid-2022 (correct, luckily) then inverted deeply Nov-2022 through 2024 signaling high recession odds — no recession, SPX strongly up. A signal whose two post-pub states were 'lucky' and 'wrong', on monthly horizons, adds nothing to an hourly system that already has SPY trend + VIX + HMM. Requires GSW forward-curve data anyway (weekly Fed update). Rejected

KILL — NFCI/ANFCI: release mechanics are fine (Chicago Fed, Wednesdays 8:30 ET covering through prior Friday; ALFRED vintages exist; history re-estimated weekly so vintages are MANDATORY), but the 105-indicator factor loads on VIX/credit/equity vol the app already has via the VIX ladder, HMM, and the already-fetched STLFSI2 — and Plagborg-Moller, Reichlin, Ricco & Hasenzagl (2020, BPEA, 'When Is Growth at Risk?') find financial-conditions indices provide no robust out-of-sample advance warning of tail risks beyond mean predictors, directly tempering Adrian-Boyarchenko-Giannone (2019, AER 109(4), 'Vulnerable Growth'). Redundant; rejected

KILL — ISM/PMI new-orders-minus-inventories: ISM data was removed from FRED June 24, 2016 (licensing); S&P Global flash PMI historical data is subscription-only with IP-restricted press releases. No free, redistributable, point-in-time source exists; monthly cadence is marginal for this system anyway. Rejected on data-rights grounds
findings.effect_size_net: EBP >= ~1 (one-ish sigma) or model recession-prob >= 35% marked 1990, 2000-01, 2007-08, 2020, and the 2022 trough region, with the main false-ish positive in 2011-12 (Euro crisis — SPX -19% drawdown anyway, so 'false' is generous) — call it 5-of-6 useful activations over 35 years at monthly granularity. As a 0.7x gross multiplier during elevated months on a $100k high-beta book, expect low-single-digit max-drawdown reduction across recessionary episodes for ~zero incremental transaction cost (multiplier changes a few times per decade-cycle; deltas ride scheduled rebalances). The honest limit: monthly cadence + up-to-5-week staleness means it NEVER catches shock crashes — it is a slow-cycle anchor only, and must be subordinate to the daily layers.
findings.decay_evidence: EBP remains the Fed's actively maintained recession-risk input ten years post-FEDS-note — no retirement, no sign flip; 2022-23 saw elevated EBP without recession (drawdown happened anyway: SPX -25%), 2024-25 EBP stayed benign through the rally (correct). The macro-credit channel is structural, not crowdable. Main risk is the point-in-time one (next field), not decay.
findings.free_data_source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/notes/feds-notes/ebp_csv.csv — monthly CSV (EBP + GZ spread + recession probability, 1973-present), refreshed after ~10:00 ET on the FOURTH business day of each month with data through the prior month (worst-case ~5-week staleness; model that exact lag). POINT-IN-TIME WARNING: the full history is re-estimated each month (balance-sheet updates, sample composition); revisions are 'modest and concentrated in recent months' per the Fed, but there is NO ALFRED vintage archive for EBP. Mitigation: (a) start archiving the CSV on the 4th business day of every month NOW (it is the live signal going forward), (b) in backtests, lag the revised series an extra month AND haircut the recent-month values, or validate sensitivity to +/-10bp EBP noise; if the overlay's value dies under that haircut, don't ship it.
findings.build_sketch: macro_indicators.py: fetch_ebp() — one HTTPS GET of ebp_csv.csv on the 4th business day (cron via the existing daily overlay refresh; cache to disk, building the vintage archive as a side effect). get_macro_regime(): recession_prob >= 35% (validated threshold) -> sizing_mult x0.7 and stop_mult tightened one notch; feeds the same MacroRegime dataclass already consumed by stock_loop. Jetson cost: one 100KB download/month, zero compute. Strictly subordinate: applied multiplicatively with the VIX ladder/HMM, never overriding faster layers.

findings.name: Point-in-time macro data layer: ALFRED realtime vintages + release-time stamping as architecture (prerequisite for every macro overlay above)
findings.mechanism: The app currently fetches latest-vintage FRED CSVs (fredgraph.csv for VIXCLS/STLFSI2) with no vintage or release-time handling. Any backtest of macro overlays on latest-vintage data leaks two ways: (1) REVISIONS — NFCI/STLFSI2 histories are re-estimated weekly, claims seasonal factors are rewritten annually, EBP is re-estimated monthly; the 'history' you download today is not what was knowable then (Croushore-Stark formalized this; Orphanides showed real-time-vs-revised data reverses policy-rule conclusions — same trap for trading rules); (2) TIMING — a Thursday-released weekly value naively merged on its Friday period-end date appears 6 days early. The fix is structural, not per-signal: a single vintage-aware fetcher + a release-lag table, so every macro series enters the panel stamped with when it was actually knowable. This is what makes findings 1-4 validatable on the existing purged-WF/DSR harness instead of silently optimistic.
key_papers: Croushore & Stark (2001), Journal of Econometrics 105(1):111-130, 'A Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists' — the foundational demonstration that macro results change materially on real-time vs revised data; the reason ALFRED exists

Orphanides (2001), American Economic Review 91(4):964-985, 'Monetary Policy Rules Based on Real-Time Data' — canonical magnitude evidence: real-time vs revised inputs flip substantive conclusions; the exact failure mode a revised-data backtest of NFCI/claims overlays would hit

Operational: FRED API fred/series/observations with realtime_start=realtime_end=as-of-date (free API key) returns exactly what was published as of any date — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_observations.html; ALFRED vintage archives confirmed for NFCI, STLFSI2, ICSA/ICNSA, WRESBAL
findings.effect_size_net: No direct P&L; the effect is avoided FALSE P&L. Vintage-vs-revised gaps are largest exactly where the overlays operate: claims SA factors (2026-03-19 release rewrote 2021-forward — COVID-era SA claims were misleading by tens of percent in real time), weekly factor-model indices (NFCI/STLFSI2 2008 vintages differ visibly from today's history), EBP recent months. A macro gate that only works on revised data is a disqualified signal under the project's own rules — this layer is what enforces that automatically. Cost: a few hours of build, ~MBs of vintage matrices downloaded once, zero recurring Jetson load beyond existing fetches.
findings.decay_evidence: Not applicable in the anomaly sense — this is methodology with permanent validity. The supporting evidence base (Croushore-Stark real-time literature) has only strengthened: real-time macro evaluation is now the default standard in the forecasting literature, and ALFRED coverage keeps expanding (NFCI vintages through 2026 confirmed).
findings.free_data_source: ALFRED/FRED API, free key from https://fredaccount.stlouisfed.org: GET fred/series/observations?series_id=X&realtime_start=D&realtime_end=D. Series and their archives used here: ICNSA/ICSA (vintages on ALFRED), NFCI/ANFCI (vintages 1971-present data, archived weekly), STLFSI2, WRESBAL; rate series (SOFR/SOFR99/EFFR/IORB) and BAMLH0A0HYM2 are unrevised so latest = real-time, needing only the release-lag stamp; EBP has NO public vintages — self-archive monthly (finding #4). Release-lag table (knowable-at timestamps, ET): claims Thu 8:30; NFCI Wed 8:30; H.4.1/WRESBAL Thu 16:30; SOFR/SOFR99 ~8:00 next bus. day; HY OAS next bus. morning; EBP 4th bus. day ~10:00.

CROSS-ASSET and CROSS-SECTOR lead-lag for stock prediction. Dig into: Hong-Torous-Valka

findings.name: Cross-industry gradual-diffusion lead-lag: lagged financials + commodity/materials sector returns as panel features for other sectors' names
findings.mechanism: Gradual information diffusion across economically linked industries (Hong-Stein 1999 limited attention; Merton 1987 segmentation). Specialized investors process only their own sector; information originating in financials (credit conditions for downstream borrowers) and commodity/material producers (input-cost and end-demand news propagating through the production network) reaches prices of economically linked sectors with a 1-2 month lag. HTV verified the auxiliary prediction that leading industries also forecast industrial production growth — it is fundamentals diffusion, not stat artifact; signs are industry-specific (retail up = good news for market; petroleum up = bad news). RSTZ 2019 show predictive pervasiveness of an industry correlates with its centrality in the US production network. CRITICAL DISTINCTION for decay: the industry->AGGREGATE-MARKET timing version decayed (Tse 2015), but the industry->INDUSTRY cross-sectional network version survives with multiple-testing controls — and the cross-sectional version is exactly what a top-7-of-50 ranking model consumes.
key_papers: Hong, Torous, Valkanov (2007, Journal of Financial Economics 83:367-396) 'Do Industries Lead Stock Markets?': 1946-2002, 14 of 34 US industries (retail, services, commercial real estate, metal, petroleum, financial) predict the market 1 month ahead; petroleum, metal, financial predict 2 months ahead; only 0.04% of random simulations produce >=14 significant industries; forecasting power comparable to dividend yield and default spread; same pattern in 8 largest non-US markets.

Rapach, Strauss, Tu, Zhou (2019, Journal of Financial Data Science 1(3):9-28) 'Industry Return Predictability: A Machine Learning Approach': adaptive-LASSO on lagged monthly industry returns, controls for post-selection inference and multiple testing; lagged FINANCIAL-sector and COMMODITY/MATERIAL-producing industry returns show widespread cross-industry predictive ability; OOS industry-rotation long-short earns >8%/yr annualized alpha vs leading multifactor models, with largest gains in downturns incl. the Great Recession.

Hou (2007, Review of Financial Studies 20(4):1113-1138) 'Industry Information Diffusion and the Lead-Lag Effect in Stock Returns': big->small lead-lag is predominantly INTRA-industry, driven by sluggish adjustment to negative news, concentrated in small/neglected/less-competitive industries — mechanism support, and the reason a big-leads-small clone inside a mega-cap liquid universe is NOT proposed.
Tse (2015, Journal of Empirical Finance 34:195-203) 'Do industries lead stock markets? A reexamination': decay evidence — see decay field.
findings.effect_size_net: RSTZ monthly cross-industry rotation: >8%/yr OOS alpha gross on long-short deciles of 30 industries; expect the long-only, 50-name, already-momentum-tilted version to retain perhaps 1-3%/yr of ranking improvement — but implementation is PURE FEATURE ADDITION to the LightGBM ranker, so incremental cost is ~zero round trips (signals shift rankings inside the existing top-7/top-15 hysteresis; 11bps+spread RT cost only applies if turnover rises — keep the hold-15 band as the turnover guardrail). HTV-scale magnitudes: per-1-sigma industry move, next-month market effect was on the order of 20-40bp (comparable to default-spread predictor) — at feature level this is well above label noise at weekly-monthly horizons.
findings.decay_evidence: Honest and mixed, direction matters: Tse (2015 JEF), extending to 1946-2013 with 48 industries, finds only 1-7 industries still significantly predict the AGGREGATE market (10%/5% levels), weaker results after CRSP data revisions, and some reverse-direction predictability — the market-timing version is largely dead. HTV's own 2014 note (Rady/UCSD) extends to 2013 and defends continued predictability in rolling regressions. RSTZ (2019), using post-selection-robust inference through ~2016, find the cross-INDUSTRY network version strongly alive (financials, commodities/materials as hubs). McLean-Pontiff baseline ~58% post-publication decay should be assumed. Related kill confirmed and folded here: classic Lo-MacKinlay (1990 RFS) big->small lead-lag has collapsed (weekly small-cap-on-lagged-big-cap correlation 0.210 in 1962-1988 to 0.085 in 1988-2002, milliseconds at HF today), and Hou's effect lives in small/neglected names — so no NVDA->semis-bucket daily lead feature for a mega-cap universe; the surviving exploitable form is sector-level, weeks-horizon, cross-sectional.
findings.free_data_source: Alpaca daily bars (GET /v2/stocks/bars, adjustment=all — verified supported: raw/split/dividend/spin-off/all) for sector ETFs XLF XLE XLB XLI XLK XLP XLU XLV XLY + SMH + IYT; all NYSE-Arca-listed, in Alpaca's coverage; Alpaca history reaches ~2016, backfill 1998-2016 from yfinance adjusted daily closes (SPDR sectors exist since Dec 1998) for training only. Publication lag ZERO (exchange closes), no revisions, point-in-time by construction. Alternative/supplement: compute the same lagged returns from the app's own ~96-name panel sector buckets (stock_config.py already maps names to financials/energy/semis/staples buckets) — fully self-contained.
findings.build_sketch: New sector_leads.py (or extend panel_ranks.py add_panel_ranks): once daily after close, pull adjusted daily bars for the ~11 sector ETFs; compute trailing 5d and 21d log returns EXCESS of SPY (cheap orthogonalization so the existing SPY-trend/breadth features don't double-count the market factor); z-score each vs its own 1y history. Broadcast the resulting ~22 features to every panel row (let LightGBM learn which consuming sector responds to which leader — mirrors RSTZ's finding that financials/materials lags matter for most targets), or optionally interact with the name's own sector bucket one-hot. Features constant within the trading day (lead horizon is weeks; hourly ranker just reuses them). Optional quarterly adaptive-LASSO preselection (11 predictors x ~10 sector targets, scikit-learn, seconds on Jetson CPU). Jetson cost: 11 ETFs x 1 daily bar fetch + arithmetic — negligible memory/CPU.

findings.name: Credit-tape risk overlay: duration-hedged HYG vs LQD/IEF relative strength as a daily risk-appetite state variable, used as credit-vs-VIX divergence sizing logic
findings.mechanism: Aggregate credit spreads price corporate default expectations PLUS intermediary risk-bearing capacity; the non-default component (Gilchrist-Zakrajsek excess bond premium) is a forward indicator of activity and risk-asset performance because constrained intermediaries withdraw risk capital before equity investors reprice. Key honesty constraint that shapes the design: at the SINGLE-NAME level information flows equity->credit, NOT credit->equity (Hilscher-Pollet-Wilson 2015) — so this is not a return-alpha lead-lag; the aggregate credit tape is a SECOND, slower state variable that is empirically distinct from implied vol. Divergences are the payload for a high-beta long-only book: sustained credit widening with moderate VIX (2015-16 HY/energy bust) = genuine de-risk regimes the VIX ladder misses; VIX spikes with calm credit (Aug-2024 carry unwind, where credit lagged) = technical vol events where full de-risking is the wrong move. This complements, not duplicates, the existing VIX level ladder and weekly STLFSI2.
key_papers: Gilchrist, Zakrajsek (2012, American Economic Review 102(4):1692-1720) 'Credit Spreads and Business Cycle Fluctuations': GZ spread decomposition; a 1-sigma shock to the excess bond premium (EBP) leads to significant declines in activity and risk-asset prices over the following year; EBP remains the Fed's maintained recession-risk indicator (FEDS Notes, updated monthly).

Lopez-Salido, Stein, Zakrajsek (2017, Quarterly Journal of Economics 132(3):1373-1426) 'Credit-Market Sentiment and the Business Cycle': elevated credit-market sentiment predicts spread widening, lower growth, and poor risk-asset performance 1-2 years ahead — the slow-moving cycle anchor.

Hilscher, Pollet, Wilson (2015, Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 50(3)) 'Are Credit Default Swaps a Sideshow?': equity returns lead credit-protection returns at daily/weekly frequency, credit does not lead equity at firm level — the explicit reason this is built as an aggregate REGIME overlay, not a stock-prediction feature.
findings.effect_size_net: Not a mean-alpha signal: expected gains are drawdown/left-tail reduction on a high-beta long book — historically, regimes with credit z-scores in the worst quintile carry materially negative high-beta equity Sharpe (GZ-style state dependence), and overlay implementation changes only position SIZES, so incremental transaction cost ~zero (the book already re-sizes via GARCH/EWMA daily). Realistic effect at this scale: cutting gross 30-50% during sustained-credit-widening regimes that the VIX ladder under-flags; backtestable against 2015-16 and 2018Q4 with HYG/LQD/IEF history from 2007 via yfinance backfill (covers GFC).
findings.decay_evidence: State variables, not anomalies — outside the McLean-Pontiff decay universe; EBP/credit-conditions indicators have survived 14+ years post-GZ as Fed-maintained tools. Documented failure mode rather than decay: credit can LAG in purely vol/positioning-driven selloffs (Aug 2024 yen-carry unwind — credit barely moved while VIX spiked), which is precisely why it enters as divergence logic beside the VIX ladder instead of a standalone hard gate (and hard gates on single indicators are already a wave-3 lesson).
findings.free_data_source: PRIMARY (zero lag, fully PIT): Alpaca daily bars adjustment=all for HYG, LQD, IEF — adjustment=all is mandatory because HYG/LQD pay ~monthly distributions (~0.3-0.5%) that saw-tooth a raw price ratio; Alpaca history ~2016+, yfinance adjusted closes backfill to 2007 for training. SECONDARY (sanity check only): FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA US HY OAS), daily with 1-business-day publication lag, levels not revised — but VERIFIED: as of April 2026 FRED truncates ALL ICE BofA series to a rolling 3-year window, so it CANNOT be the training source; the bar-computed signal is the only fully point-in-time-reconstructable option. Pattern matches existing macro_indicators.py FRED/yfinance fallback design.
findings.build_sketch: Extend macro_indicators.py with fetch_credit_regime() (daily cache, like fetch_vix): (1) duration-hedged HY excess return r_HYG - beta*r_IEF with rolling 63d beta (~0.35-0.45), (2) 21d change in log(HYG/LQD) adjusted ratio; z-score both vs trailing 1y; credit_stress = max of the two inverted z's. Consume in the sizing layer beside the VIX ladder: credit_z < -1.5 => gross tilt 0.7x and block the overnight sleeve; credit_z < -2.5 => 0.5x; VIX-elevated AND credit_z > -0.5 => floor the VIX ladder's de-risk at 0.8x (buyable-vol-spike branch). All thresholds validated in purged walk-forward before promotion, like the existing ladders. Jetson cost: 3 daily bar series + one rolling regression — nil.

findings.name: Foreign lagged-weekly-return features for US single names (Foreign Signal Radar): 1-4 week lagged country-index/ETF returns into the pooled LightGBM ranker
findings.mechanism: Slow cross-border information diffusion into BOTH multinational and domestic US firms: investors have limited attention for foreign developments, so value-relevant foreign-market moves (supply chains, end-market demand, geopolitics) are absorbed into US single-name prices over 4-8 WEEKS, fastest when media coverage of foreign news is high and for stocks with foreign institutional ownership. Predictability is concentrated where attention is scarcest (low-media-coverage periods, EM/low-coverage source markets). Direction asymmetry matters: at the INDEX level the US leads the world, not vice versa (Rapach-Strauss-Zhou 2013) — so the exploitable object is cross-sectional single-name prediction from lagged weekly foreign returns, not US market timing; this matches the app's per-symbol pooled architecture exactly (the paper trains per-stock models on rolling 252d windows — structurally our setup).
key_papers: Jiao (2025, working paper, Rutgers; arXiv 2504.07855, version March 2025) 'Foreign Signal Radar': 188 signals = lagged 1-4 week returns of 47 foreign markets; per-stock LASSO/RF/GB/NN on rolling 4-quarter windows predicting DAILY S&P 500 constituent returns; long-short top/bottom 5% by predicted return earns 5.63bp/day abnormal (14.2%/yr, LASSO; NN 5.77, RF 3.81, GB 3.80), robust in early/late subsamples and to US or global factor models; positive OOS R^2 for 24%/22%/36%/8% of names (LASSO/RF/GB/NN) averaging 1.6-3.6% among predictable names; signal importance decays from 1-week to 4-week lags; full incorporation takes 4-8 weeks; effects similar for domestic and multinational firms; the ~13,000-signal individual-foreign-stock pool adds nothing over market indices (sparsity).

Rapach, Strauss, Zhou (2013, Journal of Finance 68(4):1633-1662) 'International Stock Return Predictability: What Is the Role of the United States?': lagged US returns predict numerous non-US industrialized markets monthly; lagged non-US returns show LIMITED ability to predict US returns — kills the naive foreign->US index-timing version and the Nikkei-gates-the-overnight-sleeve idea (Tokyo also opens hours AFTER the 15:50 ET sleeve decision, so it is not even point-in-time feasible).
findings.effect_size_net: Gross 14.2%/yr on daily-turnover long-short top/bottom 5% is NOT harvestable at our cost structure as a strategy (daily L/S turnover at 11bps+spread RT eats most of 5.6bp/day). As FEATURES the economics invert: ~20 lagged weekly country-ETF returns added to the pooled LightGBM change rankings only — zero mandated extra turnover, and only the 22-36% of names with genuine foreign exposure will load. Expected contribution: a modest ranking-IC improvement concentrated in the panel's internationally exposed names (semis with Asia supply chains, energy, industrials); realistically a low-single-digit relative IC gain — cheap to test through the existing DSR holdout + challenger shadow gauntlet.
findings.decay_evidence: Working paper (March 2025), NOT yet peer-reviewed — the main caveat; no third-party replication yet. Self-decay analysis included: the paper documents markets becoming MORE efficient at absorbing foreign info over time, with the improvement concentrated in emerging-market signals (Bai-Philippon-Savov price-informativeness trend) and during high-attention episodes like COVID — assume the post-2020 harvestable share is meaningfully below full-sample. The structural friction (attention to 47 markets) is not arbitrageable to zero by HFT since horizon is weeks. Treat as exploratory feature block, kill via feature-importance/SHAP review if it never loads.
findings.free_data_source: Alpaca daily bars adjustment=all for US-listed country ETFs (all NYSE Arca): EWJ (Japan), MCHI or FXI (China), EWY (Korea), EWT (Taiwan), EWG (Germany), EWU (UK), EWQ (France), EWZ (Brazil), INDA (India), EEM (EM agg) — ~2016+ history, yfinance backfill earlier (or yfinance local indices ^N225 ^GDAXI ^STOXX50E for longer training history). Use COMPLETED prior trading weeks computed from US-session ETF closes: point-in-time by construction, zero publication lag, and sidesteps foreign-local-close timestamp alignment entirely (the ETF close already impounds the foreign session through US hours). No paid data needed since the paper itself shows individual foreign STOCK signals add nothing over market-level signals.
findings.build_sketch: Extend the panel feature builder (panel_ranks.py / model feature assembly): weekly (Fri-close) resample of ~10 country ETFs; features = {1w lag, 4w-cum lag} log returns per ETF (~20 features), each z-scored vs 1y, neutral-filled via existing neutral_fill_cs; broadcast to all panel rows and let pooled LightGBM learn name-specific loadings (matches the paper's per-stock heterogeneity without 100k models). Constant intraday; refreshed weekly. Optional: quarterly per-symbol LASSO screen to zero out features for never-loading names (seconds on CPU). Jetson cost: 10 daily-bar series + resampling — negligible; +20 features is well within LightGBM headroom on 8GB.

findings.name: Regime-conditioned industrial-metals overlay (copper/aluminum via CPER, vs GLD): sign-flipping Dr.-Copper signal as a daily risk-tilt input; oil explicitly excluded
findings.mechanism: Industrial metals prices impound real-time global demand information (inventory/convenience-yield channel; commodity futures as growth barometers per Hu-Xiong), and equity investors underreact to it — but the SIGN of the equity implication is state-dependent, which is why naive Dr.-Copper rules fail: in EXPANSIONS rising metals are inflation/tightening news (1-sigma metal return => about -1.5% next-month equity), in RECESSIONS/slumps rising metals are demand-recovery news (=> about +0.5% next month). The copper/gold ratio variant additionally nets out the monetary/safe-haven component. Oil is deliberately EXCLUDED from this family: its equity relation flipped sign around 2008 (negative per Driesprong et al., then persistently positive as demand shocks dominated post-financialization, per Kilian-Park decompositions) and fails the sign-stability bar.
key_papers: Jacobsen, Marshall, Visaltanachoti (2019, Management Science 65(7):3026-3042) 'Stock Market Predictability and Industrial Metal Returns': monthly horizon; +1-sigma industrial-metal return predicts about -1.5% next-month equity in expansions and about +0.5% in recessions; monthly OOS R^2 of 3-8%, favorable vs established predictors (dividend yield, term spread class).

Driesprong, Jacobsen, Maat (2008, Journal of Financial Economics 89(2):307-327) 'Striking Oil: Another Puzzle?': oil changes negatively predicted world equity with ~6-10 day delayed reaction — cited as the EXCLUSION case: post-2008 the oil-equity correlation turned significantly positive (demand-shock dominance, Kilian-Park 2009 AER/IER framework), so the oil version is sign-unstable and rejected.

Kilian, Park (2009, International Economic Review 50(4)) 'The Impact of Oil Price Shocks on the U.S. Stock Market': demand- vs supply-shock decomposition explaining why undifferentiated oil signals flip sign across regimes.
findings.effect_size_net: JMV's 3-8% monthly OOS R^2 is large for an aggregate predictor, but the harvestable version here is a bounded daily SIZING tilt (no new trades, cost ~zero): scale the existing risk-based gross up/down by up to ~10-15% as f(21d metal z-score, regime state). Expected contribution is timing-quality of the existing exposure dial, not new alpha streams; at 50-name top-7 scale that is worth single-digit bps/month in better drawdown timing — justified only because implementation cost is near-zero and it diversifies the VIX/credit/trend state set with a REAL-economy price signal.
findings.decay_evidence: Published 2019 (Management Science); no major published replication challenge found in searches; metals are less financialized than oil but increasingly ETF-ized — assume partial decay. The serious caveat is POINT-IN-TIME conditioning: JMV condition on NBER expansion/recession dating, which is announced ~4-12+ months late and therefore NOT usable live; the PIT-safe surrogate is the app's existing SPY-200d trend or HMM state as the regime switch, and that substitution MUST be validated in purged walk-forward before any weight is trusted — if the sign-conditioning does not survive the surrogate regime variable, kill the overlay (cheap to test, cheap to kill).
findings.free_data_source: Alpaca daily bars adjustment=all for CPER (US Copper Index Fund, NYSE Arca, inception 2011 — futures-roll based, fine for 21d return signals) and GLD; COPX (copper miners) is ALREADY in the app's panel/ETF list (stock_config.py ETF_TICKERS) as an equity-side cross-check but is contaminated by equity beta, so CPER is the cleaner signal. Zero publication lag, no revisions, PIT by construction. Pre-2011 training backfill: yfinance HG=F front-month (Comex) or LME-tracking series — training-only, flagged as lower fidelity. FRED copper (PCOPPUSDM) is monthly IMF data with ~1-month lag — usable only as a slow sanity check, not the live signal.
findings.build_sketch: Extend macro_indicators.py: daily cached compute of (a) 21d CPER log return z-scored vs 1y, (b) 21d change in log(CPER/GLD); regime_state from the existing SPY-200d/HMM plumbing; risk_tilt = clamp(-k * z_metal, +/-0.15) in trend-up state and clamp(+k * z_metal, +/-0.10) in trend-down state (sign flip per JMV), with k tuned in walk-forward; multiply into the GARCH/EWMA gross-sizing chain next to the VIX ladder and credit overlay; never gates entries, only scales. Jetson cost: 2 daily bar series + arithmetic — nil; daily cadence (overlay), not hourly.
