Regime-conditional jobless-claims momentum: fastest free labor signal, with the Boyd-Hu-Jagannathan sign flip built in M

fatal_flaws: In-era evidence is net-negative, not positive: reconstructing the exact proposed trigger point-in-time (ICNSA 4wk avg, 364-day YoY, Thursday release, price-weak gate) shows that in the app's entire backtestable era (2017-2026, 481 weeks) the composite fired in exactly ONE episode - 9 releases from 2020-03-26 to 2020-05-21 - beginning three days AFTER the 2020-03-23 SPX closing low and spanning a +15.2% SPX rebound (larger in high-beta). Claims YoY was negative (-8% to -2%) through the entire Feb-Mar 2020 crash; the 5-day lag + weekly cadence + YoY threshold make it structurally late for fast crashes. The only in-sample contribution is forgone recovery upside on a long-only high-beta book, with zero drawdown protection delivered.

All supporting episodes (first fires Oct-1989, Nov-2000, Mar-2008) predate Alpaca hourly data and cannot enter the system's own validation stack (purged walk-forward, DSR holdout, DM-HLN shadow promotion). A <2%-of-weeks overlay cannot be certified by that machinery within years, so it would ship as a permanently untested hand rule - contradicting the system's governance. The 12-15% threshold is unidentifiable in-panel (2020 jumped +340% in one week, so any threshold from 10% to 300% fires identically in-era); 'threshold fit on purged WF' is theater, and the chosen value is implicitly snooped on ~3 pre-2010 episodes (n_effective ~4 celebrated events for a multi-parameter rule family - squarely in Sullivan-Timmermann-White / Bajgrowicz-Scaillet rejection territory).

Redundancy is structural, not incidental: the composite is by construction a subset of price-weak states, and in its only in-era firing VIX was 30-80, so the VIX ladder, GARCH/EWMA vol sizing, meta-label veto, and q10 tail veto were already maximally defensive - the 0.6x was an extra cut on an already-cut book during the rebound. Standalone, the claims leg fired 20 episodes since 1967 with roughly half non-recessionary (1985; 1994; 1995-96 for 15 weeks during a raging bull; 2005 Katrina; Jun-Sep 2023 peak +19% in the fraud-distorted period; Oct-2024 Helene/Milton + Boeing strike) - every false positive is suppressed solely by the price gate, i.e., the claims signal does no discriminating work the existing regime layer is not already doing, while the 12-15% threshold sits inside NSA distortion noise.

Theory mis-transplant: Boyd-Hu-Jagannathan measures announcement-DAY repricing of monthly unemployment-rate surprises conditioned on the business-cycle (NBER) state; it contains no evidence of multi-week drift predictability after conditioning on a price-based regime, and the proposal's own concession that announcement effects are arbitraged in minutes implies the print's content is in prices by the 9:45 entry window - where the HMM/trend/VIX stack already reads it. Substituting a frequent price-HMM weak state for NBER contraction also breaks BHJ's conditioning in shallow price-weak windows, where BHJ says the labor-bad-news response is positive.

Asymmetric failure mode with no remedy in spec: large claims episodes hold YoY above threshold for 52-81 weeks (2020: 52 weeks to Mar-2021; 2008-09: 81 weeks to Sep-2009), so in any V-shaped episode the flag is late on the way down and then taxes the highest-beta recovery weeks; the rule can only cut size, never re-add, and has no hysteresis/expiry.

Real-time availability hole, verified via ALFRED vintages: as of vintage 2025-11-05 the latest ICNSA observation was still week-ending 2025-09-20 - the weekly release went dark ~6 weeks during the Oct-Nov 2025 government shutdown. Final-vintage backtests overstate real-time availability and the build spec has no missing-data policy for its 'fastest free labor signal'.
surviving_caveats: Point-in-time plumbing is genuinely best-practice and verified: ICNSA raw counts take only one small prior-week revision, ALFRED carries usable vintages (vintage pulls tested and working), and the Thursday 8:30 ET release lands before the 9:45 entry window with no intraday plumbing needed.
Cost and compute claims are honest: ~zero incremental transaction cost (it only scales already-planned trades), nil Jetson load, and weekly cadence is within the allowed overlay cadence.
The no-crowding argument holds: slow macro-state content has no McLean-Pontiff decay channel, and BHJ-style state dependence of macro-news responses replicates qualitatively in later literature.

Claims genuinely led the bulk of damage in pre-2010 slow-burn recessions (first composite-eligible fires Oct-1989, Nov-2000, Mar-2008 - the last ahead of the Sep-Nov 2008 collapse), and the composite was correctly silent in 1995-96, Jun-Sep 2023, and Oct-2024 false-positive windows (albeit thanks to the price gate). A re-specified version could merit consideration as explicit, unvalidatable tail insurance outside the promotion stack: fire only on FRESH threshold crossings with an 8-12 week expiry (kills the 52-81 week recovery-echo drag), require the claims crossing to PRECEDE the price-weak state rather than follow it, and treat missing releases as no-signal.
output.notes: Adjudicated with data, not just argument. Pulled full ICNSA from FRED, SP500 daily (2016+), and ALFRED vintage snapshots; reconstructed the exact proposed trigger point-in-time (4wk NSA avg, 364-day same-week YoY, Thursday obs+5d release, SPX<200dma as the proposal's price-weak gate proxy) at both 12% and 15% thresholds. Artifacts: /tmp/claims_analysis.py, /tmp/icnsa.csv, /tmp/sp500.csv, /tmp/icnsa_v20251105.csv. Key numbers: composite ON 9 of 481 weeks (1.9%) in 2017-2026, all in one episode 2020-03-26 to 2020-05-21 (first fire 3 days after the SPX low; SPX +15.2% while ON); claims YoY negative throughout the actual Feb-Mar 2020 crash; claims-leg-only fired 20 episodes since 1967 (~half non-recessionary); YoY echo persists 52-81 weeks after major shocks; ALFRED confirms ~6 missing weekly releases during the Oct-Nov 2025 shutdown. Axes conceded to the proposal: decay/crowding, transaction costs, Jetson compute, overlay cadence, and the plumbing design itself. The claim fails the survival bar on surviving evidence (only in-era firing was net-harmful; favorable episodes are pre-2010 and outside the app's validation machinery) and on genuine non-redundancy (strict subset of price-weak states; all false-positive control comes from the existing gate). Confidence 2/5 rather than 1 because a materially re-specified fresh-crossing/expiry variant framed as untestable tail insurance retains some merit - but that is a different proposal than the one claimed."}

hint: Round-number and reference-level microstructure: distance-to-round-number features (hourly) + Osler-aware stop/take-prof

fatal_flaws: PIT/adjusted-bars grid corruption (verified in repo): training bars are fetched with adjustment='all' (market_data.py:257-262) and the yfinance fallback uses auto_adjust=True (data_sources.py:154-163). dist_round = price mod $1/$5/$10 is the ONLY proposed feature class that is not scale-invariant, so split/dividend adjustment silently destroys it: a 10:1 split maps the historical $1 grid to $0.10 (NVDA/TSLA/AMZN-class splits are inside any multi-year panel window), and every dividend multiplies history by a non-round factor pushing all prior closes off the actually-traded grid. Result: feature history is fiction for large swaths of the panel while live values are computed on true prices -> systematic train/serve skew that walk-forward cannot detect, plus non-reproducibility (the same historical bar's feature value changes every time a new corporate action re-adjusts the series). The BUILD never mentions raw-price plumbing; as specified it fails the clean-PIT requirement.

Equity return evidence lives in one pre-HFT window: BHJ (Mgmt Sci 2012) is 100 firms/year, 2001-2006 TAQ; Kavajecz-Odders-White is 1999 NYSE specialist-era order books. No peer-reviewed post-2010 US replication of the conditional drift exists. The only modern support (Zhang, SSRN 4718961, 2023: +24.6bps/day close-above-round) is non-peer-reviewed and concentrated in low-priced retail-heavy names -- by the proposal's own Zarattini guardrail (rejecting non-peer-reviewed short-sample WPs) it cannot be load-bearing. The -7bps/24h BHJ effect is also conditional on tick-level quote events ('ask falls below integer') that are unobservable in hourly OHLCV, so the cited effect size does not transfer to the implementable hourly-close-distance feature.

The exit-overlay cent geometry is folklore for equities: Osler's TP-at/SL-beyond clustering comes from one FX dealer's 1999-2000 order book measured in pips; BHJ documents quote/trade imbalances, not stop-order resting locations; no public US equity stop-order dataset validates a 1-5c cascade zone or a 3-6c nudge. The nudge mechanically WIDENS every affected stop (3-12bps extra realized loss on a $50-100 stock each time the stop fires anyway) against an unverifiable cascade saving -- 'essentially zero downside risk' is false, and it adds operational risk to the most safety-hardened code path (bracket legs + server-side stop re-placement).

Claimed benefit is unmeasurable in the current environment and mis-sized ~10x: Alpaca PAPER fills trigger bracket legs at quote touch with no depth, queue position, or cascade dynamics, so the proposed A/B nudge log can only record the overlay's mechanical costs, never its benefit. Zone-coverage arithmetic: stop zone [L-5c,L-1c] covers ~5% and TP zone ~3% of placements on the $1 grid, roughly half of round trips exit via stop/TP -> book-level expectation ~0.05-0.2bps even if the FX geometry transferred perfectly, not 'a real fraction of net edge.'
surviving_caveats: The underlying mechanism is genuinely alive (unlike wave-3 kills): round-number ORDER CLUSTERING replicates continuously from Harris 1991 through post-decimalization TAQ to present-day crypto liquidation maps; nothing here is sign-flipped or arbitraged to zero. The kill is against this build, not the physics.

Feature channel is salvageable with specified repair: add a raw-price side-feed (Alpaca adjustment='raw' is the API default per the repo's own comment) or store cumulative adjustment factors and reconstruct the as-of grid point-in-time; then ship dist_round as low-prior gated ranker features under the existing meta-label/DSR gates. Zhang (SSRN 4718961; 18 markets, intraday robustness, causal split/dividend identification) gives directional support pending peer review. Budget the extra bar storage against Jetson 8GB before approving.

Crypto is the defensible slice of the overlay: crypto bars are unadjusted (no grid corruption), resting GTC stop-limits already exist (crypto_loop.py _place_resting_stop, lines 157-234), and round-number liquidation clustering is currently documented (CoinGlass-style heatmaps; 2023-2026 cascade episodes clustered at $5k/$10k levels). But derive the avoid-zone width in percent/ATR terms from liquidation data -- 'cents' geometry does not translate to BTC at six figures.
Equity exit-stack nudge: defer until live-money trading, where fills can actually express cascade/queue effects; the shadow-log A/B design is sound there and worthless in paper.

PDH/PDL/opening-range features are near-PIT-clean (only wrong across ex-div/split boundary days due to short lookback) and verified non-redundant with existing features (repo has only session VWAP ratio, Gap_Pct, BB, ROD_Ret -- no level features); but they are admitted evidence-free, so strictly low-prior, gated, and killed by walk-forward if empty.

Redundancy and compute axes PASS: no existing round-number/reference-level features in indicators.py/indicator_config.py/panel_ranks.py, and the arithmetic is negligible on Jetson. Long-only usage (entry-timing tiebreak, ranker input) is viable.
output.notes: Verdict: REFUTED AS SPECIFIED, with a narrow salvage path. The conjunctive bar for survives=true fails on two of four prongs. (1) Clean PIT plumbing: verified against the actual codebase, the proposal's feature channel computes a price-level-mod-grid quantity on dividend/split-adjusted history (market_data.py:257-262 adjustment='all'; data_sources.py yfinance auto_adjust=True) -- the one feature type for which adjustment is fatal, and the failure is silent (no error; corrupted training history, clean live values, features that mutate retroactively at each corporate action). (2) Surviving evidence: clustering-the-phenomenon survives every decay test, but the equity RETURN effect's peer-reviewed support is entirely 2001-2006 (BHJ) at tick-level event granularity that hourly bars cannot observe, and the overlay's cents-level cascade-zone geometry has zero equity evidence (Osler is one FX dealer, 1999-2000, in pips). The modern supporting paper (Zhang SSRN 4718961) is exactly the class of non-peer-reviewed WP the proposal itself uses as a counter-evidence guardrail against Zarattini. (3) The execution overlay's claimed 1-5bps is conditional on ~5-8% of exits -> ~0.1bps book-level, is unmeasurable in Alpaca paper fills (no depth/queue/cascade simulation -- the A/B can only log costs), and the stop-widening side strictly increases realized losses on stops that fire anyway. Repo verification also confirmed the overlay WOULD mechanically apply (stock buys are bracket orders with server-side stop/TP legs, stock_loop.py:136-148; crypto has resting GTC stops, crypto_loop.py:157-234) and that the feature direction is genuinely non-redundant (no existing level features). Recommended disposition for the wave-4 queue: REJECT the equity execution overlay until live-money; ACCEPT-IF-REBUILT the dist_round feature channel strictly conditional on a raw-price/adjustment-factor side-feed with as-of grid reconstruction (budget Jetson storage first); consider a percent/ATR-calibrated round-number avoid-zone for the EXISTING crypto resting-stop placement as the only near-term build, sized by liquidation-map evidence. Confidence 2/5: mechanism real, build broken, net effect overstated. Sources: BHJ Mgmt Sci (https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.1110.1364, https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1569922), Zhang (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4718961), retail round-number behavior (https://cri.georgetown.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/Bloomfield-Chin-Craig-2024-Georgetown-CRI-WP.pdf), crypto liquidation clustering (https://www.coinglass.com/liquidation-levels).

hint: SENTIMENT and POSITIONING leading indicators from free point-in-time sources. Dig into:

findings.name: Daily shorting-flow ratio (long-window FINRA Reg SHO short volume) as per-name positioning feature + entry tilt
findings.mechanism: Short sellers are informed, anomaly-exploiting traders; their flow predicts negative returns even when publicly disclosed in real time because the market underreacts (day-1 reaction only 3.4-4bps vs alpha lasting up to a year). Critically for a LONG-ONLY book, the spread is driven by the OUTPERFORMANCE of the lightly-shorted quintile (significant positive alpha) rather than underperformance of heavily-shorted names — i.e., low shorting flow marks names institutions are not betting against. Post-2010, LONG-horizon shorting flows (weeks-months) carry the information; 1-5 day spikes do NOT predict (short sellers shifted from short-term private info to slow public/anomaly information).
key_papers: Wang, Yan, Zheng (2020), Journal of Financial Economics 135:191-212, 'Shorting flows, public disclosure, and market efficiency' — 2010-2015 with REAL-TIME public FINRA data: high-minus-low shorting quintile = -12.6%/yr FF3 alpha EW (t=6.00), -6.0%/yr VW (t=4.03) over days 2-21; large-cap VW spread 1.3bp/day (t=2.17), 2.2bp/day EW (t=4.95); predictability decays slowly, lasts ~1 year; low-shorting quintile has the significant positive alpha; abnormal SHORT-term flows have no predictive power

Diether, Lee, Werner (2009), Review of Financial Studies 22(2):575-607 — public Reg SHO data 2005: +10pp short share of volume -> -0.94%/mo (NYSE) / -0.72%/mo (Nasdaq); low-minus-high daily-shorting strategy ~1.39-1.41%/mo abnormal
Boehmer, Jones, Zhang (2008), Journal of Finance 63(2) — proprietary NYSE shorting flow: heavily shorted underperform ~1.16%/mo risk-adjusted (the day 2-21 design WYZ replicate on public data)
findings.effect_size_net: For a large/liquid high-beta 50-name universe, the relevant magnitude is the WYZ large-cap VW figure: ~1.3-2.2bp/day (~3-5.5%/yr) quintile spread, of which the long-only-capturable half (low-shorting tilt) is ~1.5-3%/yr gross on the tilted sleeve. Used as a cross-sectional feature/tilt inside the existing top-7 entry ranking it adds ZERO incremental round trips, so net ~= gross x post-publication haircut. Applying a 50% post-pub haircut: roughly +0.5-1.5%/yr at book level. Signal horizon (weeks-year) is far longer than the 11bps+spread cost scale of existing trades — cost-viability is not the binding constraint; signal-vs-noise at hourly entries is, hence use as ranking feature/tilt, not a standalone trigger.
findings.decay_evidence: This is the rare signal whose flagship study IS the post-disclosure replication: WYZ 2020 shows the DLW/BJZ effect SURVIVED real-time public dissemination (2010-2015) at roughly half the 2005-2007 magnitude, with the horizon lengthening — consistent with McLean-Pontiff ~50% post-publication decay already realized. Supporting recent work: 'Surprise in short interest' (Journal of Financial Markets, 2023) finds short-positioning surprises still price-relevant. Known caveats: FINRA daily files cover only off-exchange (TRF/ADF/ORF) prints and include market-maker liquidity shorts — mitigate by z-scoring each name's short-volume ratio against its own trailing distribution and using 21d+ windows (exactly the construction WYZ validate); 2021 squeeze episodes argue for using it long-only (avoid/underweight heavily-shorted, prefer lightly-shorted) rather than as a short signal.
findings.free_data_source: VERIFIED LIVE: https://cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/CNMSshvolYYYYMMDD.txt (pipe-delimited: Date|Symbol|ShortVolume|ShortExemptVolume|TotalVolume|Market) — published same day after regular trading hours (per WYZ fn.2: 'typically on the same day of trading... in rare instances during the next business day'); never materially revised; FREE BACKFILL to Aug 2009, so the LSTM/LGBM panel can be trained point-in-time immediately. PIT rule: data for day T usable from T+1 open (assume evening publication).
findings.build_sketch: New short_flow.py mirroring funding_archive.py pattern: nightly job (after 18:30 ET) curls CNMSshvol file, filters to ~96-name training panel, appends to parquet (~50KB/day). Compute per-name SVR_21 = 21d sum(ShortVolume)/sum(TotalVolume), z vs own 252d history, plus GKX-style cross-sectional rank into panel_ranks.py. Wire as LGBM/LSTM feature (backfill to 2009 = full training history) and as a soft tilt in the top-7 entry ranker (penalize top-quintile z, bonus bottom-quintile). Daily cadence feeding hourly decisions. Jetson cost: one 5-10MB download + pandas groupby, <30s/day, no model-memory impact.

findings.name: Aggregate Short Interest Index (SII) as slow market-exposure overlay
findings.mechanism: Aggregate short interest is informed positioning at the market level: short sellers anticipate aggregate cash-flow news (RRZ's VAR decomposition attributes the predictability predominantly to a cash-flow channel, not discount-rate noise). High detrended aggregate short interest = informed pessimism -> lower future market returns; it is a CONTINUOUS slow signal (not contrarian-at-extremes — it trades WITH the smart money), complementary to the app's price-based SPY 200d filter and VIX ladder because it is positioning-based and orthogonal to realized price/vol.
key_papers: Rapach, Ringgenberg, Zhou (2016), Journal of Financial Economics 121(1):46-65, 'Short interest and aggregate stock returns' — 'arguably the strongest known predictor of aggregate stock returns' 1973-2014: annual-horizon R2 12.89% in-sample, 13.24% out-of-sample; beats 14 Goyal-Welch predictors; >300bps/yr certainty-equivalent gain (CXO's independent read: 3.5-4.6%/yr CE gains 1990-2012 OOS)

Priestley (2019, SSRN wp 3384620) 'Short Interest, Macroeconomic Variables and Aggregate Stock Returns' — critique: SII's predictive content overlaps macro-state variables (relevant since the app already has macro/regime layers)
CXO Advisory independent replication — confirms negative OOS relation but shows gains concentrated in late-1990s and 2008-09, underperformance 1990-95 and 2000-07: expect lumpy, regime-like payoff
findings.effect_size_net: As a +/-20% gross-exposure scalar on the existing book (no new trades, just sizing existing entries), a 300-460bps/yr CE gain for a full market-timer realistically dilutes to ~30-80bps/yr at this app's tilt size, essentially cost-free since turnover at entry time is unchanged. Twice-monthly update cadence matches the data; this is strictly an overlay-cadence signal — useless at hourly horizon by construction.
findings.decay_evidence: Published 2016; OOS evidence inside the paper is genuine (recursive estimation 1990-2014) but post-2014 live evidence is thin and CXO documents episode-concentration; Priestley argues macro-overlap, which for this app means: expect partial redundancy with the existing HMM/VIX/FOMC layers and size accordingly (use as one vote, not a hard gate). Ringgenberg maintains a free updated SII through 2021-12 (matthewringgenberg.com/data, Google Drive link) — use it to validate the home-built series before going live. CRITICAL implementation trap: detrending must be RECURSIVE (expanding-window), never full-sample, or the backtest inherits look-ahead.
findings.free_data_source: VERIFIED: FINRA Equity Short Interest files (finra.org/finra-data/browse-catalog/equity-short-interest/data; OTC + exchange-listed), twice monthly, settlement dates ~15th and month-end; firms report T+2; FINRA PUBLISHES ON THE 7TH BUSINESS DAY AFTER SETTLEMENT (verified examples: Nov 14 settle -> Nov 25 publish; Dec 31 -> Jan 12). Values not revised. PIT rule: each observation usable only from its publication date (~9-12 calendar days after settlement). Aggregate construction: sum shares short across universe / shares outstanding (or share volume), log, recursively detrend, z-score. Backfill: Ringgenberg's free SII 1973-2021 + FINRA files (5 rolling years on site) stitched.
findings.build_sketch: Extend macro_indicators.py: biweekly fetch of FINRA short interest file on publication dates, compute universe-aggregate SI ratio, expanding-window detrend, z-score; expose sii_z to the existing sizing stack (portfolio.py) as a gross multiplier in [0.8, 1.2] (clip at |z|=2), one vote alongside VIX ladder/HMM with explicit correlation monitoring vs those gates. Jetson cost: trivial (one CSV, vectorized ops, runs twice a month).

findings.name: Per-name option/stock volume ratio (O/S) from free Cboe per-symbol files — collect-forward bearish-flow veto, later a model feature
findings.mechanism: When short-selling is costly, informed traders with NEGATIVE information migrate to options, so high option-volume-relative-to-stock-volume predicts low future returns even WITHOUT signed/open-buy data (this is the answer to the Pan-Poteshman signed-data objection: Johnson-So derive and validate the unsigned construction; Ge-Lin-Pearson confirm with signed data that the O/S effect loads on short-sale-constraint-driven put trading). High-beta momentum names pre-earnings/news are exactly where this flow concentrates — complements the existing earnings/8-K gates with a flow-based early warning.
key_papers: Johnson, So (2012), Journal of Financial Economics 106(2):262-286, 'The option to stock volume ratio and future returns' — lowest O/S decile outperforms highest by 0.34%/WEEK (19.3% annualized); stronger when short-sale costs high; O/S predicts firm-specific earnings news

Ge, Lin, Pearson (2016), Journal of Financial Economics 120(3) 'Why does the option to stock volume ratio predict stock returns?' — signed-data confirmation of mechanism; predictability tied to opening positions consistent with constrained informed trading

Pan, Poteshman (2006), Review of Financial Studies 19(3) — signed put/call ratios predict (~40bps/week initially) but PUBLICLY OBSERVABLE unsigned put/call has much weaker/insignificant power — which also KILLS the index-level equity-only P/C timing overlay (corroborated by later studies finding public PCR statistically insignificant for index forecasting); per-name O/S is the only public-data construction with top-journal support
findings.effect_size_net: JS gross 19.3%/yr decile L/S; apply McLean-Pontiff ~50% post-pub haircut -> ~8-10%/yr L/S, of which a long-only AVOID gate (skip entries in the top O/S-z decile of the universe that hour/day) captures a small but nearly free slice — realistically tens of bps/yr of avoided losses on ~50 names with zero added turnover (it only blocks/delays entries, like the existing meta-label veto). Not separately tradable at this scale; value is loss-avoidance + later feature value.
findings.decay_evidence: O/S survives in open replication libraries (Chen-Zimmermann open-source asset pricing) with attenuated but significant post-sample alpha; GLP 2016 is effectively an in-family replication. Honest constraint found in live verification: Cboe's per-symbol endpoint serves CURRENT-DAY data only (the dt= parameter is ignored — verified by requesting 2022/2024 dates and receiving identical current-day rows), so there is NO free historical backfill of per-name option volume: the signal must be collected forward (~6 months before the gate is validatable on own data, ~1-2 years before it earns a model-feature slot). Coverage caveat: Cboe C1 endpoint verified working (C2/BZX/EDGX market codes need confirming during build); Cboe exchanges ~30% of US options volume — cross-sectionally informative but a noisy subset of OPRA totals (OCC batch endpoint verified to be aggregate-only, no per-symbol history).
findings.free_data_source: VERIFIED LIVE: https://www.cboe.com/us/options/market_statistics/symbol_data/csv/?mkt=cone — per-contract rows (Symbol, Call/Put, Expiration, Strike, Volume) for Cboe C1, free, no auth; snapshot of current day -> archive daily after close (PIT-clean going forward, like the app's existing oi_archive.py crypto collection). Stock volume denominator from Alpaca bars. Market-level equity-only P/C (currently published daily at cboe.com/us/options/market_statistics/daily/, legacy CSV archive 2006-2019 at cdn.cboe.com/resources/options/volume_and_call_put_ratios/equitypc.csv) is available but REJECTED as a timing overlay per the evidence above.
findings.build_sketch: New cboe_options_archive.py cloned from oi_archive.py: daily ~16:35 ET pull of symbol_data CSV(s), aggregate to per-underlying call_vol/put_vol for the ~96-name panel, append parquet (filtered, <100KB/day). Compute O/S = (call+put)/stock_volume and per-name z vs trailing 60d; after 6 months' collection, enable entry veto: block new entries when O/S-z > +2 AND put-share elevated (belt-and-suspenders with existing earnings gate); after 12-24 months, promote O/S-z and put-share to LGBM features through the standard challenger/DM-HLN path. Jetson: one CSV parse/day, negligible.

findings.name: AAII bull-bear spread (+ NAAIM cross-check) extreme-pessimism contrarian sizing overlay
findings.mechanism: Survey expectations are extrapolative (formed from past returns), so EXTREMES mark crowd positioning limits: when individual-investor bearishness is at multi-sigma extremes, marginal selling is exhausted and subsequent 3-12 month returns are above average. Greenwood-Shleifer show survey expectations (including AAII) correlate positively with past returns/flows and NEGATIVELY with subsequent realized 12m returns — the relation is real but slow and ASYMMETRIC: bearish extremes (fear) are a materially better contrarian signal than bullish extremes (greed). In the middle of the range the spread carries ~no information — map it as extreme-only, never continuous.
key_papers: Greenwood, Shleifer (2014), Review of Financial Studies 27(3):714-746 'Expectations of Returns and Expected Returns' — six survey expectation series incl. AAII: highly correlated with each other, with past returns and inflows, and NEGATIVELY with subsequent ~12m returns; rejects rational-expectations mapping; the rigorous foundation for contrarian use

Fisher, Statman (2000), Financial Analysts Journal 56(2) 'Investor Sentiment and Stock Returns' — AAII individual sentiment negatively related to subsequent S&P returns; statistically significant but LOW R2 (a few % at monthly horizon)

Brown, Cliff (2004), Journal of Empirical Finance 11(1) — sentiment co-moves with contemporaneous returns but has LITTLE NEAR-TERM (weekly/monthly) predictive power; their 2005 Journal of Business follow-up finds the payoff at 1-3 YEAR horizons — i.e., this is strictly an overlay, never a trade-cadence signal
findings.effect_size_net: Honest sizing: at |z|>=1.5-2 extremes (bull-bear spread below ~-20pp historically), subsequent 6-12m S&P returns run above unconditional averages, but conditional edges are single-digit annualized percent on the timed notional and the 2022 episode (spread <-41%, 2.6 sigma, for months) delivered UNDERWHELMING 1-year forward returns — so cap the lever at +/-10-15% gross. Implemented as a sizing scalar (and as a 'faster re-risk after macro standdown' permission), incremental trading cost ~0; realistic contribution: tens of bps/yr with low variance added. Skip the bullish-extreme de-risk leg or weight it half (weaker side per the asymmetry evidence).
findings.decay_evidence: Never a published 'anomaly' with alpha to decay — it is a weak-but-stable conditional relation that survived 38 years of free publication, which is itself informative (no crowding because the edge is too slow/small for funds). Documented failures: 2022 (extreme fear, weak forward returns in a rate-shock regime — argues for combining with the existing VIX/HMM regime state rather than standalone). NAAIM (manager equity exposure, weekly since 2006) has essentially NO peer-reviewed support — use only as a confirming z-score, never alone. RELATED DOMAIN KILLS (verified this wave, do not build): CFTC TFF e-mini asset-manager/leveraged-fund positioning — only weak/dated support (De Roon et al. 2000 JF hedging pressure; Wang 2003; one mid-tier JIFMIM 2013 study), 3-day publication lag, structural basis-trade contamination of leveraged-fund shorts, and the late-2025 shutdown created a multi-week COT publication gap (a live PIT hazard); Google Trends FEARS (Da-Engelberg-Gao 2015 RFS, daily fear -> 2-day reversal, 2004-2011) — pytrends archived 4/17/2025, official Trends API still alpha/waitlisted (launched 7/24/2025), and per-download rescaling/sampling noise (Eichenauer et al. 2022, Economic Inquiry) makes point-in-time backtest reconstruction impossible -> rejected on implementability; ICI weekly flows — Ben-Rephael-Kandel-Wohl 2012 JFE net-exchanges reversal (1 SD ~ 1.95% contemporaneous, 85% reversed in 4 months) is real but the predictive variable is MONTHLY net exchanges published with ~1-month lag, and the weekly ICI estimate is a different variable -> rejected.
findings.free_data_source: AAII: survey runs Thu-Wed, results published Thursday morning ET, values NEVER revised — so historical backfill from any mirror is PIT-safe if each weekly value is timestamped to its Thursday release (direct aaii.com sentiment XLS now returns 403/registration-gated — capture weekly from the public release going forward + one-time mirror backfill, e.g., the widely-mirrored sentiment.xls copies on GitHub, validated against published values). NAAIM: VERIFIED free Excel 'data since inception' at naaim.org/programs/naaim-exposure-index/, Wednesday survey -> Thursday posting (verified 'Posted on Thursday, June 11, 2026'). PIT rule for both: usable from Thursday close / Friday open.
findings.build_sketch: Extend macro_indicators.py (or new sentiment_surveys.py): weekly Thursday-evening job ingests AAII bull/bear/neutral + NAAIM number; compute spread z vs expanding history; expose survey_fear_z to sizing: if z <= -1.5 AND existing regime gates not in standdown -> gross multiplier up to 1.10-1.15 and permit faster re-entry after FOMC/CPI standdowns; if z >= +2 -> 0.90. Weekly overlay cadence only. Jetson: trivial (two small files/week).

findings.name: Per-name short interest ratio / days-to-cover spike gate (biweekly FINRA positions file)
findings.mechanism: Stock-level short INTEREST (positions, not flow) is the slow-moving complement to finding #1: persistently high short-interest-ratio/days-to-cover names underperform because divergence-of-opinion plus constraints keep prices above fundamentals (Miller overpricing), while LOW short interest is positive news ('good news in short interest'). For a long-only high-beta book the use is defensive: do not initiate new longs into names where informed short positioning has spiked, EXCEPT when the spike is squeeze-prone (2021 regime) — hence gate on level+change with a days-to-cover cap, not a return forecast.
key_papers: Asquith, Pathak, Ritter (2005), Journal of Financial Economics 78(2) — high short-interest-ratio (esp. with low institutional ownership) stocks underperform ~ -1%+/mo in the constrained tail

Boehmer, Huszar, Jordan (2010), Journal of Financial Economics 96(1) 'The good news in short interest' — lightly-shorted stocks earn significantly POSITIVE abnormal returns (the long-only-relevant leg), large and liquid names included

Hong, Li, Ni, Scheinkman, Yan (2015), NBER WP 21166 'Days to Cover and Stock Returns' — DTC (short interest / average daily volume) is the better cross-sectional sort than raw SI ratio (~1.2%/mo L/S), rationalized by crowded-trade unwind risk
findings.effect_size_net: Gate-only economics: blocking new entries in the top-decile DTC/SIR-z slice of a 50-name universe touches few candidate entries, costs zero turnover, and avoids the most squeeze/unwind-prone longs; expected contribution is small (est. 10-40bps/yr avoided drawdown contribution) but the marginal build cost is ~zero because it reuses finding #2's fetcher and file. Net-positive at any scale; never use as a standalone alpha at this cadence.
findings.decay_evidence: Cross-sectional short-interest predictors show the standard ~50% post-publication attenuation (McLean-Pontiff 2016 JF; Chen-Zimmermann replications; decay estimates rise to ~72% excluding pre-2005 data — Jensen et al./post-2022 work), and the short LEG carries 2021-style squeeze regime risk — which is precisely why this is shipped as an avoid-gate on fresh longs rather than an alpha tilt. The low-SI positive-alpha leg (BHJ 2010) is the part a long-only book monetizes and it is the more robust leg in replications.
findings.free_data_source: Same VERIFIED file as finding #2: FINRA Equity Short Interest (twice monthly; settlement 15th/EOM; firms report T+2; PUBLISHED 7th business day after settlement — verified Nov 14 -> Nov 25, Dec 31 -> Jan 12; 5 rolling years downloadable; values effectively unrevised). Per-name fields: shares short, avg daily volume, days to cover. PIT rule: usable from publication date only (~9-12 calendar days after settlement) — model this lag explicitly in the panel join.
findings.build_sketch: Reuse the finding-#2 fetcher in macro_indicators.py/short_flow.py: on each publication date, join per-name DTC and SIR into the panel keyed by publication date (not settlement date); compute z vs own 2y history + cross-sectional rank; entry gate in stock_loop.py: skip new entries when DTC-z > 2 OR (SIR-z > 2 AND ΔSI > 0 across last two reports); expose same fields to LGBM as slow features (backfillable point-in-time from the 5-year file archive + settlement/publication calendar). Biweekly overlay cadence feeding the hourly entry stack. Jetson: trivial.

findings.name: Pooled-panel HAR/HExp realized-volatility engine from own hourly bars, replacing per-name hourly EGARCH(1,1) for position sizing and stop calibration
findings.mechanism: Volatility is highly persistent with long-memory-like decay. A day of intraday squared returns plus the overnight gap is a far less noisy daily volatility observation than the single daily (or per-hour) return that GARCH filters, and the HAR/HExp cascade of daily/weekly/monthly components approximates long memory that GARCH(1,1)'s single exponential decay cannot (it over-reacts short-run, under-persists long-run). Second mechanism, directly relevant to a 50-96 name panel with short histories on a Jetson: normalized vol dynamics are nearly identical across assets (Bollerslev et al. 2018, Fig. 3), so POOLING the regression coefficients across the panel (after 'centering' each name by its expanding long-run mean RV) slashes estimation variance — out-of-sample the pooled model beats per-name estimation even though it loses in-sample. This is a bias-variance argument, not an anomaly, so there is no arbitrage channel to erode it.
key_papers: Corsi (2009), J. Financial Econometrics 7(2):174-196 — HAR-RV: daily+weekly+monthly RV lags; the standard benchmark that reduced-form RV models beat GARCH/SV forecasts.
Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold, Labys (2003), Econometrica 71(2):579-625 — simple autoregressions on realized volatility dominate GARCH out-of-sample.

Bollerslev, Hood, Huss, Pedersen (2018), Review of Financial Studies 31(7):2729-2773 — 58 assets: for EQUITIES, 20-day-ahead OOS R^2 = 8.1% for daily-squared-return models, 25.6% for 21-day rolling RV, 41.2% individually-estimated HAR, 45.8% PANEL HAR, 48.3-50.7% HExp (mixture of 4 EWMAs, centers-of-mass 1/5/25/125d), 53.8% panel HExpGl; mega-pooling cuts forecast variance ~30%; in-/out-of-sample ranking of individual-vs-panel REVERSES OOS; realized-utility value of the risk model: 48bps/yr vs best static, 19bps/yr vs daily-data risk models, 8bps/yr vs 21-day RV (SR=0.4, gamma=2, 20% vol target), net of transaction costs; HExp forecasts churn far less (AC1 of daily forecast changes -0.01 vs -0.21 for HAR).

Hansen, Lunde (2005), J. Applied Econometrics 20(7):873-889 — GARCH(1,1) is unbeatable on daily data alone but loses decisively once intraday RV information is used (the precise reason our hourly bars are an unexploited asset).
Liu, Patton, Sheppard (2015), J. Econometrics 187(1):293-311 — across ~400 estimators and 31 assets, simple RV is extremely hard to beat: license to keep the estimator simple.
Clements, Preve (2021), J. Banking & Finance 133:106285 — practitioner replication: HAR robust across markets; WLS/log transforms and forecast 'insanity filters' materially improve plain OLS-HAR.
findings.effect_size_net: At our scale the gain arrives through three channels, all near-zero-cost: (1) risk-targeting accuracy — BHHP's utility metric puts panel-HExp ~19bps/yr of wealth over daily-return-based models (GARCH/EWMA class) at a 20% vol target, measured net of realistic t-costs; our stock book is intraday-only so pro-rate down, order 5-15bps/yr, but it stacks with (2) churn reduction: smoother forecasts mean the 0.5-1.5x sizing clamp flips less often, saving rebalancing round-trips at ~11bps+spread each; and (3) stop quality: forward-looking sigma for stop width instead of backward ATR/EGARCH reduces premature stop-outs (each avoided stop-out+re-entry saves ~15-25bps). HONEST sampling caveat: with M≈7 RTH hourly returns/day, per-day relative SE of RV is sqrt(2/M)·sqrt(IQ)/IV ≈ 55-90% — the daily lag will be attenuated; the weekly (~33 obs, the same quality as French-Schwert-Stambaugh 1987 monthly-from-daily) and monthly (~145 obs) components carry most signal. This still strictly dominates the GARCH information set (7 obs/day + gap vs 1/day). For crypto (24 bars/day, 168/week) the upgrade is full-strength and unambiguous.
findings.decay_evidence: Not a traded anomaly — no McLean-Pontiff decay channel; vol forecastability is a statistical property that replications keep confirming post-publication: Liu-Patton-Sheppard 2015 (400 estimators), BHHP 2018 (58 assets, net of costs), Clements-Preve 2021, Christensen-Siggaard-Veliyev 2023 (J. Financial Econometrics: ML models beat HAR only modestly, gains concentrated in high-vol episodes — HAR remains the benchmark). Adversarial evidence on the SIZING use specifically: Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang, Yan (2020, JFE 138(1):95-117) show Moreira-Muir style vol-managed PORTFOLIOS often fail real-time utility tests across 103 factor portfolios — but that critique targets return-enhancement claims from leverage timing; our use is two-sided risk targeting with clamps, exactly the BHHP realized-utility setting that survived net of costs.

findings.name: Signed semivariance asymmetry and jump non-persistence (SHAR + MedRV/bipower split) for stop width and post-shock sizing — fixes the post-gap ATR/GARCH ratchet
findings.mechanism: Two robust facts the current ATR/EGARCH stack ignores. (1) Sign asymmetry: future volatility loads on the DOWNSIDE semivariance of past returns; upside variation — especially positive jumps — predicts LOWER future vol (uncertainty resolution), while negative jumps predict higher vol (risk-off feedback, margin/hedging flows). (2) Jump non-persistence: the jump component of realized variance is close to serially unpredictable; only the continuous (diffusive) component cascades forward. ATR-14 and EGARCH both integrate a one-off gap into their level for days-weeks, so after an up-gap the system sets stops too wide and positions too small on a name whose diffusive vol never changed, and after a down-gap it does the reverse (stops too tight is the dangerous side). Example arithmetic: a single 5% news gap in a 2%-ATR name inflates 14-bar ATR ~20-30% for ~2 weeks; with atr_stop_mult 2.0-2.5 that moves the stop distance by the same factor in exactly the wrong cases.
key_papers: Patton, Sheppard (2015), Review of Economics and Statistics 97(3):683-697 — realized semivariances (RS-, RS+) for S&P 500 + 105 individual stocks: future vol driven by RS-; negative jumps raise, positive jumps LOWER future vol; SHAR significantly beats HAR OOS.

Bollerslev, Patton, Quaedvlieg (2016), J. Econometrics 192(1):1-18, Table 13 replication — S&P 500 SHAR coefficients: beta1- = 1.128 (s.e. 0.277) vs beta1+ = -0.373 (s.e. 0.177): the downside lag carries ~3x the (opposite-signed) weight; HAR-J jump coefficient -1.00 (jumps subtracted from next-day vol expectations); jump terms significant for 60% of DJIA names; SHAR OOS QLIKE ratio vs HAR on S&P = 0.9375 (RW), ~parity on single names.

Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold (2007), Review of Economics and Statistics 89(4):701-720 — HAR-CJ decomposition: jump component largely unpredictable; continuous bipower component is what forecasts vol.
Barndorff-Nielsen, Shephard (2004), J. Financial Econometrics 2(1):1-37 and (2006) 4(1):1-30 — bipower variation and the jump test foundations.

Andersen, Dobrev, Schaumburg (2012), J. Econometrics 169(1):75-93 — MedRV nearest-neighbor truncation: the jump-robust estimator with the best finite-sample behavior at LOW sampling frequency, which is exactly our regime.
Barndorff-Nielsen, Kinnebrock, Shephard (2010, Volatility and Time Series Econometrics, OUP) — realized semivariance estimator itself.
findings.effect_size_net: Forecast-loss gains from SHAR per se are modest on single names (BPQ Table 4: ~par to 1% loss reduction; ~6% QLIKE on the index), but the coefficient asymmetry (1.13 vs -0.37) is strongly significant and stable, and the operational payoff at our scale is in the EXIT stack, not the forecast horse-race: (a) stop widths keyed to jump-robust MedRV-based vol + a separate gap term stop ratcheting after one-off jumps — every premature stop-out avoided saves a ~15-25bps round trip (11bps RT cost + spread) plus foregone edge, and the high-beta universe gaps constantly; (b) post-down-jump the same logic correctly WIDENS stops/cuts size when vol genuinely rises. Costs: zero new data, a few extra columns in the pooled OLS. HONEST estimation constraint: at M≈7/day, per-day RS-/RS+/MedRV are too noisy — compute over trailing 5-day windows of hourly bars (~33 obs), which is sufficient for the weekly-cadence asymmetry that drives the effect; crypto gets clean daily semivariances at 24 bars/day.
findings.decay_evidence: Same non-anomaly status as HAR — replicated rather than arbitraged: BPQ 2016 independently replicate SHAR on S&P + 27 DJIA names; the leverage-effect/semivariance asymmetry is confirmed across asset classes in subsequent literature (e.g., Bollerslev, Li, Zhao 2020 JFQA 'Good volatility, bad volatility and the cross-section of stock returns' extends signed-vol pricing cross-sectionally); jump non-persistence (ABD 2007) has held in every major HAR-CJ replication including BPQ's CHAR results. No post-publication sign flips reported.

findings.name: Overnight-specific gap-volatility model for the overnight sleeve — size the only uncontrollable risk segment on its own conditional distribution
findings.mechanism: Overnight is a structurally different stochastic process from intraday: no continuous trading, so 'vol' is discrete news arrival resolved at the opening auction; overnight returns are extremely fat-tailed (Bouchaud et al. find near-infinite kurtosis) and have their OWN clustering channel — past overnight shocks feed future overnight vol strongly but intraday vol only weakly, while intraday vol feeds both. A total-vol estimate (current: EGARCH on hourly returns, ATR stops) therefore systematically mis-measures gap risk, and heterogeneously across names (overnight share of close-to-close variance runs ~15-35% for liquid large-caps and varies by name/news exposure; French-Roll: open-to-close variance ~6x weekend close-to-open). Decisive operational point: the sleeve's GTC stop CANNOT control gap risk — a stop fills at/after the open, past the gap — so position size is the only overnight risk control, and it is currently set from intraday-vol logic (stock_loop.py sleeve keeps up to 2 names at up to 5% equity each, GTC stop at an ATR multiple, stock_loop.py:405).
key_papers: French, Roll (1986), J. Financial Economics 17(1):5-26 — trading-time vs non-trading-time variance: per-hour variance during trading vastly exceeds overnight; the foundational ON/ID split, never overturned in 40 years.

Blanc, Chicheportiche, Bouchaud (2014), Physica A 402:58-75 — intraday/overnight ARCH decomposition on US stocks: overnight returns strongly feed future OVERNIGHT vol but weakly intraday vol; intraday feeds both; overnight returns have ~infinite kurtosis; the ID/ON model significantly beats standard ARCH out-of-sample — total-vol models mix two different processes.

Linton, Wu (2020), J. Econometrics (S0304407619302601) — incorporating overnight and intraday returns separately into (multivariate) GARCH improves daily vol forecasts; overnight decompositions raise predictive ability.

Hansen, Lunde (2005), J. Financial Econometrics 3(4):525-554 — optimal combination of overnight squared return and intraday RV for whole-day variance (with BHHP 2018 footnote 6 honesty: for WHOLE-DAY risk, simply adding the gap^2 is not dominated — our target here is different: the conditional ON segment itself).

Lou, Polk, Skouras (2019), J. Financial Economics 134(1):192-213 — the overnight/intraday return decomposition the sleeve is already built on (cited in strategy_config.py); confirms ON/ID are economically distinct (clientele mechanism).
Patton-Sheppard (2015) asymmetry (above) applies to gaps too: down-gaps raise subsequent vol, up-gaps do not.
findings.effect_size_net: This is a risk-correctness fix with ~zero added trading: sleeve names with the same total vol differ up to ~1.5-2x in conditional gap sigma (sqrt of a 15-35% overnight-share spread), so sizing on total vol mis-sizes overnight risk by 30-60% per name and ranks the wrong keepers. At sleeve scale (<=2 names x 5% equity), correct sizing/keeper-ranking cuts the tail of overnight book damage materially (the q05 overnight move on a high-beta name is multiple percent even off earnings nights) while preserving the Lou-Polk-Skouras premium the sleeve harvests; expected cost: none beyond replacing the ranking/cap inputs in decisions already being made. Honest caveat: one gap observation per night means the per-name conditional model must lean on pooled/panel estimation and EWMA aggregation (60-90d half-lives) — fine, because the cross-name pooled standardized-gap distribution is exactly what sizes the fat tail.
findings.decay_evidence: The ON/ID variance split is microstructure, not an anomaly: French-Roll (1986) has replicated for four decades across markets; the recent ON/ID modeling literature (Bouchaud et al. 2014; Linton-Wu 2020; multiple HAR-with-overnight papers) consistently finds separate dynamics. The RETURN side (overnight premium) is the part with post-publication controversy (tug-of-war profitability shrank post-2019 publication) — but the sleeve already exists; this finding only fixes its RISK model, which does not depend on the premium persisting.

findings.name: HARQ-style measurement-error attenuation: realized-quarticity (vol-of-vol) driven shrinkage of the daily RV lag — the estimation-risk haircut
findings.mechanism: RV = IV + measurement error with conditional error variance 2*Delta*IQ (Barndorff-Nielsen-Shephard asymptotics), so the RV autoregression suffers TIME-VARYING errors-in-variables attenuation: on days when RV is precisely measured it should be trusted (high effective persistence), on noisy days the forecast should shrink toward the weekly/monthly components. HARQ implements this with one interaction term: beta1_t = beta1 + beta1Q * RQ_{t-1}^{1/2}, beta1Q < 0, where RQ = (M/3) * sum r^4 proxies the error variance. This is MOST conceptually valuable exactly where measurement error is largest — our M≈7 hourly-bar regime — and it doubles as a principled 'estimation-risk haircut' on sizing: trust noisy vol estimates less, default toward the slow components.
key_papers: Bollerslev, Patton, Quaedvlieg (2016), J. Econometrics 192(1):1-18 — S&P 500: average beta1 rises 0.227 (HAR) to 0.602 (HARQ) with beta1Q=-0.36 (t~-5.7); OOS vs HAR across 27 DJIA stocks: avg MSE ratio 0.935 (rolling) / 0.953 (increasing), QLIKE 0.990/0.949; HARQ significantly beats ALL benchmarks (AR, HAR, HAR-J, CHAR, SHAR, ARQ, HARQ-F) for 44% (5% level) / 63% (10%) of stocks under MSE; gains largest for assets with the most heteroskedastic measurement error.

BPQ 2016 simulations (Table 1, Fig. 3) — THE honesty constraint: gains are U-shaped in observations/day, maximized at 2-10 minute sampling; at M=39 OOS gains persist (MSE 0.988, QLIKE 0.968) but shrink as M falls because RQ itself degrades; their simulation grid stops at 13 obs/day — our M≈7 is BELOW the tested range, so sign-preservation is plausible (the attenuation logic is frequency-free) but magnitude is unproven.

BPQ 2016 Table 11 — RQ-estimator robustness: the wild BOOTSTRAP variance of RV is the only alternative that systematically improves on raw RQ (ratios 0.993-1.000); RQ^{1/2} is the most stable transformation (Table 12); insanity filter (Swanson-White 1997) mandatory.
Hansen, Lunde (2014), Econometric Theory 30(1):60-93 — instrumented persistence of latent IV ~0.95 vs ~0.65 measured: the attenuation being corrected is enormous at coarse sampling.
Bollerslev, Patton, Quaedvlieg (2016b, J. Econometrics 'Modeling and forecasting (un)reliable realized covariances') — same logic extends to covariance/ENB inputs later if desired.
findings.effect_size_net: Expect low-single-digit percent forecast-loss reduction at our sampling (extrapolating BPQ's U-shape below their tested floor — claimed honestly as a hypothesis to be validated, not an established result), PLUS a second-order benefit that is certain: HARQ-type shrinkage makes forecasts more stable on noisy days, which reduces sizing churn through the 0.5-1.5x clamp (each avoided flip-flop saves rebalancing cost at ~11bps+spread on the traded slice). Implementation cost is one regressor and one filter; if the DSR holdout shows nothing at stock M≈7, keep it for crypto (M=24, comfortably inside BPQ's validated range) where gains should approach their reported magnitudes.

Forecasting; Clements-Preve 2021 include Q-corrections among robust improvements; BPQ's own covariance follow-up). As a statistical correction it has no arbitrage decay channel. The known failure mode is documented by the authors themselves: HARQ-F (all lags adjusted) overfits on ~1000-observation windows — use the simple HARQ only.

findings.name: Post-jump continuation tilt: jump returns (especially overnight gaps) as information-shock underreaction features for entry conditioning
findings.mechanism: Large discrete price moves are information events (news), and limited investor attention causes UNDERreaction to them: stocks drift in the direction of the jump for weeks, the opposite of the mean-reversion that diffusive overbought/oversold moves exhibit. For our long-only top-7 ranker the operational risk today is that reversal-flavored features (ROD_Ret, RSI/BB/Stoch) mark a just-gapped-up name as overbought and push it out of the entry set precisely when it carries continuation edge — and symmetric: a gapped-DOWN name can look attractively 'oversold' while it still carries negative drift. A jump/gap feature lets LightGBM separate jump moves (continuation) from diffusive moves (reversal-prone). This complements finding 3, which handles the VOL consequences of jumps; this one handles the RETURN consequences.
key_papers: Jiang, Zhu (2017), J. Financial Economics 124(1):43-64 — jumps as info-shock proxies; decile portfolios long positive- / short negative-jump-return stocks earn significantly positive returns over 1-3 month horizons; INTRADAY and especially OVERNIGHT jumps carry the effect; robust to firm characteristics, distinct from and beyond earnings surprises (we already gate earnings — this is the non-earnings news residual: 8-Ks we miss, analyst actions, product news); attention mechanism.

Jiang, Li, Wang (2021), J. Financial Economics 141(2):573-599, 'Pervasive underreaction: Evidence from high-frequency data' — post-publication confirmation that high-frequency-identified information arrival is systematically underreacted to.

Lee, Mykland (2008), Review of Financial Studies 21(6):2535-2563 — the nonparametric jump statistic |r_i| / sqrt(local BV): directly usable at hourly frequency for 24/7 crypto; for stocks at M≈7 the operative and most powerful jump test is simply the standardized overnight gap (gap_z), since most single-name jumps occur overnight.
Patton-Sheppard (2015) (finding 3) — independent corroboration that up-jumps and down-jumps have asymmetric aftermaths.
findings.effect_size_net: Jiang-Zhu report significant 1-3 month decile long-short returns (economically meaningful in their 1993-2013 sample; the published abstract does not pin a single headline number and I will not invent one — the portable content for us is the SIGN and ranking monotonicity, not the level). For a long-only hourly system the realistic harvest is modest and indirect: not a standalone rule but a feature that (a) stops the ranker from systematically fading fresh up-jumps and (b) suppresses 'oversold' entries into post-down-jump drift. Cost: zero new data; effect must clear the existing triple-barrier label fit + DSR holdout to ship, which is exactly the right bar for a return-side feature with decay risk. Expected contribution if it validates: a small hit-rate improvement concentrated on jump days, which in a high-beta universe is a non-trivial fraction of days.
findings.decay_evidence: This one IS exposed to McLean-Pontiff decay (published 2017; M-P average post-publication decay ~32% for return predictors, and attention-based effects decay as attention technology improves). Mitigants: Jiang-Li-Wang 2021 confirms the underreaction channel out-of-sample post-2017; the effect is a drift/continuation phenomenon (costly to arbitrage in size on illiquid jumpy names, the M-P persistence condition); and our use is defensive (don't fade jumps) rather than harvesting the full L/S spread, so even a half-decayed effect retains value. Treated as the lowest-confidence, gated-by-validation finding here by design.

Zero publication lag; point-in-time by construction (uses only closed bars and pre-announced corporate-action factors).

fatal_flaws: CLAIMED NET EFFECT (40-80bps/mo on sleeve capital) is refuted AS SPECIFIED: the build re-ranks the existing sleeve but never specifies a morning exit. The current implementation (stock_loop.py _select_overnight_keepers + _prepare_overnight_keepers) holds keepers with GTC stops into normal next-day management, so what is harvested is the close-to-close alpha of ON-momentum names, which per LPS's own Table is only ~+0.45%/mo spread (+3.47 overnight minus 3.02 intraday giveback), ~5-7x below the claimed number. The overnight leg is only capturable if ON_mom-selected keepers are systematically exited in the 9:45-11:00 window (zero incremental trade count, but it must be built).

Scale overstatement: the sleeve selects 2 names from the <=15 already-held, model-filtered, earnings-gated candidates (not a top-slice of the 50-name universe) and is hard-capped at 2 x 5% = <=10% of equity (strategy_config.py). Even granting the full corrected per-sleeve edge, realistic book-level impact is ~1-4bps/mo, an order of magnitude below the pitch's framing.
surviving_caveats: Momentum-specific overnight concentration post-2013 in US large caps rests on indirect confirmations (Bogousslavsky's second-half strengthening; S&P500 2008-2023 U-shape paper; G7 paper US/Canada only — effect NOT predictive in EU/Japan, so external validity is partial); validate in-system via the existing purged WFCV + DSR + challenger shadow gates before promotion.

Mechanism is contested (clientele demand vs U-shaped auction liquidity provision vs fast/slow arbitrageur models): if the premium is auction-structure rent, the spread of 24/5 overnight equity sessions (including Alpaca's own) can erode the close-open boundary that generates it — add a drift monitor on realized ON-vs-ID spread of the sleeve.
